Title: A novel uncertainty-aware framework for remaining useful life prediction integrating uncertainty quantification and calibration
Authors: Weijun Xu; Shuang Gao; Zongyao Wang; Enrico Zio
Abstract: Deep learning (DL) has shown great potential for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, yet most existing methods focus on point estimates and lack reliable uncertainty quantification and calibration, which are crucial for risk-aware decision-making in prognostic applications. This paper proposes a unified uncertainty-aware framework for RUL prediction that integrates Bayesian deep learning (BDL)–based uncertainty quantification with principled uncertainty calibration. Deep Bayesian neural networks trained via Gaussian dropout are employed to jointly model epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties, and ensemble predictive distributions are obtained through stochastic forward passes. A key insight of this work is that, for a well-calibrated model, prediction residuals should be positively correlated with predictive variance. Based on this principle, isotonic regression is introduced as a monotonic structural constraint to actively calibrate heteroscedastic predictive uncertainty. Title: Multivariate feature-disentangled graph-enforced domain adaptation with multi-objective deep learning for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
Authors: Md Shoaib Akhter Rafi; Md Kamrul Hasan
Abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is widely recognized as a cornerstone for ensuring reliability, safety, and cost-effectiveness in next-generation energy storage systems, yet remains challenging due to the complex, nonlinear nature of battery degradation. Existing approaches to battery RUL prognostics are hindered by three persistent domain gaps: (i) models often isolate macroscopic state-of-health (SOH) trajectories from short-term sensor dynamics, failing to capture their complementarity; (ii) sensor- and health-driven embeddings evolve at different rates, leading to structural misalignment and fragmented latent spaces; and (iii) feature distributions shift across diverse battery chemistries, restricting transferability. To address these challenges, we present a multivariate feature-disentangled, graph-enforced domain adaptation framework with multi-objective deep learning for RUL prediction. At its core, SHER-Net fuses SOH embeddings with high-frequency sensor representations to capture both long-term and short-term dynamics. Graph-based enforced consistency learning (GECL) provides training-time structural alignment, mitigating intra- and inter-modal drift without inference overhead. A dual-stream disentangled fusion network (DDFN) with split embedding-based domain adaptation (SEDA) partitions the latent space into domain-invariant and domain-specific subspaces, thereby eliminating negative transfer and over-alignment. Finally, a multi-objective loss synchronizes predictive accuracy, structural consistency, and feature disentanglement, completing the adaptation cycle. Extensive evaluation on public and proprietary datasets demonstrates that this framework consistently surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving normalized RMSE of 1.10%–3.33% and establishing a new benchmark for transferable, inference-efficient, and accurate battery prognostics.

Title: A graph convolutional network-based data-model interactive remaining useful life prediction method for stochastic degrading systems
Authors: Zhaoju Zeng; Zhengxin Zhang; Tianmei Li; Lei Feng; Xiaosheng Si; Jianxun Zhang
Abstract: For industrial systems, remaining useful life (RUL) prediction can provide reference information for maintenance planning and spare parts ordering, thereby playing a crucial role in prognostics and health management (PHM). Recently, data-model interaction prognosis methods, which combine the flexibility in feature extraction from data-driven methods and the interpretability of stochastic models, have garnered increasing attention, especially for degrading systems equipped with multiple sensors. However, existing approaches often fail to adequately capture the correlations and interdependencies among different sensors, resulting in inaccurate and unreliable RUL predictions. Inspired by graph convolutional networks (GCNs), which represent data as graphs to effectively explore relational structures, this paper proposes a novel GCN-based data-model interaction framework for accurate and reliable RUL prediction in stochastic degrading systems. First, cosine similarity is employed to assess the relationships among condition monitoring data collected from various sensors, enabling the construction of a sensor network topology. Based on this topology, a GCN is utilized to aggregate information from neighboring sensor nodes and construct a univariate composite health index (CHI) that reflects the overall system health state. Second, the temporal evolution of the constructed CHI is modeled using a Wiener process, allowing for analytically tractable expressions of the expected value and variance of the RUL defined in the sense of first hitting time (FHT). The interaction between the GCN-extracted CHI and the Wiener process model is achieved by minimizing a loss function defined by the mean squared error (MSE) between predicted and actual RULs. Additionally, for in-service degrading systems, a Bayesian framework is introduced to update the parameters within the degradation models and account for the uncertainties of RUL estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments on both the C-MAPSS dataset and the milling cutter wear dataset.

The SRRM effectively isolates fault-induced transients by removing deterministic gear mesh frequency (GMF) components through spectral editing, while the SLF captures broadband spectral energy growth characteristic of progressive surface degradation. Unlike time-domain metrics, the SLF maintains strict monotonicity throughout the entire degradation cycle, providing a stable input for the stochastic prognostic model. Uncertainty quantification is achieved through the Delta method, propagating state covariance to generate statistically rigorous 95% confidence intervals for RUL predictions. Abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for lithium-ion batteries is critical for ensuring the reliability of electric vehicles. This method blends bio-inspired optimization, topological dependency modeling, and mathematical dimensionality reduction to provide a new way to properly assess the health status of lithium-ion batteries. It makes real-world battery management systems far better at predicting future behavior and more efficient.

Title: Two-phase system degradation modeling and remaining useful life prediction based on Lévy process

Abstract: Prognostics and health management is a critical research field for ensuring the safety of modern industrial systems. Its primary objectives are to accurately characterize degradation behavior and predict the remaining useful life of devices. However, traditional stochastic process models impose relatively strict requirements on degradation increments and their distributions, which contradicts actual situations. Finally, the model’s performance was evaluated using simulated data and a publicly available lithium-ion battery degradation dataset from the Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering at the University of Maryland. The results show that the proposed model achieves higher prediction accuracy compared to existing models.

Title: A two-stage degradation-aware model for coupled early degradation onset detection and remaining useful life prediction of aero-engines
Authors: Qifan Zhou; Xiongfei Liu; Chenchao Tang; Yingqing Guo; Bosong Chai
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) estimation for aero-engines is hindered by long healthy operating periods, variability in operating-conditions, and the entanglement of slow degradation processes with short-term cyclic disturbances. This paper presents a two-stage prognostics framework that couples early degradation onset detection (EDOD) with RUL regression within a unified learning pipeline. In Stage I, an EDOD module is trained using multi-resolution views and a consensus-promoting regularization strategy to stabilize degradation onset identification under operating-condition shifts and stochastic sensor corruption, yielding a reliable estimate of the degradation starting point and thereby narrowing the effective prediction horizon. In Stage II, we introduce a Fourier-based seasonal–trend decomposition with gated reconstruction to separate low-frequency degradation dynamics from oscillatory components prior to feature learning. The reconstructed sequence is then processed by a Dual-Dependency Interaction (DDI) block, which explicitly couples temporal dependency modeling with channel-wise dependency interactions to produce a degradation-aware representation. To exploit complementary inductive biases, two predictors operate in parallel: a liquid neural model that captures continuous-time degradation dynamics, and a wavelet-based multi-resolution mixer branch for scale-specific pattern extraction. Their outputs are fused via uncertainty-aware weighting, improving robustness across diverse operating regimes and failure modes. Meanwhile to substantiate the early-stage prognostic claim, we further introduce horizon-stratified and onset-aligned evaluation protocols, which separately assess predictive performance far from failure and immediately after degradation onset. Extensive experiments and ablation studies on the C-MAPSS dataset demonstrate that the proposed architecture enhances both early degradation onset detection reliability and RUL prediction accuracy, while providing interpretable decomposition and principled fusion supports near-real-time execution of the regression stage under the benchmark update regime.

Title: Multiscale root mean square for hydropower generation systems: a scalable feature extraction method for condition-based maintenance
Authors: Fei Chen; Zhigao Zhao; Xiaoxi Hu; Dong Liu; Xiuxing Yin
Abstract: With the advancement of smart power stations, the maintenance paradigm for hydropower generation systems is shifting from scheduled routines to condition-based strategies, thereby posing new challenges for efficient anomaly detection from large-scale monitoring data. Existing signal feature extraction methods are largely based on nonlinear dynamic metrics, which identify anomalies in components like bearings and gearboxes by quantifying signal complexity. However, due to the abruptness and complexity of signals in hydropower systems, the effectiveness and applicability of complexity-driven methods in scenarios dominated by signal intensity variations remain to be fully validated. Therefore, the comparative assessment of intensity-based and complexity-based feature extraction approaches is essential for evaluating their suitability in extracting abnormal information from hydropower generation systems. Firstly, this paper summarizes various nonlinear dynamic and signal strength indicators, expanding them into multiscale indicators. Then, it compares their effectiveness in identifying abnormal processes in pump-turbine units. Subsequently, their performance in fault early warning scenarios is analyzed. Finally, the dynamic response of each method to different signal types under extreme load rejection conditions is observed. The results across various hydropower operation and maintenance scenarios demonstrate that the proposed signal intensity-based method named multiscale root mean square, significantly outperforms traditional entropy-based approaches, confirming its effectiveness and advantages. This study offers valuable guidance for the condition-based maintenance of hydropower generation systems and contributes to advancing the intelligence level of hydropower stations.

Title: State of health estimation and remaining useful life prediction of Li-ion battery oriented to real-world electric vehicles: A comprehensive evaluation methodology
Authors: Haixu Yang; Fengwei Liang; Kerui Li; Jichao Hong; Jinghan Zhang; Xiaohui Chen
Abstract: State of health estimation is essential to ensure the battery's reliability, safety and economy. It is an integral part of the battery management system. Estimation often faces the problems of a lone indicator and ineffective real-vehicle application. The use of a lone indicator leads to biased and inaccurate state estimation. The complexity of real-world driving scenarios renders the method impractical and inaccurate. Here, we propose a comprehensive evaluation method oriented to real-world electric vehicles. Capacity, ohmic internal resistance, cell voltage inconsistency, and battery pack temperature inconsistency are considered as four indicators of battery degradation. For each indicator, a state of health estimation value can be obtained. A fuzzy matrix is used to fuse the four indicators for a comprehensive evaluation. Also, the fuzzy matrix gives the weights of different health indicators as 0.1988, 0.2463, 0.3183, and 0.2366. The inconsistency of cell voltages carries the highest weighting among these indicators, exerting a more significant influence than the other three. In terms of artificial intelligence, this paper proposes a complete set of data processing, feature computation, and fusion estimation methods for battery health state. In engineering applications, the metrics for health state assessment are greatly enriched and the degree of accuracy is significantly improved. The method breaks through the limitations of the traditional evaluation based on a singular indicator, achieving a multi-dimensional comprehensive and objective evaluation of automotive batteries.

Title: A novel CEEMDAN-TPWP-based phased prediction model for remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries
Authors: Yuying Liang; Xiufen Zhang; Zaizai Yan
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) aging studies, but noise and self-recovery-induced capacity fluctuations severely impair accuracy. To address this problem, a novel CEEMDAN-TPWP model for RUL prediction is presented. The model employs CEEMDAN to effectively filter out noise induced by capacity self-recovery. And a two-phase Wiener process (TPWP) model is constructed to characterize the capacity variation patterns, thereby significantly enhancing the accuracy of RUL prediction. Based on the Kolmogorov formula combined with the convolution formula, an analytical expression for the RUL probability density function (PDF) is derived. Furthermore, a two-step estimation procedure is presented to deal with the parameter estimation problem. Finally, reliability analysis was performed on the NASA and CALCE battery datasets respectively, with comparative experiments conducted against the single-phase Wiener process and Cross-Sample Gaussian process regression (CS-GPR) models. The results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the other two methods, further confirming the effectiveness and applicability of the developed framework.

Title: RAG And Multimodal Feature Fusion For Intelligent Predictive Maintenance Of Industrial Power Equipment
Authors: Hong Yang; Xiaokai Meng; Hua Yu; Yang Bai; Yu Han; Yongxin Liu
Abstract: Predictive maintenance in smart manufacturing demands real-time, accurate fault diagnosis across heterogeneous equipment and multi-source data modalities-challenges that rulebased systems and static knowledge bases fail to address at scale. Title: Remaining useful life aware physics-informed Bayesian digital twin for safety-constrained control in robot-integrated battery manufacturing
Authors: Faizanbasha A.; U. Rizwan; Syed Tahir Hussainy; Naif Almakayeel; Fazilath Basha Asif
Abstract: Industrial robotics cells in battery manufacturing must sustain high throughput without compromising safety under distribution shift and rare failures, yet most digital twins remain data-only, deliver uncalibrated Remaining Useful Life (RUL), or lack runtime safety mechanisms for action. Title: A complementary continual semi-supervised learning scheme using contrastive variational autoencoder for remaining useful life estimation
Authors: Tiancheng Wang; Tao Sun; Fuxiang Quan; Xi Ming Sun
Abstract: As a solution in the field of remaining useful life, deep learning has improved its accuracy compared to traditional machine learning, but it also has some common problems in application, such as the labor-intensive process of data labeling and the catastrophic forgetting of continual learning. Finally, Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks which have continual learning capability are also applied to further improve the continual learning performance. Title: A physics-informed recurrent neural network for long sequence remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearing with implicit function
Authors: Qiwu Zhao; Xiaoli Zhang; Xin Luo; Wang Liang; Erick Mbeka
Abstract: Accurate long-sequence remaining useful life (LSRUL) prediction for rolling bearings is crucial for providing a broad operational horizon, enabling proactive decision-making and catastrophic failure prevention. However, prevailing data-driven approaches often suffer from limited accuracy due to dynamic perturbations and error accumulation during multistep prediction, as well as poor interpretability from a lack of physical guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed recurrent neural network (PIRNN). The PIRNN architecture integrates a variational recurrent neural network (VRNN) and an implicit function solver (IFS). The former captures long-range temporal dependencies for robust LSRUL forecasting, while a novel weighted multistep prediction mechanism mitigates error propagation. Concurrently, the IFS constrains the solution space by approximating the implicit functions within the time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) governing the rolling bearing's physics, which enhances the model's interpretability, improves prediction accuracy, and accelerates convergence. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed PIRNN are validated through comprehensive experiments on both open-source and real-world rolling bearing run-to-failure datasets, demonstrating its outperformance over other state-of-the-art prediction models.

Additionally, a data augmentation module optimizes temporal quality and mitigates noise to ensure robust maintenance decision support. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that STGFormer achieves state-of-the-art performance, providing a scalable solution for maintaining energy stability in Smart Manufacturing Systems.

Authors: Konrad Krzempek; Mateusz Janik; Piotr Sobecki; Dariusz Mazurkiewicz; Tomasz Żabiński; Grzegorz Piecuch
Abstract: The optimization of machining processes through predictive maintenance has gained significant traction in modern manufacturing. However, the existing analytical methods of predictive maintenance often fail to fully leverage high frequency sensor data, leading to suboptimal predictions of tool wear and failure. This study addresses these limitations by integrating wavelet energy analysis with advanced machine learning models to enhance predictive accuracy. A systematic approach to feature extraction and frequency band selection is employed, ensuring that the most relevant signal components are utilized for modeling. The effectiveness of various predictive algorithms, including random forests and gradient boosting, is evaluated to determine their suitability for tool wear prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating wavelet-based features significantly improves prediction performance, providing a robust framework for more efficient and cost-effective machining operations. This research contributes to advancing data-driven maintenance strategies by bridging the gap between signal processing techniques and machine learning applications in industrial settings.

Title: Remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion battery packs using prior cell degradation and limited pack-level data
Authors: Yuhang Du; Datong Liu; Yuchen Song
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion battery packs is important for reliable operation and maintenance. However, pack-level lifecycle degradation data are costly and time-consuming to obtain, which limits the development of data-driven prediction models. In addition, pack degradation is not directly equivalent to cell degradation because it is affected by inter-cell inconsistency and series constraints. This discrepancy further increases the difficulty of RUL prediction with limited pack-level data. To address this problem, this paper proposes a cross-level RUL prediction method using prior cell degradation and limited pack-level data. Full-lifecycle cell data are first used to establish long-timescale state of health (SOH) trend priors and short-timescale degradation-rate priors through a multi-kernel deep Gaussian process. Limited early-stage pack-level data and a voltage-derived inconsistency feature are then introduced to calibrate the discrepancy between cell-level priors and pack-level degradation behavior through cross-level scaling and residual compensation. During recursive prediction, particle filtering is used to fuse the corrected SOH prediction and degradation-rate prediction, so that the pack-level SOH trajectory and RUL can be obtained. Experimental results on laboratory and electric-vehicle battery pack datasets show that the proposed method achieves an average RUL prediction error of about 4 cycles when only 17.46% of the pack-level lifecycle data are used for model construction. These results indicate that the proposed method can reduce the dependence on costly pack-level lifecycle data while maintaining accurate pack-level RUL prediction under limited-data conditions.

Title: SPPL: Predicting remaining useful life of aircraft engine via structural prior-guided patch-wise learning
Authors: Yulin Du; Haichuan Fang; Xin Li; Hongfu Zuo; Xincan Zhao
Abstract: Aero-engines are the primary power units of aircraft, and accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for condition-based maintenance and flight safety. However, most existing RUL prediction methods treat long time-series data as a single modeling unit, thereby masking short-term degradation features. Moreover, they rely primarily on purely data-driven learning and thus fail to effectively exploit engine structural priors. To address these issues, we propose a novel Structural Prior-guided Patch-wise Learning (SPPL) method that partitions long time-series data into consecutive, non-overlapping patches. Within each patch, an intra-patch spatial-temporal fusion (Intra-PSTF) module is devised to integrate engine topology with multi-sensor data, construct a temporally connected sensor graph, and employ a graph neural network to model local spatial and temporal interactions for learning sensor representations. Across patches, an Inter-patch global temporal integration (Inter-PGTI) module is developed to build a patch-level relational graph from patch features, capture long-range dependencies, and integrate them via temporal aggregation to derive patch representations. Finally, SPPL fuses sensor-level and patch-level representations to jointly preserve intra-patch degradation patterns and inter-patch long-term evolution for RUL prediction. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPPL captures local and global degradation information, improving RUL prediction accuracy and robustness.

Title: A Temporal Graph Neural Network with Gated Recurrent Unit for robust in-situ prediction of milling tool remaining useful life
Authors: Dingli Guo; Honggen Zhou; Guochao Li; Li Sun
Abstract: In-situ prediction of tool remaining useful life (RUL) is critical for maintaining machining quality and minimizing production downtime. However, existing graph neural network (GNN) approaches often suffer from degraded performance under varying sensor configurations and are inapplicable in strict single-sensor scenarios. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Temporal Graph Neural Network integrated with a Gated Recurrent Unit (TGNN-GRU) for robust in-situ tool RUL prediction. The model employs a temporal graph-structured data construction method to simultaneously capture spatiotemporal dependencies from multi-source cutting signals. Notably, the architecture decouples model complexity from sensor quantity, ensuring robust performance even when sensor data are limited or heterogeneous. The proposed method is validated on both a local milling dataset and the public PHM2010 dataset. Results demonstrate that the TGNN-GRU model consistently outperforms conventional GNNs: on the local dataset, it reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by averages of 84.52%, 84.50%, and 80.60%, respectively. Crucially, under strict single-sensor conditions, the model maintains high predictive fidelity—exhibiting only marginal increases in error metrics compared to the optimal multi-sensor configuration—while training and inference time remain nearly invariant to sensor count. These findings confirm that the TGNN-GRU model offers a highly accurate, efficient, and reliable solution, significantly advancing the practical deployment of in-situ tool RUL prediction systems.

Title: Reliability-aware vibration measurement framework for predictive maintenance of rotating machinery: Probability of detection, uncertainty-quantified remaining useful life, and simulator-based hardware-in-the-loop reliability evaluation
Authors: Ali Sayghe
Abstract: Vibration-based predictive maintenance (PdM) of rotating machinery is increasingly informed by data-driven models, yet two measurement-system limitations restrict deployment in safety-relevant industrial settings: classification accuracy on benchmark data does not characterise the conditional probability of detecting a fault at a given severity along an instrumented measurement chain, and remaining-useful-life (RUL) point estimates do not quantify the uncertainty that risk-informed scheduling requires. This paper develops a reliability-oriented measurement framework that formalises uncertainty propagation from sensor noise and bearing-geometry tolerance through to the inference outputs, and reports three metrological indicators that conventional accuracy-only evaluation does not deliver. The framework combines (i) a Wasserstein conditional GAN with gradient penalty (WCGAN-GP), conditioned on fault label and operating regime, whose synthetic vibration signals are screened by a narrowband signal-to-noise physics-consistency score derived from bearing characteristic frequencies; (ii) a hybrid digital shadow at the edge that fuses a lumped-parameter bearing model with an LSTM-autoencoder anomaly score through a Kalman filter, with Monte Carlo Dropout (p<inf>d</inf>=0.10, M=100 stochastic forward passes) providing calibrated predictive intervals on RUL; and (iii) a severity-stratified probability-of-detection (PoD) protocol implemented on a simulator-based hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed with controlled fault injection (n=300 trials per fault × severity cell). The framework is evaluated on CWRU for imbalanced bearing-fault classification (with bearing-wise cross-validation to prevent window-overlap leakage), on the four C-MAPSS sub-datasets for RUL uncertainty calibration, and on the simulator-based HIL testbed for severity-resolved PoD. Augmentation raises minority-class macro-F1 from 0.71±0.05 to 0.95±0.02 (p<0.001, paired Wilcoxon, five random seeds, Holm–Bonferroni-corrected); the 90% RUL prediction interval achieves empirical coverage 88.4–91.2% on FD001–FD004; HIL PoD exceeds 95% for inner-race, outer-race and ball faults at severity Level 2 and above, falling to 68–79% at incipient severity. End-to-end edge latency on NVIDIA Jetson Orin remains below 85 ms at the 95th percentile, including uncertainty quantification. The results support simulated-HIL reliability evaluation for single bearing faults under controlled severity and stress conditions; field PoD stability for naturally degraded bearings and compound faults remains future work. The contribution is positioned as a reliability-oriented vibration measurement methodology rather than as an AI classifier: uncertainty is propagated from accelerometer noise and bearing-geometry tolerance through to the reported indicators; sensor calibration is traceable under ISO/IEC 17025; severity and PoD are calibrated against the broadband noise floor estimated from a 30-minute baseline acquisition; and every reported headline figure is paired with a confidence interval. The AI components are the means by which the measurement-system indicators are produced, not the contribution itself.

Title: Signal-quality-aware adaptive prediction for lithium-ion battery remaining useful life under noisy and resource-constrained conditions
Authors: Difan Yu; Haijun Wei
Abstract: Deploying deep learning for lithium-ion battery Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction in edge Battery Management Systems (BMS) is challenged by varying measurement conditions and limited computational resources. While existing studies primarily improve prediction accuracy through increasingly complex architectures, the influence of signal quality on model behavior remains insufficiently explored. To address this gap, a signal-quality-aware adaptive prediction framework is proposed. The framework combines physics-informed health indicators with a lightweight adaptive routing mechanism. An Input Variance Score (IVS) is introduced to characterize real-time signal quality and measurement conditions, enabling dynamic activation or bypass of the attention module according to input reliability. Experimental results on NASA, XJTU-SY, and CALCE datasets demonstrate RMSE values of 5.65 cycles and 9.88 cycles on the NASA and XJTU-SY datasets, respectively. On the low-signal-quality CALCE dataset, an attention degradation phenomenon is observed, where attention effectiveness deteriorates under severe measurement disturbances. By adaptively adjusting the computational pathway, the proposed method reduces prediction error by 13.6% compared with static attention configurations. Deployment on a Raspberry Pi 4B confirms real-time feasibility for embedded BMS applications. The results suggest that signal quality should be explicitly considered in prognostic model design rather than treated solely as a preprocessing issue, providing a measurement-oriented perspective for robust battery health prediction.

Title: A physics-informed neural network enhanced by fuzzy inference for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
Authors: Linbin Mao; Fahui Miao; Chunyu Liu; Xuanzhe Ma
Abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of energy storage systems. However, this task remains highly challenging due to measurement noise and the difficulty of maintaining physical consistency in purely data-driven models. To reconcile electrochemical physical fidelity with data adaptability, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) incorporating fuzzy inference system (FIS) enhancement is proposed, where a Takagi-Sugeno-Kang neuro-fuzzy (TSK-FIS) inference system is employed as a surrogate network to improve feature representation of nonlinear battery degradation. The resulting features are then fed into a Deep Hidden Physics Model (DeepHPM), the core physics-constrained component of the framework, within which an adaptive gated residual connection (AGRC) is embedded to tightly couple latent degradation dynamics with the network architecture. This structure effectively alleviates the error accumulation issue commonly encountered in long-horizon RUL prediction. Furthermore, to improve robustness against noise and outliers in battery data, a SoftAdapt-driven Cauchy–HawkEye loss function is designed. By introducing a small insensitive zone around the zero-residual region and adaptively balancing multiple loss components, the training stability and optimization robustness are significantly improved. Experimental results across multiple datasets indicate that the proposed method achieves superior overall predictive performance compared with baseline models, yielding a substantial reduction in RMSE while maintaining strong robustness and generalization capability.

Title: A Remaining Useful Life Prediction Framework for IGBT Based on Dynamic Precursor Weighting
Authors: Jianhua Zhang; Maoliang Jian; Haorui Zhu; Lianqiao Yang
Abstract: In power electronic systems, accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of insulated gate bipolar transistors is essential for ensuring system reliability. This article presents a robust RUL prediction framework that integrates dynamic precursor weighting, health indicator (HI) construction, and deep learning. First, power cycling tests are conducted to obtain aging-sensitive precursors. A sliding-window-based degradation rate analysis is employed to assign time-varying weights for adaptive precursor selection and fusion, resulting in an HI that captures the degradation trend. Wavelet threshold denoising is then applied to the constructed HI to reduce noise and enhance smoothness. Next, a comprehensive set of time-domain features is extracted from the denoised HI, and relevant features are selected using correlation, monotonicity, similarity, and redundancy criteria. To further capture frequency-domain information, variational mode decomposition is applied, producing intrinsic mode functions that are also used as predictive inputs. The selected features are fed into a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1-D CNN)-Informer model for RUL prediction. Two evaluation strategies are employed to assess the generalization performance. The proposed HI consistently outperforms classical aging precursors across all tasks, demonstrating its superior capability in capturing degradation patterns. In addition, comparative experiments with 1-D CNN-Transformer and 1-D CNN-long short-term memory (LSTM) models show that the CNN-Informer achieves higher prediction accuracy and better training efficiency. These results confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework.

Title: Dynamic curvature pooling graph convolutional network to fuse multi-sensor signals for remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Linjie Zheng; Fei Wu; Chuan Li; Edgar Estupinan; Yi Qin
Abstract: The core objective of graph neural network (GNN)-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction methods for equipment with multi-source sensors is to learn effective graph representations, and graph pooling is an efficient approach to achieve it. However, existing graph pooling techniques are limited in modeling hierarchical structures and have limitations in embedding space representation. To overcome these limitations, a dynamic curvature pooling graph convolutional network (DCPGCN) is proposed for RUL prediction of equipment with multi-source sensors. DCPGCN develops a hyperbolic hierarchical graph pooling framework. By leveraging the geometric advantages of hyperbolic space for hierarchical representation, the proposed framework more effectively captures multi-level structural information in graphs, significantly improving the overall structural fidelity of the graph representation. Moreover, a curvature predictor driven by pooling path deviation is proposed. By quantifying the geometric distortion along leaf-to-root paths in hyperbolic space, the predictor dynamically adjusts the curvature parameter, improving the embedding space’s adaptability and expressiveness for the graph’s hierarchical structure. Finally, experiments on the CMAPSS dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms multiple state-of-the-art approaches in prediction accuracy, while experiments on real-world wind turbine RUL prediction further confirm its superiority and potential in engineering applications.

Title: A low-quality imbalanced multi-modal data-based remaining useful life prediction method of rotating machinery with interpretability
Authors: Fuyuan Zhao; Xiangang Cao; Yong Duan; Xin Yang; Xinyuan Zhang; Ke Han; Yubo Zhang
Abstract: Remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery is critical for ensuring safe operation and optimizing maintenance decisions. Under complex operating conditions, multi-modal monitoring data, including vibration, acoustic, electrical, and infrared thermal signals, provide multiple physical perspectives for characterizing degradation processes. However, noise, incompleteness, and information discrepancies often result in low-quality and imbalanced representations, substantially degrading fusion effectiveness, robustness, and prediction reliability. Moreover, existing methods typically suffer from limited cross-modal semantic modeling capability, high feature redundancy, and insufficient interpretability, restricting practical engineering applicability. A multi-modal conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model–based cross-modal enhancement module is developed, in which task guidance and adaptive weighting are incorporated as conditional constraints during the reverse diffusion process to reconstruct low-quality modalities and enhance cross-modal representations. An efficient cross-modal fusion module integrating a pairwise multi-modal bottleneck Transformer and bidirectional long short-term memory is designed. Learnable bottleneck tokens establish a shared semantic space, while bidirectional temporal dependencies of degradation evolution are captured, enabling lightweight and robust representation learning. Furthermore, a DeepSHAP–based interpretability mechanism is introduced to quantify contributions of different modalities and feature dimensions, thereby clarifying the model’s decision-making process. Experiments on two multi-modal datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in prediction accuracy, cross-modal collaborative representation, and training stability across multiple operating conditions, while providing strong engineering interpretability and practical applicability.

Title: A TFT-inspired hybrid BiLSTM–attention framework for uncertainty-aware remaining useful life prediction in aero-engine prognostics
Authors: Tamrat Yifter Meles; Chao Lung Yang; Atinkut Atinafu Yilma; Melkamu Mengistnew Teshome; Yulius Harjoseputro
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is fundamental to predictive maintenance in safety–critical systems such as aero-engines. While deep learning models have significantly improved predictive accuracy, many existing approaches remain deterministic and do not explicitly characterize uncertainty, thereby limiting their suitability for risk-sensitive decision-making. This study introduces an uncertainty-aware RUL prediction framework built upon a TFT-inspired hybrid Bidirectional LSTM–Attention architecture, integrated with a Bayesian neural network (BNN) and Conformal Prediction. The proposed model captures complex degradation behavior by combining bidirectional recurrent layers for modelling local temporal dependencies with multi-head self-attention to emphasize the most informative time steps within extended sensor sequences. Gated residual networks further stabilize feature representations while preserving computational efficiency. Epistemic uncertainty is quantified through Bayesian variational inference, whereby probability distributions are learned over the regression-layer parameters and predictive uncertainty is obtained via posterior sampling. To ensure statistically reliable coverage, Conformal Prediction is employed to calibrate the prediction intervals. The framework is evaluated on benchmark aero-engine datasets under multiple operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate consistently strong predictive performance across all subsets. The resulting uncertainty estimates are well calibrated, achieving high prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) with relatively low prediction interval normalized average width (PINAW), indicating an effective trade-off between reliability and sharpness. Overall, the proposed approach delivers accurate RUL estimates alongside principled and trustworthy uncertainty quantification, thereby supporting risk-aware maintenance decision-making in industrial prognostics.

Authors: Kun Wang; Ai He; Jiashuai Liu; Qifan Zhou; Zhongzhi Hu; Jinshen Wang
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aero-engines is a key technology for prognostics and health management (PHM). Experiments on the N-CMAPSS and real-world quick access recorder datasets validate the effectiveness, showing significant improvements in accuracy and generalization, with Scores of 0.33, 0.41, and 0.39 on DS01, DS04, and DS06, respectively. Title: Information-theoretic limits of health indicator construction for remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Huy Hoang Le; Kim Anh Nguyen
Abstract: In data-driven remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, practitioners face a recurring design choice: should engineering effort focus on health indicator (HI) construction or on model architecture? This paper provides quantitative tools to answer that question before model training begins , using only knowledge of the degradation physics. We develop an information-theoretic framework that yields three practical outputs. First, a single scalar diagnostic — the information non-uniformity index η, computable from the degradation model class — predicts whether a given domain is HI-limited (η>1: invest in HI design) or model-limited (η<0.3: invest in model architecture). Second, a closed-form formula determines the minimum HI dimensionality d<sup>∗</sup> needed to capture a prescribed fraction of the available prognostic signal, preventing both under-dimensioned HIs (irreducible accuracy loss) and over-dimensioned ones (overfitting risk). Third, a bottleneck ratio ρ<inf>HI</inf> quantifies the fraction of prognostic information lost at the HI compression step versus the modeling step, directly identifying the pipeline’s weakest link. These tools are derived from three theorems establishing the fundamental limits of HI-based prediction for exponential, power-law, and stretched-exponential degradation classes, with robustness extensions to non-Gaussian noise, correlated channels, and nonlinear HIs. Cross-domain comparison against published results from turbofan engines, lithium-ion batteries, and rolling element bearings is consistent with the framework’s predictions: domains flagged as HI-limited (batteries, bearings) are those where published studies report that HI design dominates model architecture. Because the per-domain η values are derived from assumed degradation-class parameters rather than computed from raw data, this cross-domain ordering serves as a consistency check; the primary causal evidence is a controlled experiment on three benchmark datasets (C-MAPSS FD001, NASA Battery, C-MAPSS FD004), which confirms that the effective optimal HI dimensionality increases with system complexity as predicted.

Title: A meta-curriculum dynamic weighting network equipped with frequency-aware attention for bearing cross-domain remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Jiayang Zhao; Deqiang He; Zhenzhen Jin; Xingwu Zhang; Song Zhang; Xianwang Li; Yang Fu
Abstract: Bearing function as the core transmission components in rotating machinery systems. Its operational status directly influences the reliability of critical equipment in fields like wind power generation and rail transportation. Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction constitutes a crucial element for preventing unexpected failures and optimizing condition-based maintenance decisions. However, in practical engineering domains, bearing RUL often faces cross-domain scenarios with large distributional differences. Traditional transfer learning methods adopt the same weights for all source domain samples, ignoring the transfer benefit from sample variability in cross-domain scenarios, resulting in model validity that is not always guaranteed and triggering negative transfer effects. Meanwhile, end-to-end feature learning mechanisms tend to obscure physical degradation information across different failure modes, resulting in suboptimal prediction accuracy. To address these issues, this paper introduces an innovative framework integrating frequency-aware spectral attention with meta-curriculum transfer learning. Firstly, by designing a dynamic fault prototype parameter mechanism, the physical a priori knowledge of bearing failures is introduced to improve the physical interpretability and prediction accuracy of the model. Simultaneously, a weighted network based on meta-curriculum learning dynamically assigns multiple types of weights to the samples, enabling adaptive learning toward more favorable update directions. Experimental validation using the XJTU-SY dataset demonstrates satisfactory RUL prediction performance across diverse cross-domain scenarios. Compared with state-of-the-art models, our method significantly reduces the prediction error, validating the advantages of the proposed method for engineering applications.

Abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of implementing predictive maintenance (PdM) for aero-engines, where the scarcity and high cost of real engine test data hinder model development and validation. Based on this paradigm, we construct two predictive frameworks: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-Self-Attention Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-Genetic Algorithm (GA) and PCA-Transformer-GA. Unlike existing studies that often focus on isolated techniques, our work provides a holistic framework that synergizes PCA for dimensionality reduction, GA for hyperparameter optimization, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation, validated across multi-source data scenarios. The feasibility of the proposed frameworks is first verified through remaining useful life (RUL) prediction experiments using the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) dataset. Subsequently, thrust prediction validation is conducted using real engine test data from a 1000 kg class turbofan engine, demonstrating the framework’s engineering applicability. The results show that the GA-LSTM model achieves optimal performance on the augmented dataset, with an average root mean square error (RMSE) of 48.22. Furthermore, the RMSE of the Transformer model gradually decreases as the data scale expands, revealing its superior potential in handling long-sequence data. This study advances the field by offering a comparative analysis of LSTM and Transformer architectures in aero-engine PdM, providing practical guidance on model selection, data processing, and optimization strategies. Our findings also illustrate a feasible path for expanding high-value datasets with limited economic input, thereby contributing valuable theoretical and practical insights to the development of cost-effective and intelligent aero-engine maintenance systems.

Authors: Abdullah Memon; Muhammad Majid Gulzar; Shahid A. Hasib; Salman Habib; Ali Arishi
Abstract: The growing adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has intensified the need for accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction and intelligent Battery Management Systems (BMS) to ensure safety, reliability, and sustainable operation of Li-ion batteries. This review provides a structured synthesis of recent advancements in RUL estimation methodologies, categorizing them into data-driven, model-based, hybrid, and filtering approaches. In addition to methodological developments, the paper systematically examines publicly available Li-ion battery datasets, highlighting their characteristics, experimental conditions, and limitations, and discussing their influence on model generalizability and benchmarking practices. Unlike prior reviews that treat RUL prediction or BMS functionalities separately, this work explicitly integrates RUL estimation within BMS architectures, addressing energy management, thermal regulation, safety monitoring, and real-time implementation constraints. Furthermore, deployment considerations such as computational efficiency, uncertainty quantification, and embedded system limitations are critically analyzed from a sustainable computing perspective. By connecting datasets, modeling strategies, system integration, and deployment challenges, this review offers a comprehensive framework to guide future research toward scalable, interpretable, and real-time RUL prediction solutions for next-generation EV battery systems.

Abstract: Lithium-ion battery Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction with high accuracy is essential to guarantee the reliability, safety, and economic efficiency of energy storage systems (EESs). To meet this challenge, the present study introduces a novel hybrid DL approach named Multi-Head Self-Attention Long Short-Term Memory with Harris Hawks Optimization (MHA_LSTM_HHO) for high-precision lithium-ion battery RUL prediction. The proposed framework combines the MHA mechanism and an LSTM network to learn from long-range temporal dependencies and degradation-sensitive features in a battery charging and discharging pattern. Moreover, the HHO algorithm is used to automatically optimize the critical hyperparameters of the DL model, which enhances the stability of convergence and robustness of prediction. The proposed model is tested for the benchmark HNEI NMC-LCO 18650 lithium-ion battery degradation dataset, and tested with various battery aging conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed MHA_LSTM_HHO model achieves considerable performance improvement compared to the traditional LSTM model, the attention-based LSTM model, and other optimization-assisted models. Title: An uncertainty-aware adaptive feedback ensemble framework for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
Authors: Zhijian Wang; Yang Chang; Xin Fan; Weibo Ren; Zhongxin Chen; Yanfeng Li; Lei Dong
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for the health management of lithium-ion batteries. However, health indicators often exhibit non-monotonic fluctuations due to multiple factors, including measurement noise, operating-condition variations, temperature effects, and uncertainties introduced during feature extraction. Furthermore, single degradation models fail to fully capture battery-to-battery variability and multi-stage nonlinear evolution, which compromises prediction accuracy. To overcome these limitations, an uncertainty-aware adaptive feedback framework is proposed for probabilistic RUL prediction. First, a recursive latent state estimation (RLSE) framework is formulated based on state-space models to explicitly model observation and process noise. By integrating Kalman filtering and smoothing, noisy multi-source health indicators are transformed into smooth and robust latent health indicators (LHIs). Second, an adaptive dynamic feature fusion (ADFF) strategy is proposed, where the predictive capability of each LHI is continuously evaluated via staged RUL (SRUL) feedback. Fusion weights are dynamically updated to construct a comprehensive health indicator (CHI) that characterizes the overall degradation state. Third, to accommodate time-varying and nonlinear degradation patterns, an adaptive model selection for prediction (AMSP) method is introduced. Driven by the SRUL feedback mechanism, the framework dynamically switches among power-law, exponential, and hybrid Wiener process models to better match the current degradation state. Title: Remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries by physics-interpretable enhanced electrochemical features and adaptive spline modeling based on TCN-KAN
Authors: Xiaoli Zhang; Jie Lv; Junzhe Xie; Haopeng Han; Xudong Zhang; Qiwu Zhao
Abstract: In most lithium-ion battery prediction methods, externally measured capacity values are used; however, intrinsic electrochemical aging processes are insufficiently represented, and prediction reliability is reduced. In mainstream deep learning approaches, MLP architectures are commonly adopted, and physical interpretability is limited. To address these limitations, a physics-informed hybrid TCN–KAN framework is proposed, in which temporal convolutional networks (TCN) and Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KAN) are integrated into a unified architecture to couple electrochemical mechanisms with nonlinear degradation modeling. An equivalent circuit model is employed to fit electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data, and a physics-guided feature-screening process is established based on Spearman rank correlation analysis. In this framework, conventional capacity testing is replaced with an EIS-derived feature extraction strategy, and an electrochemically relevant feature set is generated so that energy dissipation and aging behavior can be characterized. Long-term degradation dynamics are captured by the TCN module through dilated causal convolutions, while black-box MLP layers are replaced by the KAN module with learnable B-spline basis functions, enhancing nonlinear mapping interpretability. Interpretable deep modeling of degradation patterns is enabled by this integration, and a mechanism-consistent, structurally transparent architecture is provided for battery lifespan prediction. Experiments are conducted on the publicly available Cambridge battery dataset. A minimum prediction RMSE of 0.00421 is achieved by the proposed method, and remaining useful life prediction errors ranging from 1.7% to 2.6% are obtained. Both baseline models and recent advanced models are outperformed in terms of accuracy and interpretability.

Title: Uncertainty-aware remaining useful life prediction and PPO based optimal maintenance scheduling in industrial IoT
Authors: Guneet Kaur Walia; Mohit Kumar
Abstract: The rapid emergence of digitized factories and advanced automotive manufacturing has paved the way for the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to maximize equipment uptime, that enhances manufacturing operations and support reliability. Predictive maintenance (PdM) is a key approach that leverages equipment sensor data to monitor performance abnormalities. Further, the estimation of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) aids in predicting potential or impeding failover before its actual breakdown. However, only few studies extend the work of RUL prognostics prediction to scheduling equipment maintenance, but suffer from few challenges such as overestimation of Q-values, instability during training, and inefficient performance. In addition to this, existing investigations often consider single-point RUL predictions, however in real-world scenario, many factors such as noise, distinct operating conditions of the equipment and nevertheless complex nature of equipment agening, introduces the concept of uncertainity. Hence, it becomes paramount to quantify the uncertainity of RUL, for which the authors propose non-parametric probabilistic prediction method, known as Quantile Regression (QR) integrated with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for predicting RUL values of the equipment. Further, the RUL values are utilized to design better adaptive maintenance scheduling plans using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) approach. The work has been tested on a prominent NASA turbofan engine dataset, which illustrates the promising performance of the proposed framework. The experimental results validate that the proposed work improves RUL prediction up to 19.08 % and minimizes maintenance schedule time up to 24.18 % in comparison to state-of-the-art approaches.

Title: A coordinate-aware Mamba2 framework for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion battery
Authors: Longqing He; Ming Zhang; Sujuan Huang; Zongyang Jing; Wenqing Wei; Kai Wang
Abstract: To address the limitations of existing methods in capturing long-term temporal dependencies, local capacity regeneration, and nonlinear degradation characteristics in lithium-ion battery remaining useful life prediction, this paper proposes a coordinate-aware Mamba2 framework based on state-space modeling. Mamba2 is adopted as the backbone to model long-range degradation evolution, while a coordinate feature attention network is introduced in the feature extraction stage to enhance the selection and representation of key degradation in00formation. Additionally, a swiGLU-gated residual network is constructed for feature transformation and prediction, improving the modeling of complex dynamic relationships and endpoint stability. Through the collaborative design of these modules, the proposed framework effectively captures both global degradation trends and local fluctuation patterns. Experiments were conducted on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Tongji University, and Xi’an Jiaotong University datasets under single-variable input, multivariable input, and cross-dataset generalization settings. The mean absolute error values are lower than 0.0098, 0.0016, and 0.0083, while the root mean square error values are lower than 0.0172, 0.0024, and 0.0111, respectively. Results demonstrate that coordinate-aware Mamba2 achieves superior accuracy, lower computational cost, faster training and inference, and stronger robustness to different prediction starting points. Title: Self-attention enhanced TCN for remaining useful life prediction of roller in a hot rolling process with uncertainty assessment
Authors: Di Zhou; Canyang Ding; Zhen Chen; Ershun Pan; Huimin Chen; Ting Zhu
Abstract: The roller is a critical component in the steel rolling process directly impacts the quality of rolled steel products. The remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of roller is of great significance for stable steel production. Existing studies have extensively explored the integration of attention mechanisms with temporal models for industrial equipment RUL prediction. However, these approaches typically employ serial interaction for shallow integration, failing to adequately model the deep temporal dependencies in equipment degradation sequences. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Self-Attention Temporal Convolutional Network (SATCN) model that embeds self-attention mechanisms within the residual blocks of the TCN architecture. This innovative design enables each layer of the model to effectively capture deep degradation features in roller deterioration time-series data. Meanwhile, the Monte Carlo Dropout (MC Dropout) technique is incorporated to obtain both mean predictions and uncertainty intervals for the roller. Furthermore, an uncertainty interval adjustment strategy is proposed to appropriately scaling and adjusting the obtained uncertainty intervals. It is then applied to yield a more rational uncertainty assessment for the roller. Finally, experimental results show that the evaluation metric R <sup>2</sup> of the method proposed in this paper is improved by 2.3% compared with other time-series prediction models. Prediction accuracy exceeds 96.9% across three different degradation types of roller data, confirming the superiority of the method proposed in this paper.

Title: Deep transfer learning based on cross-domain subsequence alignment and feature contribution interpretation for remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Tongshan Liu; Yiming Li; Zhihao Hu; Congjie Fu; Guiqiu Song
Abstract: Deep transfer learning enables the transfer of knowledge learned from a source domain to a target domain, thereby alleviating the few-shot problem in remaining useful life (RUL) prediction tasks. However, due to differences in operating conditions and working scenarios, a significant domain shift commonly exists between the source and target domains. Existing cross-domain transfer learning still faces the following challenges: difficulties in cross-domain subsequence alignment, insufficient robustness under few-shot conditions, and limited interpretability of model decisions, which collectively degrade the stability and reliability of prediction results. To address these issues, this paper proposes a RUL transfer prediction method based on cross-domain subsequence alignment and feature contribution interpretation to optimize the cross-domain transfer process. First, a multi-scale subsequence alignment strategy is developed to select the most informative source domain subsequences, thereby reducing the risk of negative transfer. Second, an interpretable cross-domain transfer learning model is constructed by embedding a self-attention mechanism and a Bayesian linear layer into the domain adaptation framework, which enhances robustness in cross-domain prediction and mitigates overfitting under few-shot conditions in the target domain. Finally, a lightweight analysis method for identifying critical time steps and feature contributions is established to further improve the interpretability of the decision-making process. Experimental results on the IEEE PHM 2012 bearing dataset and the XJTU-SY bearing dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving an RMSE of 0.06, an MAE of 0.05, and an R² of 0.96.

Title: Data-driven machine learning for enhancing predictive maintenance of distribution transformers
Authors: Safae Bazi; Hasna Nhaila; Mohamed El Khaili
Abstract: Predictive maintenance of distribution transformers remains a major challenge for electric utilities, as failure events represent a minority class and entail high operational and economic costs. This study presents a data-driven framework for transformer failure prediction using readily available operational and installation data, with explicit attention to class imbalance and risk-based maintenance prioritization.A comparative evaluation of classical machine learning models is performed, including LR, SVM, DT, RF, and XGBoost. Models are assessed using stratified 10-fold cross-validation and metrics suited to imbalanced classification and failure detection, with emphasis on Recall, F1-score, Precision–Recall AUC, and the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Two experimental settings are analyzed: a baseline configuration and an imbalance-aware optimized configuration combining resampling and hyperparameter tuning.In the baseline setting, Random Forest demonstrates the most robust and stable behavior, achieving a strong balance between missed failures and false alarms (MCC ≈ 0.91). Under the optimized setting, XGBoost shows the largest improvement, reaching higher detection capability while maintaining controlled false-positive rates (Recall ≈ 0.92, F1-score ≈ 0.93, MCC ≈ 0.90), with consistent performance across folds.Model interpretability is addressed using SHAP applied to the optimized XGBoost model, highlighting coherent contributions from aggregated risk indicators, electrical stress variables, loading conditions, and installation context, thereby improving transparency without implying causality.The framework is validated on operational data from approximately 32,000 distribution transformers across 42 municipalities in the Cauca Department, Colombia (2019–2020). The results show that comparative machine learning combined with imbalance-aware evaluation and interpretability can effectively support practical, scalable, risk-based predictive maintenance strategies.

Title: Agentic AI for autonomous condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of marine vessels

Abstract: Modern marine vessels generate large volumes of high-frequency operational data, yet translating this data into reliable maintenance intelligence remains challenging. The proposed system integrates a Transformer-based Autoencoder for multivariate anomaly detection with a Large Language Model (LLM) that enables interactive, explainable analysis through structured tool-calling. Title: A stochastic optimization framework for condition-based maintenance, crew management, and spare parts logistics in solar energy systems
Authors: Muhammet Ceyhan Sahin; Shijia Zhao; Feng Qiu; Murat Yildirim
Abstract: The rapid deployment of photovoltaic (PV) systems underscored the need for efficient operations and maintenance (O&M) strategies, especially in geographically distributed fleets. This paper presents COMPASS (Condition-based Operations and Maintenance Planning Approach for Solar Systems), a comprehensive stochastic optimization framework that integrates condition-based maintenance scheduling, crew management, and spare parts logistics. The framework leverages predictive analytics on real-world sensor data to generate maintenance signals and explicitly models uncertainties in solar power generation, electricity prices, and maintenance durations through scenario-based planning. A two-stage stochastic mixed-integer optimization model coordinates both hourly and daily decisions to balance preventive and corrective maintenance, crew routing, inventory control, and production planning. To solve the problem, a receding horizon procedure is developed to adaptively incorporate new information over a 30-day horizon. Extensive computational experiments on a real-world PV fleet with 300 assets across 25 locations demonstrate that COMPASS significantly reduces total costs, asset downtime, and inventory costs when compared to the state-of-the-art models.

Title: Sparse Gramian Angular Field-Based Bayesian-Weighted Multi-Source domain adaptation for remaining useful life prediction of belt conveyors
Authors: Xueqi Yang; Xinqin Gao; Jiarong Qiu; Zhoupeng Han
Abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for belt conveyor idler bearings is essential to ensure continuous transportation and reduce maintenance costs. However, industrial settings often face a shortage of fault samples. Existing domain adaptation methods fail to effectively leverage prior knowledge between inter-source domains to mitigate negative transfer and are further hindered by high computational redundancy when integrated with image coding techniques. To address these issues, a Sparse-Gramian Angular Field-based Bayesian-Weighted Multi-Source Domain Adaptation (SGB-MSDA) method is proposed for the RUL prediction of the belt conveyor idler bearings. The method introduces a Sparse-Gramian Angular Field (Sparse-GAF) adaptive encoding that identifies high-information segments based on information entropy and generates high-resolution images, while low-information segments are represented at lower resolution to retain fault features while significantly reducing computational overhead. An inter-source graph structure alignment strategy is constructed to capture differences in feature distributions across source domains, with feature consistency enhanced via graph regularization. Source-target domain similarity is integrated with inter-source alignment results to design a Bayesian source-domain re-weighting mechanism that dynamically adjusts transfer weights, emphasizing high-correlation sources and suppressing low-correlation sources to mitigate negative transfer. Additionally, domain adversarial learning and discrepancy-based alignment are jointly optimized to obtain domain-invariant representations. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in prediction accuracy, generalization, and computational efficiency. On the coal-mine belt conveyor idler bearing dataset, it achieves MAE and RMSE values of 0.0462 and 0.0618, respectively, improving upon state-of-the-art methods by 20.9% and 26.6%, showing strong promise for industrial applicability.

Title: Integrated optimization framework for condition-based maintenance and spare parts inventory in photovoltaic systems using deep reinforcement learning
Authors: Yunxin Zhu; Meimei Zheng; Tangbin Xia; Tao Ma; Dong Wang; Wei Weng
Abstract: Maintenance and spare parts ordering optimization is crucial for ensuring reliability and reducing operational costs in photovoltaic (PV) systems. This paper investigates a joint optimization framework for condition-based maintenance and spare parts inventory replenishment for PV systems, which consist of multiple subsystems composed of PV arrays and inverters connected in series and parallel. A Markov decision process (MDP) is formulated to model the stochastic degradation of PV arrays, sudden inverter failures, along with maintenance actions and spare parts ordering decisions. A proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based joint maintenance and ordering (PJMO) algorithm with heuristic behavior cloning is developed to efficiently derive the joint maintenance and inventory strategies. Case studies show that the proposed PJMO algorithm reduces operational cost by 11.48% on average compared with the traditional threshold policy, while also achieving a 40% reduction in computational time. Compared with a separate PPO-based strategy for maintenance and inventory, the PJMO algorithm achieves an average cost reduction of 6.22% and a computational time decrease of 64%. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrates the advantage of the proposed joint maintenance and spare parts ordering strategy over the separate strategy, while also revealing the conditions under which the benefit of the joint strategy is greater.

Title: An Intelligent predictive maintenance framework for fault prediction in industrial internet of things environments
Authors: Baihua Zhang
Abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) remains an important component in maintaining the long-term reliability and performance of industrial systems, especially in Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Existing PdM methods often fail when dealing with high-dimensional, noisy, and heterogeneous sensor data due to poor feature selection and the inability to model multi-scale temporal dependencies. Thus, the Predictive Maintenance Fault Network (PdM-FaultNet) is designed to enhance fault prediction accuracy. PdM-FaultNet is the combination of the Enhanced Wombat Optimization Algorithm (EWOA) for the feature selection and Dual Quantum-inspired Denoising Autoencoder Transformer (DQDAT) for the predictive modeling. The EWOA enhances the search diversity, convergence speed, and identifies informative feature subsets. The DQDAT employs a dual-path decomposition strategy to capture long-term and short-term temporal patterns. It integrates Quantum-inspired Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) into a denoising autoencoder to derive nonlinear representation and a transformer to derive long-range dependencies. It attained a precision of 95.12%, 95.46%, and 96.08%, recall of 94.98%, 95.31%, and 96.03%, accuracy of 95.63%, 95.87%, and 96.54%, specificity of 94.74%, 95.02%, and 95.71%, and F1-scores of 95.05%, 95.38%, and 96.06% for the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance, Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems and SCANIA Component X datasets, respectively. Thus, PdM-FaultNet is a robust and reliable solution for advancing fault prediction capabilities in industrial applications.

Title: Multi-task hierarchical domain adaptation multi-expert attention network for cross-domain tool wear monitoring and remaining useful life estimation
Authors: Junbo Xin; Hua Huang; Yadong Wu; Yapeng Ren; Keren Wang; Zixiang Zhang
Abstract: Accurate tool wear monitoring and reliable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation of cutting tools are critical to guaranteeing the machining quality and production efficiency of CNC machining processes. However, existing methods generally exhibit limited generalization capability under cross-operating conditions, and fail to effectively characterize the dynamic coupling interactions between multiple cutting edges during tool degradation. To address this critical challenge, this paper proposes a novel Multi-Task Hierarchical Domain-Adaptive Multi-Expert Attention Network (MTHDA-MEA). First, time–frequency domain feature extraction and standardization are performed on multi-source sensor signals to enhance the feature representation capability for tool wear characterization. On this basis, a multi-task learning framework with a multi-expert mixture structure is constructed, where each expert module consists of a residual network (ResNet) cascaded with a multi-head self-attention (MHSA) mechanism. These modules collaboratively extract local temporal features and global long-range dependencies from the signals, while simultaneously capturing the common wear evolution patterns and individual wear characteristics of each cutting edge. To further improve the model's adaptability to variable machining conditions, a hierarchical domain adaptation mechanism is developed. This mechanism first aligns the global feature distributions to mitigate the overall inter-domain discrepancies, and then implements more refined distribution matching via sub-domain division according to physical tool wear stages. Finally, a health indicator is established by extracting the global maximum wear value from the model's output sequences, and a random forest regression model is adopted to construct the nonlinear mapping between this health indicator and tool RUL, thus achieving accurate RUL estimation. Experimental results on the PHM 2010 and Ideahouse 2021 public datasets demonstrate that the proposed MTHDA-MEA outperforms conventional single-domain adaptation methods and non-adaptive baseline models, achieving superior prediction accuracy and operational stability in cross-condition tool wear monitoring and RUL estimation tasks.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Predictive Maintenance for Mechanical Equipment in Smart Manufacturing
Authors: Jugulkar Lalitkumar Maikulal; Avinash H. Kolekar; Sushil Kumar Choudhary; Prashant Kumar Bhatiya; Manjeet Raj; Sourav Samanta; Chandan Kumar Choubey
Abstract: In computer numerical control (CNC) systems, the remaining useful life (RUL) of cutting tools is an important factor to be considered to prevent unplanned tool stoppages, premature tool replacement, and to ensure machining quality. This research suggests a group-aware and explainable machine learning-based approach to normalized RUL prediction using vibration, current and operating condition features. In contrast to the traditional CNC RUL studies performed by observation level random splitting, the proposed method ensures complete separation of tools between training, validation, and independent test partitions to avoid any information leakage between partitions at the level of the tools. Seven stable predictors were identified: five vibration variables, one current variable and the hardness of the workpiece, by using the stability-based feature selection. Four methods of repeated group validation, formal validation, macro-tool error and worst-tool performance were used to compare baseline and nonlinear regression models. Random Forest was chosen as the final model, with the validation RMSE value of 0.1676 and test RMSE value of 0.2377 and test R^2of 0.3417. The framework showed that unseen-tool generalization could be measured, but there was a variation between test tools that showed the difficulty of cross-tool degradation variability. The features related to vibration accounted for 66.29% of the total model importance, while the workpiece hardness and current variability accounted for 26.72% and 6.99% respectively. When the dominant predictive information was extracted from the vibration, the best performance was achieved by sensor-group ablation, and the complete feature configuration gave the best performance in terms of validation.

Title: Robust probabilistic estimating remaining useful life by considering aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty on health index data
Authors: Hamid Shiri; Pawel Zimroz; GovindVashishtha
Abstract: The estimation of remaining useful life (RUL) for industrial machinery is of utmost importance in condition-based maintenance (CBM) programs. Numerous studies have been conducted in this regard. However, the majority of machines operate under nonstationary conditions, posing a significant challenge for most approaches. Moreover, data collected from machines operating in harsh environments, such as mining equipment, wind turbines, and helicopters, are subject to non-Gaussian noise, further complicating traditional approaches. This paper presents a novel approach for prognosis purposes, specifically targeting the challenges posed by nonstationary characteristics, short-term dependence, and non-Gaussian noise in degradation modelling. Our approach is based on the maximum correntropy extended Kalman filter (MCEKF) and auto-regressive (AR) model to develop a robust technique that can provide a probabilistic solution for predicting RUL. To evaluate its effectiveness, we applied the proposed model to simulated degradation curves, considering both Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise, and conducted Monte Carlo analysis. In addition, we utilized two benchmark datasets to validate the performance of our approach in real-world scenarios. The results obtained from both the simulated and real datasets strongly support the efficacy of the proposed method.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Key Components of Transportation Vehicles: A Physics-Informed Perspective
Authors: Qing Zhu; Yucong Shi; Yun Feng; Ya Zhi Zhang; Haoran Tan; Yaonan Wang; Wanke Yu; Yongfu Li
Abstract: In transportation systems, accurately estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of critical components, such as aircraft engines, Battery Management Systems (BMSs), is crucial for the safe and reliable operation and manufacturing of transportation vehicles. However, most existing research overlooks the underlying physical information, which is vital for more precise RUL prediction. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a physics-informed method for predicting the RUL of key components of transportation vehicles. By integrating the Mamba network with a multi-head attention mechanism, we capture and emphasize key features and trends in the equipment’s operational state, improving prediction accuracy. Additionally, we introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework to model the underlying physical relationships between RUL and sensor data, incorporating these relationships as a regularization term in the loss function to enhance predictive capability and interpretability. We conducted experimental validation using the C-MAPSS aircraft engine dataset (operation) and the transportation vehicle chip manufacturing dataset (manufacture). The results show that the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of RUL prediction, providing strong support for the intelligent maintenance and reliability management of key components in transportation vehicles.
