Title: Synthetic Data-driven Hybrid Deep Learning Methodology for Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Sensors in Downhole Drilling Equipment
Authors: Aamir Bader Shah; Yu Wen; Jiefu Chen; Xuqing Wu; Renjie Hu; Xin Fu
Abstract: This work addresses the challenges of predictive maintenance in Industry 4.0 by applying advanced Deep Learning (DL) techniques to forecast the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of downhole drilling sensors. Due to the scarcity of publicly available run-to-failure datasets for downhole drilling tools, we generate synthetic data by applying sensor degradation characteristics to the open-source FORGE and Volve datasets. The synthetic data captures temperature fluctuations typically seen during drilling, reflecting common sensor failure modes. This methodology enables proactive maintenance planning by accurately predicting sensor failures in real-world drilling operations. The synthetic data driven approach allows us to infuse simulated anomalies into sensor data, reflective of wear from temperature exposure. These anomalies include zeroes and drifts, which represent common failure modes. Additionally, a cumulative temperature metric is integrated to comprehend stress accumulation. Given the variability in manufacturing and environmental conditions, sensors may exhibit different failure dynamics. To address this, we synthesize data across a spectrum of parameters to mirror an array of potential RUL trajectories, creating comprehensive training features for DL models. This approach allows us to accurately predict RUL on FORGE and Volve datasets, using a hybrid DL model. We experiment with various DL architectures to validate our approach. Initial results show that most DL models predict accurately during the early stages of sensor life. However, as sensors near end-of-life, readings become more nonlinear, causing prediction accuracy to decrease. We also observe that training on individual FORGE or Volve datasets yields precise RUL predictions, but accuracy declines when trained on combined datasets. To address these challenges, we implement a hybrid model with bidirectional GRU and LSTM networks, capitalizing on the unique features of our synthetic dataset through the networks' bidirectional learning capability. This model yields a notable MAPE of 14.92% on the combined dataset, validating our hybrid approach in forecasting sensor RUL in downhole drilling scenarios. We also propose a novel method for generating synthetic, yet realistic run-to-failure data for downhole drilling sensors, incorporating non-linear degradation patterns across various failure modes. By combining the FORGE and Volve datasets, both related to downhole drilling operations, we simulate a wide spectrum of operational conditions and sensor failure trajectories, improving model generalization and robustness. Additionally, we integrate temperature-driven failure mechanisms, enabling bidirectional learning to capture complex temporal dependencies, significantly enhancing RUL prediction accuracy. This approach extends beyond oil and gas, offering a scalable framework for predictive maintenance across diverse industrial systems.

Title: Enhance Predictive Maintenance with AI Models: Utilizing Real-Time Sensor Data with Industrial IoT to Prevent Equipment Failure
Authors: G. Pradeep; R. Rekha; S. Ganga; Maram Y. Al-Safarini; P. Nishitha; G. Karthikeyan
Abstract: Maintenance Practices in the Industry are Changing As predictive maintenance (PdM) is transforming how industries operate, managing and replacing parts after they broke or on a fixed calendar schedule to intervention only as needed based on the data that the part will fail before it does. Traditional maintenance plays critical roles in industrial systems, maintaining the equilibrium of either toomuch downtime or over-servicing that derive performancerobbing inefficiencies with specific consequences including safety hazards and costs. The growing world of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has opened up new ways to take advantage of real time sensor data, and how we can leverage this data for deeper insights into the health and prognosis of a machine. This study presents a holistic framework that incorporates AI models into IIoT based real-time monitoring systems to improve the predictive maintenance to reduce equipment downtime. The system operates through a network of sensors placed in the machinery on an industrial scale, which collect the data constantly from the parameters-such as vibration, temperature, pressure, acoustic signals and current flow. Various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models like Random Forests, SVMs, CNNs, LSTM are fed with these data streams to model the data. The same each algorithm is used to help prevent anomalies ahead of time, predict failure patterns and predict RUL. The network layers of edge/fog computing stream the data into the system with real-time data ingestion for instant analysis and decision making. One of its key characteristics is that it is compatible with various types of machines and industrial contexts. It automatically enables the system for use with specific equipment-rotating machinery, HVAC systems or conveyor motors-an example of a data preprocessing approach combined with feature selection that allows for retraining the model. On the plus side, including unsupervised learning methods also means we can identify new/unseen failure modes and further improve our maintenance system's robustness. We experimentally validated our method on public benchmark datasets and real-world industrial testbeds. That study shows that predictive maintenance using AI tools is 35 % more effective in reducing the duration of unexpected stops and increases the accuracy of scheduling time for service by 40 %, compared to traditional methods. This work presents a promising approach to develop smart maintenance and asset management using real-time sensor data coupled with cutting-edge AI analytics.

Title: Wear Prediction and Remaining Useful Life Estimation in CNC Milling Using Deep Learning-Based PHM Framework
Authors: Sahbi Wannes; Lotfi Chaouech; Jaouher Ben Ali; Eric Bechhoefer; Mohamed Benbouzid
Abstract: The accurate prediction of cutting tool wear and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is critical to improving the efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining operations. Traditional empirical approaches, such as Taylor's tool life equation, often fail to capture the complex nonlinear relationships between machining parameters, material properties, and tool degradation, particularly under dynamic industrial conditions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a data-driven Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) framework for tool wear prediction based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network architecture. The proposed model leverages multisensory signals - including vibration, spindle current, and temperature-collected from industrial CNC milling processes conducted under variable cutting conditions and high-speed operations. Comprehensive pre - processing and data normalization techniques are applied to enhance model convergence and predictive accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed stacked BiLSTM model achieves superior performance, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0353 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0307, validating its robustness and suitability for real-world PHM applications. Overall, the developed approach offers an effective and flexible solution for predictive maintenance, enabling optimized tool utilization and reduced unplanned downtime in modern manufacturing environments.

Title: A Tool Remaining Useful Life Prediction Model Based on Improved TCN Combined with BiGRU
Authors: Xiangyu Pan; Hui Yi; Wenjun Zhong
Abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy in traditional tool remaining useful life prediction, this paper proposes a prediction model based on an improved Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) combined with a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU). The proposed method enhances the conventional TCN residual module by introducing a parallel pooling structure and incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to improve the extraction capability of tool wear features. Additionally, BiGRU leverages its bidirectional characteristics and gating mechanisms to capture complex temporal dependencies within the sequence, thereby enhancing the prediction capability and accuracy of the model. The proposed method is evaluated on the PHM2010 tool wear dataset, where the coefficient of determination for tools C1, C3, and C4 on the validation set reaches 0.9978,0.9843, and 0.9886, respectively. Compared to TCN, TCN-LSTM, and other baseline methods, the proposed approach achieves significantly higher prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of prediction precision.

Title: Fisher-informed continual learning for remaining useful life prediction of machining tools under varying operating conditions
Authors: Gyeongho Kim; Yun Seok Kang; Sang Min Yang; Jae Gyeong Choi; Gahyun Hwang; Hyung Wook Park; Sunghoon Lim
Abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) of equipment has become an essential task in manufacturing. It not only helps prevent unexpected failures but also enables maximal utilization of available life, thus improving process efficiency. In practice, however, the use of multiple operating conditions that vary by time impedes efficient data-driven RUL prediction. Unlike conventional supervised learning setups, varying operating conditions generate heterogeneous data with time-varying generating distributions. Thus, existing approaches cannot be effectively applied due to increasing modeling and memory costs. One of the domains that suffer from this issue is machining, where RUL prediction of cutting tools is crucial for productivity. Considering realistic circumstances with varying operating conditions, this work proposes a method named Fisher-informed continual learning (FICL), which enables efficient tool RUL prediction that adaptively learns as conditions change without storing previous data and models. FICL uses Fisher information to improve generalization via sharpness-aware minimization and transfer knowledge between operating conditions through structural regularization. Experiments using datasets from real-world machining processes under five distinct operating conditions prove FICL's efficacy, indicating its superior prediction performance to existing methods for all operating conditions. Particularly, FICL manifests the least catastrophic forgetting, implying it effectively retains informative knowledge from varying operating conditions.

Abstract: Diamond grinding tools are suitable for machining alumina ceramics, which are hard and brittle, because these tools have high hardness and wear resistance. Alternatively, tool life can be assessed using process-related signals, such as acoustic emissions, tool temperature, spindle speed, feed rate, and grinding depth. This study analyzed grinding tool wear by collecting three-axis accelerometer data in the x-direction and y-direction and three-phase spindle current signals during the grinding of alumina ceramics. With continual grinding, the tool surface experiences increasing wear and cracking, which leads to greater vibration instability and fluctuations in frequency and acceleration. These dynamic variations serve as valuable indicators for predicting tool wear and estimating tool life. This study integrated machine learning (ML) and neural network models to analyze sensor data collected on tool wear. This analysis revealed complex variable relationships, enabling the development of a robust model for tool wear prediction.

Title: Wind Turbine Failure Prediction Using EDA and Multiple Classification Models
Authors: Hoang Anh Dang; Dung Dao Van; Duong Minh Hai
Abstract: Wind turbine systems play a vital role in the global transition to clean energy but are highly prone to mechanical and operational failures under harsh environmental conditions. This study presents a predictive maintenance framework that utilizes real-world sensor data and multiple machine learning algorithms to forecast potential turbine faults and enhance system reliability. The study emphasizes the F1-score as a key metric to capture the overall effectiveness of the classification models, ensuring that the results are not only accurate but also adequately account for critical cases. This methodological framework enables the identification of early warning signs of component degradation, offering a data-driven foundation for implementing effective predictive maintenance in wind energy systems.

Title: Domain-Specific Dual Network With Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Transfer Fault Prognosis Across Machines Using Multiple Source Domains
Authors: Smaran Khanal; Hong Zhong Huang; Cheng Geng Huang; Amrit Dahal; Tudi Huang; Sajawal Gul Niazi
Abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based fault prognostic methods often require extensive training data, which can be challenging to obtain due to time, cost, or safety constraints. However, labeled data from related but distinct machines, such as from accelerated degradation experiments, can offer valuable insights. Most transfer learning (TL) methods focus on single-source domain adaptation (DA) within the same machine, overlooking variability within the source domain and missing the opportunity to leverage multisource historical data effectively for application on different machines lacking run-to-failure data. The DSDN consists of two feature extraction modules: domain-specific degradation feature extraction (DSDFE) and domain-specific high-level feature extraction (DSHLFE). These modules incorporate a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) enhanced with multiple convolutional block attention modules (CBAMs) and a multilayer perceptron (MLP). The outputs from modules are concatenated to generate domain-invariant representations, effectively capturing both time-series and time-frequency spectrum features. By incorporating the DA technique, this approach mitigates discrepancies between the source and target domains, enabling accurate remaining useful life (RUL). The proposed method enhances the extraction of robust domain-invariant features for each source-target domain pair separately, improving prognostic accuracy by mitigating negative transfer. The effectiveness of the DSDN is validated through extensive case studies on single-source and multisource bidirectional transfer fault prognosis tasks across machines, utilizing bearing datasets from the IEEE prognostic and health management (PHM) Challenge 2012 and XJTU-SY. A comparative analysis further highlights its superiority over existing methods.

Title: Lifelong Learning for Fault Prognostics in Predictive Maintenance with Bayesian Neural Networks
Authors: Quy Le Xuan; Marco Munderloh; Jörn Ostermann
Abstract: Fault prognostics is one of the key enablers for the realisation of predictive maintenance. In today's era of digital transformation, deep learning (DL) has proven to be a promising data-driven solution for the task of fault prognostics with the ability to accurately predict the remaining useful life of industrial assets based on their historical condition-monitoring data. However, the deployment of DL-based fault prognostics models in practice still faces a number of critical challenges, especially in application scenarios with dynamic or evolving contexts suffering from data distribution shifts. Jointly training DL models using data from all contexts at once is typically impossible due to practical requirements regarding privacy constraints and resource limitations. Moreover, fine-tuning or training DL models in a classical sequential manner has been observed to typically suffer from catastrophic forgetting where adapting to a new context leads to drastically forgetting what has been learned previously. To address this problem, we proposed a novel lifelong learning framework with Bayesian neural networks for fault prognostics. Our proposed Bayesian lifelong learning method focuses not only on preserving the old knowledge learned so far but also allows to reserve the model flexibility for learning new knowledge from upcoming contexts. Experimental results on the benchmark C-MAPSS dataset of turbofan engine degradation data show the superiority of our proposed framework over other relevant lifelong learning methods. On average, we achieve a performance improvement of 10.2% and 75.3% in terms of final prediction accuracy and forgetting measure, respectively.

Title: Predictive Maintenance Optimization for Offshore Wind Farms with Power Losses and Wake Effect Considerations
Authors: Mingxin Li; Yuka Kikuchi
Abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, scheduling predictive maintenance reduces offshore wind farm maintenance costs and increases production efficiency. This paper optimizes maintenance planning for offshore wind farms by integrating wind farm layout and wake effects. A predictive maintenance model is developed to connect component health to proactive maintenance decisions. To enhance power production estimates, a wake model quantifies multi-wake-induced losses under varying wind conditions. The optimized maintenance plan minimizes costs and production losses, improving operational efficiency and economic viability. A case study of a generic offshore wind farm in Japan demonstrates the model effectiveness, providing actionable insights for better operation and maintenance (O&M) management in offshore wind projects.

Title: Threshold-Driven Performance Evaluation of VAE Anomaly Detection for Predictive Maintenance of Power Electronics Systems
Authors: Ratna Chakrabarty; Indranil Basu; Ayushmaan Dutta; Niladri Sanyal; Shubhra Samanta; Abhishek Majee
Abstract: The predictive maintenance of power electronics systems is essential for assuring reliability and reducing downtime across several applications, including electric vehicles and smart grids. Conventional rule-based fault detection techniques frequently lack the flexibility necessary for intricate, dynamic operating environments. This study introduces an innovative method for anomaly detection, an essential element of predictive maintenance, utilising a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) trained solely on normal operational data. This work's primary contribution is a threshold-based performance assessment of the Variational Autoencoder's most efficacious anomaly metric, Reconstruction Error (RE). The essential trade-off between optimising anomaly detection (Recall) and reducing false alarms (Precision) is examined by the systematic adjustment of a percentile-based threshold. Using a simulated dataset of power electronics sensor readings, our experimental findings demonstrate the superior efficacy of the VAE in anomaly identification. By conducting a comprehensive analysis of ROC/PR curves and performance metrics at various percentile thresholds, it's demonstrated that the system can be adeptly configured to emphasise either high recall or high precision, offering a pragmatic framework for real-world power electronic applications.

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Boost-Luo Converter-Fed Motor Drives in Renewable Energy Systems
Authors: G. Jawahar Sagar; Rakesh Kumar; Manoj Kumar Kar; Hasmat Malik; Amit Kumar Yadav; Tarkeshwar Matho
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy systems such as photovoltaic (PV) arrays and wind turbines demands highly efficient and reliable power conversion for motor drive applications. Boost-Luo converters, known for their high voltage gain and improved efficiency, are commonly used in such systems. However, power electronic components and motor drives are susceptible to faults due to thermal, electrical, and mechanical stress, leading to unplanned downtimes and maintenance challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive AI-based predictive maintenance framework for Boost-Luo converter-fed motor drive systems operating in renewable energy environments. The proposed system leverages Deep Neural Networks (DNN) for fault classification and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction. Multisensor data including voltage, current, temperature, and vibration are processed through feature extraction and dimensionality reduction techniques. Additionally, a Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm is employed to optimally tune the PI controller for voltage regulation and harmonic distortion minimization. Simulation results validate the system's ability to perform early fault detection, precise RUL estimation, and enhanced converter control, leading to improved system reliability and efficiency.

Title: A Predictive Maintenance Concept for LVDC Power Electronics-Based Circuit Breakers Using Artificial Intelligence
Authors: Dong Liu; Dimitrios Baros; Akshay Mahajan; Martina Josevski; Stefan Schmies; Juan Mena Carrillo; Martin Schellenberger; Lena Köhler; Johann Wagner; Anna Rusakova
Abstract: Power electronics-based circuit breakers for future DC systems, which are essential for the energy transition, have not yet reached a sufficient level of maturity. It is necessary to examine the requirements of real operation to improve these circuit breakers and to provide them with intelligent functions for optimized use under various environmental conditions. The investigation primarily focuses on researching, developing, and validating a real-time predictive maintenance concept for estimating the remaining useful lifetime (RUL) of power semiconductors in power electronics-based circuit breakers. This approach aims to significantly enhance the reliability and robustness of these circuit breakers and DC applications.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Power MOSFETs Based on UnetTSF
Authors: Jinquan Yang; Quanzhou Chen; Xinyu Li; Jiangnan Ji; Cong Peng
Abstract: Power MOSFETs are critical components in power electronic systems. Predicting its remaining useful life is crucial to prevent catastrophic failures. In this paper, we propose a method for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of power MOSFETs based on U-Net time series prediction model (UnetTSF). First, noise in the measurement data was eliminated through mode decomposition and data reconstruction, and then the degradation trajectory and RUL of the power MOSFETs are predicted using the UnetTSF. Experimental verification is conducted using NASA's public dataset, with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) selected as comparison algorithms. The experimental results indicate that the UnetTSF model achieves higher prediction accuracy and generalization, and performs well even with a small amount of data.

Title: Artificial Neural Networks Predictive Maintenance for Isolated Power DC-DC converters
Authors: Titus Fihavango; Kanat Manatov; Mehmet Timur Aydemir
Abstract: Given the increasing dependence of different industries on power electronic systems, particularly isolated power DC-DC converters, efficient predictive maintenance strategies have been developed to guarantee the reliable and efficient operation of these systems. Because of their complexity and dynamic nature, these converters are difficult to maintain using conventional methods like time-based or condition-based processes. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are a useful tool for increasing the accuracy and efficacy of predictive maintenance for isolated power DC-DC converters. The model predictive, which serves as an expert in this work, provides the data used to train the suggested ANNs. Once tuned, the ANNs are used directly to predict faults in isolated DC-DC power converters. LTspice and MATLAB simulations are used to validate the performance of the proposed artificial neural networks. The results of the simulation demonstrate that the performance of the ANNs-based isolated power DC-DC converter is improved when a trained ANNs model is used. Consequently, the F1 score of the artificial neural network is 99.34%, the accuracy score is 89.83%, the precision score is 94.64%, and the recall score is 95.83%. Based on the scores results, we suggest that artificial neural networks (ANNs) could be useful for predicting isolated power DC-DC converters.

Title: Optimizing Wind Turbine Reliability through a Machine Learning Predictive Maintenance Framework
Authors: Jack C.P. Cheng; Sergey Bronskiy; Chris K.C. Cheung
Abstract: The reliability and efficiency of wind turbines are crucial for maximizing energy production and ensuring the economic viability of wind farms. This study introduces a machine learning-based predictive maintenance pipeline designed to monitor and forecast critical faults within wind turbine systems. By leveraging Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems and comprehensive event log datasets, the pipeline incorporates advanced feature engineering techniques, along with Mutual Information and Lasso Regression, to identify and select the most relevant operational parameters. Four sophisticated classifiers LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) are employed and optimized using Genetic Algorithms (GAs), ensuring high predictive accuracy and robustness. The models address five different fault types, including generator overheating, gearbox oil issues, and fan failures. Compared to a majority-class baseline, the optimized models achieved macro-averaged accuracy exceeding 97 percent and F 1-scores ranging from 8 5 % to 9 7 % across the five fault types, demonstrating their capability to capture complex, nonlinear relationships inherent in SCADA data. The multi-class, time-aware classification framework categorizes faults into distinct time intervals (0-24 hours, 24-48 hours, 2-7 days, 1-4 weeks, and over 1 month), providing actionable time-to-failure predictions. By accurately predicting faults, the system facilitates proactive maintenance interventions, optimizing maintenance scheduling and resource allocation, and extending the lifespan of critical turbine components. This shift from reactive to proactive maintenance not only maximizes energy production but also enhances asset reliability and operational cost efficiency.

Title: Remaining useful life prediction of wind turbine high speed shaft bearing by sparsity measure based long short term memory network
Authors: Chuan Chen; Longxian Xue; Teng Wang; Yongbo Li; Khandaker Noman
Abstract: As a key component of wind turbine drive train, high-speed shaft (HSS) bearing often suffers from major failures. As a result, it is important to predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of wind turbine HSS bearing in advance. However, RUL prediction of HSS bearing often suffers from variable rotating speed of the wind turbine high speed shaft during real life application. Traditional features suitable under constant rotating speed condition are unable to track the degradation of HSS bearing in a consistent manner and thus in turn fail to facilitate efficient prediction of RUL. Considering aforementioned issue, in this research, RUL prediction method of wind turbine HSS bearing is proposed by utilizing the four representative sparsity measures namely kurtosis, gini index, negative entropy and reciprocal smoothness index. Degradation features have been fed into long short term memory (LSTM) network for calculating RUL and associated uncertainties. Effectiveness of the proposed research is validated by degradation data collected from real life 2 MW wind turbine HSS bearing. Experimental results show that the proposed approach enhances the RUL prediction capability of the wind turbine HSS bearing health along with associated uncertainty quantification in compare to traditional measures such as RMS and peak to peak value.

Title: Next-Generation Condition Monitoring: Digital Twin in RUL Predictive Maintenance for Main Bearings of Semi-Direct Drive
Authors: Da Lv; Chao Zhang; Wentao Zhao; Yongzhi Pang
Abstract: Against the backdrop of China's national strategic goals and supporting policies for carbon peak and carbon neutrality, For wind power enterprises, reducing actual operating costs has become a top priority. The main bearing's unexpected damage in Semi-Direct Drive Wind Turbines (SDDWT) due to delayed maintenance can affect the overall machine stability, even causing prolonged shutdowns. Excessive maintenance, however, also leads to a significant increase in operation and maintenance costs. High-precision remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for main bearings can effectively reduce the operation costs of SDDWT, but RUL research on large rotating machinery like SDDWT main bearings still faces critical challenges: unclear performance degradation mechanisms, limited valuable data samples, and severe lack of data labeling.To address the above issues, this paper takes the main bearings of SDDWTs as the research object. By integrating model-based Digital Twin technology with data-driven domain adaptation methods, it conducts studies on: (1) the analysis of performance degradation mechanisms for main bearings; (2) the theoretical methodology of model-data fusion for RUL prediction.

Title: Wind Turbine Reliability Through AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance and IIoT Integration
Authors: Deepak Dudeja; Nikhil Ranjan; Zainab Failhal Lami; Aya Ali Salim; Doaa Saadi Kareem
Abstract: Predominantly running to failure maintenance is practiced in the wind energy industry. This type of breakdown reaction is an expensive proposition for operators. Because wind turbines are dispersed throughout and remotely in accessible locations, they are difficult to access during the operation and maintenance of wind farms. Title: Federated Learning at the Edge for Wind Turbine Predictive Maintenance
Authors: Charis Michailidis; Alexandros Kalafatelis; Georgios Alexandridis; Averkios Vasalos; Andreas Oikonomakis; Achileas Economopoulos; Andrea Carolina Fontalvo Echavez; Daniel Iglesias Canelo; Michail Alexandros Kourtis; Panagiotis Trakadas

The proposed system leverages low-cost recording equipment to capture turbine-generated sound data, which are processed locally at the edge using Federated Learning, thus preserving data privacy and reducing communication overhead. Title: Vibration-Based Failure Prediction in Machinery: Novel Application of Time Series Decomposition and Neural Networks
Authors: W. C. Nirmal; H. K.I.S. Lakmal; K. J.P. Fernando
Abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) is critical in reducing downtime and minimizing operational costs in industrial settings. This study introduces a novel framework for vibration-based failure prediction by combining Seasonal and Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL) and deep learning models, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The framework processes multivariate vibration data collected from two-roller mills in a tire manufacturing facility. STL is employed to decompose the data into trend, seasonal, and residual components, enabling noise reduction and enhanced feature extraction. These components serve as inputs to LSTM models for predicting machine condition scores. A comprehensive analysis compared five deep learning architectures: LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Deeper LSTM, and Conv1D LSTM. The GRU and Conv1D LSTM demonstrated superior performance across multiple vibration axes, achieving low errors and high R<sup>2</sup> values. Results highlight the effectiveness of STL in preparing vibration data for sequential learning and the robust predictive capabilities of deep learning models. This study provides a scalable approach to PdM, enhancing reliability and efficiency in industrial machinery maintenance. Future work includes extending the framework to other machinery types and real-time monitoring systems.

Title: Uncertainty-Aware Online Remaining Useful Lifetime Estimation for Power Electronics
Authors: Kirill Ivanov; Horst Lewitschnig
Abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification is essential for remaining useful lifetime (RUL) estimation in safety-critical power electronics applications. This paper presents a comprehensive uncertainty estimation framework that adapts throughout the components lifetimes. We propose a novel approach that combines heteroscedastic variance modeling, adaptive prediction intervals, and asymmetric uncertainty bounds to capture both aleatory and epistemic uncertainties. Our method addresses critical challenges in quantifying uncertainty when limited degradation data is available, adapting uncertainty estimates as variance patterns change during degradation, and providing asymmetric bounds that reflect the higher risk of late failure predictions. We introduce a changepoint detection mechanism to identify variance regime transitions and adjust uncertainty quantification accordingly. Experimental validation on power MOSFET degradation data demonstrates that our uncertainty bounds achieve 94.3% coverage while maintaining tightness, with prediction intervals that appropriately widen during high-uncertainty periods and narrow as confidence increases. The proposed framework enables risk-informed maintenance decisions by providing interpretable and reliable uncertainty estimates suitable for edge deployment.

Title: Decision-making systems improvement based on explainable artificial intelligence approaches for predictive maintenance
Authors: Lala Rajaoarisoa; Raubertin Randrianandraina; Grzegorz J. Nalepa; João Gama
Abstract: To maintain the performance of the latest generation of onshore and offshore wind turbine systems, a new methodology must be proposed to enhance the maintenance policy. In this context, this paper introduces an approach to designing a decision support tool that combines predictive capabilities with anomaly explanations for effective IoT predictive maintenance tasks. Essentially, the paper proposes an approach that integrates a predictive maintenance model with an explicative decision-making system. The key challenge is to detect anomalies and provide plausible explanations, enabling human operators to determine the necessary actions swiftly. To achieve this, the proposed approach identifies a minimal set of relevant features required to generate rules that explain the root causes of issues in the physical system. It estimates that certain features, such as the active power generator, blade pitch angle, and the average water temperature of the voltage circuit protection in the generator's sub-components, are particularly critical to monitor. Additionally, the approach simplifies the computation of an efficient predictive maintenance model. Compared to other deep learning models, the identified model provides up to 80% accuracy in anomaly detection and up to 96% for predicting the remaining useful life of the system under study. These performance metrics and indicators values are essential for enhancing the decision-making process. Moreover, the proposed decision support tool elucidates the onset of degradation and its dynamic evolution based on expert knowledge and data gathered through Internet of Things (IoT) technology and inspection reports. Thus, the developed approach should aid maintenance managers in making accurate decisions regarding inspection, replacement, and repair tasks. The methodology is demonstrated using a wind farm dataset provided by Energias De Portugal.

Title: A Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework for Anomaly Detection, Fault Diagnosis, and Predictive Maintenance in Power Converter Systems
Authors: A. Aravind; C. Boopathi; M. Hariharasudhan; C. Senthilkumar
Abstract: Power converter systems are essential in modern electronics. However, they can experience various faults such as thermal issues, short circuits, open circuits, and voltage drops. These faults can cause system failures and safety risks. This paper presents a layered deep learning framework for detailed fault detection, classification, and remaining useful life prediction in power converter systems. The framework has a three-stage setup that includes an autoencoder for unsupervised anomaly detection, a convolutional neural network for classifying multiple faults, and a long short-term memory network for predicting future performance. The system processes voltage, current, and temperature data from standard sensor interfaces linked to an ESP32 microcontroller. Tested on a synthetic dataset with 10,000 samples that represent real fault patterns, the framework achieves perfect classification accuracy in classification across five fault types, 95.2% sensitivity in detecting anomalies, and a remaining useful life prediction error of 0.0000 (MAE). The layered design improves efficiency by directing data through the stages only when anomalies occur. Simulation results show inference times under 100 milliseconds and a total model size of 145.9 kilobytes, which suggests it is suitable for future embedded use. The proposed framework enhances predictive maintenance capabilities for power electronics in Industry 4.0 applications.

Title: Semi-supervised deep learning framework for predictive maintenance in offshore wind turbines
Authors: Valerio F. Barnabei; Tullio C.M. Ancora; Giovanni Delibra; Alessandro Corsini; Franco Rispoli
Abstract: The increasing deployment of wind energy systems, particularly offshore wind farms, necessitates advanced monitoring and maintenance strategies to ensure optimal performance and minimize downtime. Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems have become indispensable tools for monitoring the operational health of wind turbines, generating vast quantities of time series data from various sensors. Anomaly detection techniques applied to this data offer the potential to proactively identify deviations from normal behavior, providing early warning signals of potential component failures. Traditional model-based approaches for fault detection often struggle to capture the complexity and non-linear dynamics of wind turbine systems. This has led to a growing interest in data-driven methods, particularly those leveraging machine learning and deep learning, to address anomaly detection in wind energy applications. This study focuses on the development and application of a semi-supervised, multivariate anomaly detection model for horizontal axis wind turbines. The core of this study lies in Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BI-LSTM) networks, specifically a BI-LSTM Autoencoder architecture, to analyze time series data from a SCADA system and automatically detect anomalous behavior that could indicate potential component failures.Moreover, the approach is reinforced by the integration of the Isolation Forest algorithm, which operates in an unsupervised manner to further refine normal behaviour by identifying and excluding additional anomalous points in the training set, beyond those already labeled by the data provider. The research utilizes a real-world dataset provided by EDP Renewables, encompassing two years of comprehensive SCADA records collected from a single offshore wind turbine operating in the Gulf of Guinea. Furthemore, the dataset contains the logs of failure events and recorded alarms triggered by the SCADA system across a wide range of subsystems. The paper proposes a multi-modal anomaly detection framework orchestrating an unsupervised module (i.e. decision tree method) with a supervised one (i.e. BI-LSTM AE). The results highlighted the efficacy of the BI-LSTM Autoencoder in accurately identifying anomalies within the SCADA data that exhibit strong temporal correlation with logged warnings and the actual failure events. The model's performance is rigorously evaluated using standard machine learning metrics, including precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy, all of which demonstrate favorable results. Further analysis is conducted using CUmulative SUM (CUSUM) control charts to gain a deeper understanding of the identified anomalies' behavior, particularly their persistence and timing leading up to the failures.

Title: Machine Learning Implementation in Automotive Windshield Bending Furnace Failures Prediction

Abstract: Conveyor motors in tempering furnaces endure constant mechanical stress in windshield manufacturing, making them prone to failure. Seven machine-learning (ML) models were tested: Decision Tree (DT), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), K-Means, and Naive Bayes (NB). It achieved an accuracy of 98.43% on the validation set and 97.97% on the test set, with a precision of 97%, recall of 98%, and an F1-score of 97%. These results confirm the model's effectiveness in accurately detecting faults in tempering furnace conveyor motors. Consequently, we find that XGBoost holds significant potential for integration into automated predictive maintenance systems, aiming to reduce unplanned downtime and prolong the operational lifespan of industrial equipment.

Title: Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance of Wind Turbine: A Machine Learning Approach

Lastly, a computer-based application for the fault classification and maintenance prediction of wind turbines uses the suggested machine learning technique.

Title: Proposal for a Sustainable Model for Integrating Robotic Process Automation and Machine Learning in Failure Prediction and Operational Efficiency in Predictive Maintenance

Abstract: This paper proposes a sustainable model for integrating robotic process automation (RPA) and machine learning (ML) in predictive maintenance to enhance operational efficiency and failure prediction accuracy. The research identified a key gap in the literature, namely the limited integration of RPA, ML, and sustainability in predictive manufacturing, which led to the development of this model. Using the PICO methodology (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome), the study evaluated the implementation of these technologies in Alpha Company, comparing results before and after the model’s adoption. The intervention integrated RPA and ML to improve failure prediction accuracy and optimize maintenance operations. Results showed a 100% increase in mean time between failures (MTBF), a 67% reduction in mean time to repair (MTTR), a 37.5% decrease in maintenance costs, and a 71.4% reduction in unplanned downtime costs. Challenges such as initial implementation costs and the need for continuous training were also noted. Future research could explore integrating big data and AI to further improve prediction accuracy. This model demonstrates that integrating RPA and ML leads to operational improvements, cost reductions, and environmental benefits, contributing to the sustainability of industrial operations.

Title: Condition-Based Maintenance for Wind Farms Using a Distributionally Robust Chance Constrained Program
Authors: Heraldo Rozas; Weijun Xie; Nagi Gebraeel
Abstract: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) expenses account for up to 30% of the operating costs of wind farms. Condition-based maintenance (CBM) strategies, which incorporate predictive analytics into maintenance optimization, have been proven to be effective in reducing O&M costs in wind farms. Existing predictive CBM strategies for wind farms rely on the assumption that predictive analytics can accurately estimate the remaining lifetime distribution (RLD) of wind turbines, allowing for the direct implementation of stochastic programming or threshold-based policies. However, estimated RLDs can be inaccurate due to noisy sensors or limited training data. To address this issue, this paper develops a CBM strategy for wind farms that uses a Distributionally Robust Chance Constrained (DRCC) optimization model. Our formulation acknowledges that estimated distributions may be inaccurate and so seeks solutions that are robust against distribution perturbations within a Wasserstein ambiguity set. We show that the proposed DRCC optimization problem can be exactly reformulated as an integer linear program. We derive methods to strengthen the Big-M values of this reformulation, thereby enabling the DRCC model to be efficiently solved by off-the-shelf optimization software. The proposed strategy is validated through computational studies using real-world and synthetic degradation data, outperforming stochastic programming and robust optimization benchmark models.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Power Electronic Devices With Physics-Informed Deep Learning and Sparse Data
Authors: Le Gao; Chaoming Liu; Yiping Xiao; Chunhua Qi; Mingxue Huo
Abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of silicon carbide mosfets is essential for ensuring the reliability of power electronic systems, particularly under irradiation environments. However, most existing deep learning approaches rely on densely sampled degradation data, making them unsuitable for sparse-data conditions where degradation observations are limited. To address this limitation, we propose a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) method designed for sparse RUL prediction. The proposed method integrates total ionizing dose-induced degradation mechanisms, specifically interface and oxide trapped charge accumulation, into a Transformer-based neural architecture via a customized physics-informed loss function. This loss explicitly penalizes deviations from on-state resistance degradation trajectories, thereby embedding domain knowledge into the model training process. Subsequently, particle swarm optimization is employed to optimize the model hyperparameters. We benchmark our method against a baseline Transformer model without physics-informed components, using four evaluation metrics: mean absolute error (MAE), root-mean-square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R<sup>2</sup>), and a composite score. Under 90% data sparsity conditions, the PIDL approach achieves 27.90% reduction in MAE, 26.51% in RMSE, and 22.90% in score, demonstrating substantial gains in predictive accuracy and reliability. These results highlight the potential of PIDL in addressing sparse-data conditions.

Title: Temporal Sequence Modeling for Rare Failure Prediction in Industrial Machinery Using a Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model
Authors: Mehdi Faraz; Viktoriia Shubina; Tuomas Makila; Jukka Heikkonen
Abstract: Predictive maintenance is vital for enhancing industrial machinery reliability by detecting rare failures in high-dimensional, imbalanced sensor data. To address this, we developed a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) model for temporal sequence modeling, utilizing convolutional layers for spatial feature extraction and LSTM layers for capturing temporal dependencies within 6 -sample windows, classified as Normal or Transient (failure precursors). Main contributions include a robust feature selection method for imbalanced datasets, a comprehensive comparative analysis of state classification, temporal modeling, and unsupervised anomaly detection (Isolation Forest, One-Class Support Vector Machine), insights into temporal failure precursors, and an evaluation framework using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) to ensure robust assessment of rare events, balancing accuracy and early detection. The hybrid CNN-LSTM model achieved 97.88% overall accuracy, detecting 6 out of 7 failure cases with 85.71% recall, though precision was 30% due to false positives. Title: Predictive Maintenance and Operational Efficiency in Wind Energy using Machine Learning
Authors: Piyush Anand; Mohd Sadique; Priyanshu Kushwaha; Meenakshi Yadav
Abstract: Due to the increased reliance on renewable energy, wind power production requires increased reliability and cost-efficiency. Unforeseen failures of wind turbine parts including the generator, gearbox and blades are very costly to maintain, and also reduces energy generation. The sample has 40 predictors that consist of 40,000 training and 10,000 testing observations that represent the real-life conditions of the turbines. A number of classification models are developed and optimized, minimizing both the false negatives and false positives, the performance of which is measured using a new cost-sensitive metric that rates the ratio of the minimum possible maintenance cost to the costs caused by the model. According to experimental results, the proposed approach can not only increase the accuracy of failure detection, but also reduce total maintenance costs, which will reduce operational efficiency and reliability in wind energy systems.

Title: Predicting Pipe Failures: A Machine Learning Approach to Asset Management in District Heating
Authors: Tobias Vilbrad Rishoj Jensen; Maryamsadat Tahavori; Hamid Reza Shaker; Hamid Mirshekali
Abstract: As district heating networks (DHNs) across Europe near or surpass their intended service life, the need for proactive, data-driven maintenance and replacement planning is increasing. This paper presents a predictive asset management framework based on machine learning (ML) to assess the fault vulnerability of pipes. To train the ML algorithm, a combined dataset of both geospatial and operational data is implemented. While pressure is often estimated using complex hydraulic simulations, this study proposes and evaluates a lightweight linear pressure approximation method based on expert knowledge. The ML model is applied to a real DHN in Denmark through collaboration with the utility company HOFOR. Due to a significant class imbalance in the data (~1:215), multiple oversampling (OS) strategies are investigated. Model performance is evaluated using fault capture versus length capture (FCLC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) metrics. The inclusion of pressure data is found to improve the AUC by 4.5%, and the model captures over 40% of failures by inspecting only 10% of the network. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using ML-based fault vulnerability prediction as a tool for predictive maintenance and asset replacement planning in DHNs.

Title: A Study of Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Equipment Failures in Industrial Maintenance
Authors: Hiranmaye Sarpana Chandu
Abstract: A significant financial commitment is needed for the upkeep and replacement of highway equipment, and a thorough inspection of every piece of equipment is quite costly. Title: A Wind Turbine Gearbox Remaining Useful Life Prediction Approach Based on Optimal Dual Health Indicator and Deep Prediction Model
Authors: Li Lu; Tao Wang; Guanghui Zhai; Xinlong Yu; Bing Li; Yigang He; Fangming Deng; Wentao Dong
Abstract: Prediction of the fault trend and remaining useful life (RUL) of wind turbine gearboxes is crucial for ensuring reliable operation, yet existing methods often rely on either vibration or current signals alone. These single-modal approaches have limitations in accurately capturing both high- and low-frequency fault characteristics, which are crucial for comprehensive fault detection. To address this issue, this article proposes a novel dual health indicator method that integrates both vibration and stator current signals for more effective fault detection. The dual health indicator is constructed by combining high-order moments of vibration signals with information entropy from current signals. A deep prediction model integrating variational autoencoder (VAE), support vector data description (SVDD), and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks is proposed for realizing fault prognosis. By incorporating an attention mechanism and IMOCQPSO algorithm, the proposed method achieves improved feature extraction and fault prediction performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the effectiveness of this approach in predicting wind turbine gearbox faults under complex operating conditions, ensuring timely maintenance, and reducing downtime.

Title: A Multitask Learning Approach With Meta Auxiliary Generation Network for Remaining Useful Life Estimation
Authors: Xinyu Shang; Jie Shang; Zheng Jiang; Chen Jiang; Haobo Qiu; Liang Gao
Abstract: —The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has greatly facilitated prognostics and health management of complex mechanical equipment by enabling seamless data collection from interconnected devices, providing rich data sets crucial for advancing data-driven prognostics methodologies. In data-driven prognostics field, multitask learning (MTL) is a prominent way to acquire robust remaining useful life (RUL) estimation models by extracting complementary degradation information from highly related auxiliary tasks. However, as the key component of MTL, the auxiliary task is often designed manually with substantial effort, while not considering how to build a reasonable auxiliary task that can provide more worthy information for the primary RUL estimation task. In response to the challenge, this article proposed a MTL approach with meta auxiliary generation network for RUL estimation. First, a novel meta auxiliary generation network is developed to perform auxiliary task design. The network can generate auxiliary task labels automatically. It is updated by meta learning strategy with the RUL estimation loss as the main objective function, ensuring that the performance of the RUL estimation task can be significantly enhanced. Additionally, soft labels are introduced to the automated design to reduce the label scale difference between regression and classification tasks, and a new label regularization strategy is designed for improving the degradation consistency between regression and classification labels. Experiments on the turbofan engine and wind turbine gearbox data sets verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach.

Title: A Novel GRU-Augmented Time-Frequency Estimator for IGBT Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Yuankuang Li; Baohua Tan; Yingjie Zhang; Shuo Wang; Bolin Lian; Yuan Li; Zongming Tan
Abstract: Aging-induced failure of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) significantly restricts the reliability of power electronic systems. Accurate and efficient prediction of IGBT Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is critical for proactive risk mitigation and ensuring system stability. Despite numerous existing aging models and data-driven methodologies, maintaining prediction robustness and accuracy under diverse and complex operational scenarios remains challenging. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel GRU-Augmented Time-Frequency Estimator (GATE) tailored for IGBT lifetime prediction. GATE utilizes an autoregressive time-series prediction framework trained via the Teacher Forcing strategy to recursively decode the electrical parameters indicative of the IGBT’s aging state from rich time-frequency features. Experimental validations are performed using the square-wave power cycling dataset from the NASA Prognostics Data Repository. The results demonstrate that GATE significantly enhances prediction accuracy, reducing Mean Squared Error (MSE) to 0.0026 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) to 0.045, representing improvements of 38.1% and 19.6%, respectively, compared to the leading baseline method. Moreover, recursive forecasting experiments show that GATE precisely predicts the remaining power cycles until the aging threshold (defined as a 15% increase in Vce(on)) at various aging stages (10–60%). Ablation analyses further underline the critical contribution of the frequency-domain component. Collectively, these findings underscore GATE’s capability to reliably decode IGBT RUL directly from historical operational data, bypassing intricate electrical or mechanical modeling, thereby offering a practically deployable and broadly generalizable solution for lifetime management in power electronic devices.

Title: Condition Monitoring for Induction Motors: Vibration and Temperature Data Acquisition for Predictive Maintenance Analysis

In this study, hardware and software systems are developed. An accelerometer module and infrared temperature sensors are integrated with ESP32-based development boards, as well as the application of radio frequency transceiver modules for wireless data transmission. Printed circuit boards are designed and fabricated alongside a 3D-printed enclosure to house all of the hardware components. Data acquisition techniques for the vibration and temperature parameters are implemented and transmitted through a combination of ESP-NOW and radio frequency communication protocols. This paper recommends future studies to incorporate optimization on power management, integration of different communication protocols, reduction of device footprint, as well as field trials for outdoor, weatherexposed applications.

Abstract: The railway traction system plays a crucial role in converting electrical energy into mechanical power to move trains, making its reliability and efficiency vital for the safe and smooth operation of railways. PdM integrates diagnostic data, performance data, maintenance history, operating conditions, and equipment design to predict when maintenance is required. A key element in PdM is estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of components, which indicates how much time or usage remains before failure occurs. Accurate RUL estimation helps operators plan maintenance effectively, preventing unplanned downtime and reducing maintenance costs. The first step in this research involves calculating the Health Indicator (HI), where in this research to get value of HI is determined by multiplying the health condition parameters with a sensor coefficient. By analyzing trends in these parameters over time, the degradation behavior of the traction system can be assessed. A value under 0.8 indicates that the system is approaching a critical condition and requires maintenance to prevent failure. By applying data-driven methods for RUL estimation and health monitoring, this study contributes to improving the reliability, safety, and cost-effectiveness of railway operations through optimized maintenance strategies.

Title: Physics-informed Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Rotating Machinery
Authors: Supeng Li; Yong Zhang; Yanghui Ou; Ting Liu; Wei Zhou; Dewen Wang
Abstract: Rotating machinery often experiences fatigue and degradation under complex loads and extreme conditions. Accurately predicting their remaining useful life (RUL) is thus essential for system safety and efficient maintenance. At the same time, the rotating machinery degradation trend is nonlinear with significant individual differences, and it is difficult to accurately learn the physical degradation mechanism by relying only on the original sample data, which can easily lead to a lack of generalization and physical consistency in the prediction results. To address the above problems, this paper proposes an enhanced Transformer architecture that incorporates prior physical knowledge, referred to as the Physics-informed Transformer (PI-Transformer). The model employs a multi-layer self-attention mechanism in the encoder to deeply extract degradation-related temporal features. It innovatively incorporates prior knowledge of crack propagation by constructing a physical neuron module, and further integrates physical features with data-driven features through nonlinear fusion using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN). Experiments on real rotating machinery full life cycle data show that the method in this paper excels in accuracy, stability and interpretability, providing a new methodology support for intelligent operation and maintenance of industrial equipment.

Title: Predictive Maintenance of Aircraft Engines: Machine Learning Approaches for Remaining Useful Life Estimation
Authors: J. Deepika; Pappuru Manikanta Reddy; Kothaluri Murari; Boyana Rahul
Abstract: In the realm of predictive maintenance for aircraft engines, ensuring precise and timely predictions of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is paramount to enhancing safety, reducing costs, and minimizing downtime. While deep learning models dominate this field, their complexity, high computational demand, and lack of interpretability can hinder practical deployment in real-world scenarios. This study demonstrates the potential of machine learning models as an efficient and interpretable alternative for RUL prediction, leveraging the publicly available C-MAPSS dataset from NASA. Using C-MAPSS dataset, we integrated PostgreSQL for scalable data storage and Flask for interactive real-time visualization, creating a seamless pipeline from data ingestion to result interpretation. Preprocessing steps, including normalization, noise removal via box plots, and feature engineering, ensured a clean and reliable dataset. Among the models evaluated—XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, KNN, and Linear Regression—XGBoost emerged as the best performer, achieving an RMSE of 23.8 and an R<sup>2</sup> score of 0.67. These results nearly matches the accuracy typically associated with deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. Feature importance analysis through Explainable AI (XAI) further revealed critical insights into sensor contributions, enhancing interpretability and trust in the predictions. This work underscores the practicality and effectiveness of machine learning in predictive maintenance, offering a robust, transparent, and resource-efficient approach to RUL prediction. The findings highlight its potential to meet industry needs where simplicity, accuracy, and interpretability are critical for decision-making and operational efficiency.

Title: Understanding engine related safety occurrences and the implications for prognostics and health management systems
Authors: Alexander Somerville; Graham Wild
Abstract: This research examines trends and features in engine-related safety occurrences reported to the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) from 1970 to 2019 to inform the development and direction of research into Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) systems for aircraft engines. A logistic regression model is used to determine whether the likelihood of an occurrence being classified as serious (a combined category of accidents and serious incidents) has changed over the 50-year period, considering factors such as engine type, activity group, and registration type. The results indicate a statistically significant, though negligibly small, positive change in the likelihood of a serious engine-related occurrence over time. This change persists even after accounting for the influence of engine type, activity group, and registration type. Compared to piston engines, turboprop, turbofan, and turboshaft engines show lower odds of serious occurrences, while recreational registered aircraft show higher odds compared to Australian VH-registered aircraft. Commercial air transport is associated with lower odds of a serious occurrence, while the military activity group does not show a significant association. The findings underscore the need for continued research and development of advanced PHM systems to enhance aircraft engine safety and reliability.

Title: Aero-Engine Condition-Based Maintenance Planning Using Reinforcement Learning
Authors: Michael Q. Ignacio; Prospero C. Naval
Abstract: In commercial aviation, aircraft maintenance planning is an optimization problem that balances several factors regarding safety / reliability, cost, and other airline operation concerns. This study compared the performance of two model-free Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms, Deep Q-Network (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), in solving the maintenance planning problem of aero-engine. The Commercial Modular AeroPropulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) dataset was used to model the degradation of aero-engine health, in terms of remaining useful life (RUL), as a finite Markov Decision Process (MDP). Actual cost (in millions of US dollars, $M) related to maintenance, operations and useful life were used as penalties for the aero-engine environment. Two methods of representing the input state were also evaluated: using the mean over the decision window for each input features, and using the whole decision window time series. The PPO planning agent using mean state input has the lowest average cost and least unscheduled maintenance events. The PPO planning agent using time series state input, on the other hand, tends to prioritize higher utilization of the engine’s useful life at a comparable average cost, but allowed more unscheduled maintenance events. The above results show the inherent maintenance planning trade-off between component reliability and utilization of useful life.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Aircraft Engines by Mixer based architecture under Complex Working Condition
Authors: Yutao Jiang; Yi Chai; Yun Jiang; Liping Guo; Xiaoxiao Ma; Zhiyuan Lv
Abstract: Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction plays a critical role in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of aircraft engines, supporting condition-based maintenance, reducing operational risks, and improving overall reliability. In complex working conditions, RUL estimation is challenging due to the nonlinear and non-stationary nature of multivariate sensor data. In this work, a Mixer-based architecture for RUL prediction of aircraft engines was introduced, which effectively extracts and fuses time series features from multiple sensors in both token and channel dimensions by transposing matrix. Motivated by the similarities between multivariate time series forecasting and RUL estimation, the introduced approach leverages advanced feature fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. Furthermore, to address predictive uncertainty, we combine Distance-Weighted Information Noise Contrastive Estimation Loss with Jensen-Shannon Divergence, improving both predictive accuracy and robustness.

Title: Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Rotating Machinery via Data-Driven Models
Authors: Qi Li; Liuxiangzi Yang; Feng Wang
Abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rotating machinery is critical for ensuring operational reliability and reducing maintenance costs. This paper presents a data-driven framework for RUL prediction, integrating advanced machine learning techniques and experimental validation. The proposed method leverages vibration and sensor data from rotating machinery, combined with deep learning models such as LSTM and Transformer, to capture complex degradation patterns. The NASA C-MAPSS dataset is used to validate the approach, demonstrating significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to traditional methods. The study includes detailed mathematical derivations of model architectures, experimental data analysis, and performance evaluation using metrics like RMSE and MAE.

Title: Physics-Guided Spatio-Temporal Graph Multi-Task Learning for Aircraft Engine Prognostics and Health Management
Authors: Le Tian; Yiping Gao; Zerui Xi; Liang Gao; Xinyu Li
Abstract: Accurate health state assessment and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction are crucial for ensuring aircraft engine operational safety and formulating predictive maintenance strategies. However, most existing methods address these tasks independently, overlooking their intrinsic correlations as well as the spatio-temporal dependencies embedded in sensor data. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a Physics-Guided Spatio-Temporal Graph Multi-Task Learning (PG-STG-MTL) framework that jointly optimizes health state assessment and RUL prediction. The framework incorporates physical-guided graph structures and irreversible degradation constraints to enhance physical consistency and model robustness. It employs a Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts (MMoE) to enable task-specific feature learning while sharing latent representations, utilizes dilated temporal convolution for multi-scale feature extraction, and incorporates graph attention networks to capture sensor dependencies. Experiments on the N-CMAPSS dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving an RMSE of 5.01 for RUL prediction and an F1 score of 0.84 for health state assessment. Additionally, the model effectively detects initial failure points while imposing the irreversible degradation constraint, making it suitable for industrial applications.

Title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Aircraft Engines: A Robust Framework for Risk-Aware Maintenance
Authors: Amith Srivatsa; Vishwa Iranna B. Goudar; Thumma Naveen; Rashmitha Madhavi Peri; Debjani Kangsa Banik; M. Rajesh Kumar
Abstract: Aircraft components degrade over time, directly impacting reliability and performance. This project aims to develop a machine learning framework for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of aircraft engines based on comprehensive life cycle data, to optimize maintenance strategies and mitigate risks associated with component failure. A diverse set of regression and classification models-including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naïve Bayes, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)-are implemented and evaluated on NASA's C-MAPSS dataset to estimate engine lifetimes. The key focus is to predict the accurate RUL for turbofan engines, particularly under High-Pressure Compressor (HPC) failure scenarios, and specifically targeting low RUL values to prevent critical risks. Physics-informed machine learning approach incorporates enhanced predictions by improving the robustness of maintenance planning.

Title: Lifespan-Weighted Contrastive Learning Method and Its Application in Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rotating Machinery
Authors: Yiming Wang; Yue Zhang; Huaxi Shi; Qiaowei Tao; Liang Zhang
Abstract: Remaining useful life prediction is a crucial component of equipment fault prognosis and health management, playing a vital role in maintenance and failure prevention. With the rapid development of machine learning techniques, data-driven RUL prediction methods have been widely adopted. However, challenges such as low signal-to-noise ratio, poor data quality, label scarcity, and imbalanced data distribution persist. To address these issues, this paper proposed an end-to-end RUL prediction method based on contrastive learning. By introducing a lifespan-weighted term into the contrastive loss function, a contrastive learning pre-training method tailored for full-lifecycle data of critical rotating machinery components was constructed and adaptive learning for nonlinear degradation was achieved. Comparative experiments and ablation studies were conducted using bearing and gear datasets. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method outperforms typical models in predicting the remaining useful life.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction Method Based on Performance Trajectory Similarity and Transfer Fusion
Authors: An Zhou; Yujie Cheng; Dong Qian; Chengcheng Wang; Jia Wen; Laifa Tao
Abstract: The aircraft engine is a crucial component of aircraft. The failure of aircraft engines usually leads to serious accidents and significant economic losses. Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is crucial for enhancing the reliability of aircraft engines and flight safety. This paper proposes a method for RUL prediction based on performance trajectory similarity and transfer fusion. Firstly, time-domain moving for historical performance data is used to select similar degradation trajectory. Degradation trajectory data of similar engines is selected for model training. Subsequently, a RUL prediction model based on long short-term memory (LSTM) networks is constructed to explore the relationship between engine monitoring data and RUL. Multiple prediction models based on similar engines are used for RUL prediction of the test engine. Finally, the different prediction results are fused according to the weights of similar engines, thereby obtaining the final RUL prediction result. Besides, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated based on the C-MAPSS simulation dataset.

Title: PhyRes-BiLSTM: Physics-Informed Residual Bidirectional LSTM for Aircraft Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Changwei Liu; Jiadong Lou; Guangwei Wen; Guoqiang Li; Rui Wu; Xiaojun Liang; Chunhua Yang; Weihua Gui
Abstract: The prediction of an aircraft engine's Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is crucial for flight safety and maintenance cost control. In this paper, a novel physics-informed residual bidirectional LSTM model (PhyRes-BiLSTM) is proposed. Physical laws were integrated with deep learning to address the limitations of traditional methods. The model was constructed by 1) integrating monotonicity constraints into the Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to enforce decreasing RUL predictions over time, and 2) establishing residual connections to optimize gradient propagation and alleviate challenges in training deep networks. Experiments using the NASA CMAPSS benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed PhyRes-BiLSTM significantly outperforms mainstream models such as GRU and TCN. In the FD001 subset, it achieves improvements of 8.0%, 4.4%, 2.6%, and 2.1% in RMSE, MAE, R2, and EVS, respectively, compared to the best baseline model (Transformer). The physical constraint mechanism effectively suppresses unreasonable predictions, providing a highly reliable solution for predictive maintenance of aircraft engines.

Title: Attention-based Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit Method for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aircraft Turbofan Engine
Authors: Abuduwaili Abulaiti; Guichen Yan; Junkai Wang
Abstract: Accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) in aero-turbofan engines is critical for ensuring flight safety. However, the complex operating conditions and high-dimensional nature of sensor data present challenges for dimensionality reduction. Furthermore, the multidimensional complexity of operational data hinders prediction models' ability to focus on critical degradation features, ultimately compromising RUL prediction accuracy. To address these limitations, this study proposes an attention-integrated bidirectional gated recurrent unit model (Attention-BiGRU) for RUL prediction. The bidirectional architecture extracts both historical and prospective temporal features from time- series data, while the attention mechanism dynamically weights key information to prioritize salient degradation characteristics. This dual approach enhances prediction accuracy through targeted feature emphasis. Experimental validation on the Aircraft Turbofan Engine dataset demonstrates statistically superior prediction performance compared to existing benchmark models.

Title: Research on Aircraft Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction Based on a Hybrid CNN-LSTM Network
Authors: Jingzhi Luo
Abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of equipment is a core technical challenge in industrial operations and maintenance. The difficulty lies in the dual requirement to simultaneously capture subtle degradation features from sensor data and to model long-term temporal dependencies over the equipment's lifecycle-demands that are difficult for a single deep learning architecture to meet concurrently. Title: A Machine Learning Based Ensemble Approach to Predict Remaining Useful Life of Aircraft Engines

Abstract: The advancements in the aviation sector have propelled humanity to progress at a rapid pace in the last few decades. Recent real-life incidents due to mechanical failures relating to engine malfunction and its other related parts have claimed a lot of human lives. Title: TTSNet: Transformer–Temporal Convolutional Network–Self-Attention with Feature Fusion for Prediction of Remaining Useful Life of Aircraft Engines
Authors: Zhaofei Li; Shilin Luo; Haiqing Liu; Chaobin Tang; Jianguo Miao
Abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of aircraft engine operation. However, aircraft engines operate in harsh conditions, with the characteristics of high speed, high temperature, and high load, resulting in high-dimensional and noisy data. This makes feature extraction inadequate, leading to low accuracy in the prediction of the RUL of aircraft engines. To address this issue, Transformer-TCN-Self-attention network (TTSNet) with feature fusion, as a parallel three-branch network, is proposed for predicting the RUL of aircraft engines. The model first applies exponential smoothing to smooth the data and suppress noise to the original signal, followed by normalization. Then, it uses a parallel transformer encoder, temporal convolutional network (TCN), and multi-head attention three-branch network to capture both global and local features of the time series. The model further completes feature dimension weight allocation and fusion through a multi-head self-attention mechanism, emphasizing the contribution of different features to the model. Subsequently, it fuses the three parts of features through a linear layer and concatenation. Finally, a fully connected layer is used to establish the mapping relationship between the feature matrix and the RUL label, obtaining the RUL prediction value. The model was validated on the C-MAPSS aircraft engine dataset. Experimental results show that compared to other related RUL models, the RMSE and Score reached 11.02 and 194.6 on dataset FD001, respectively; on dataset FD002, the RMSE and Score reached 13.25 and 874.1, respectively. On dataset FD003, the RMSE and Score reached 11.06 and 200.1 and on dataset FD004, the RMSE and Score reached 18.26 and 1968.5, respectively, demonstrating better performance of RUL prediction.

Title: Aircraft Engine Remaining Useful Life Estimation via a Graph Attention Reconcile Network Model Based on Physical Equations and Sensor Data
Authors: Wenyue Cui; Shuo Zhang; Tao Sun; Rui Wang
Abstract: The prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for aircraft engines stands as a critical process ensuring the safe operation of aircraft. Traditional methods for estimating RUL primarily mine temporal features within data, frequently overlooking the complex interdependencies among multivariate signals. Furthermore, in actual physical systems such as aircraft engines, there is a dynamic linkage among the sensor data. Ignoring these subtleties can result in a reduction of estimation accuracy. Addressing this challenge, the article proposes a novel graph attention reconcile network integrated with priori knowledge to predict aircraft engine RUL. It constructs a time-series graph by fusing sensor data with aerothermodynamics equations. The network employs dual attention mechanisms to capture spatio-temporal features: a spatial attention module to identify relationships between sensors, and a temporal attention module to highlight the importance of different time steps. Additionally, a LSTM layer is incorporated to enhance RUL prediction accuracy. Comparative analysis using the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation datasets and new Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation datasets demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed model over other prevailing approaches.
