Title: Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction Based on Multi-scale Feature Extraction and Convolutional Attention Mechanism
Authors: Yuehua Yu; Qi Xi; Jing Wang
Abstract: The precise determination of a bearing’s Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is paramount for upholding equipment operational safety and for the effective execution of predictive maintenance programs. To counteract the deficiencies of established deep learning methodologies, especially their limitations in extracting bearing wear-and-tear features at diverse scales and their less-than-optimal attention frameworks for temporal data, this study introduces an innovative hybrid forecasting architecture: the Multi-scale Time-series Convolutional Transformer (MTCT). The MTCT integrates multi-scale feature fusion with convolutional attention mechanisms. The model employs a temporal multi-scale segmentation strategy to extract time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency domain features, while incorporating an improved Time-Series Convolutional Block Attention Module (TS-CBAM) to dynamically weight critical degradation features. Additionally, a Transformer encoder is utilized to capture long-range dependencies, and a bias correction mechanism is introduced in the loss function to enhance prediction stability. Empirical assessment was carried out employing vibration signals from bearings throughout their complete lifecycle, captured under various operational parameters. This involved contrasting the proposed complete architecture with its constituent variants to ascertain the effectiveness of both multi-resolution feature integration and the attention framework. The outcomes reveal that the presented model offers a significant advancement in capturing degradation progression, demonstrating prediction precision and resilience that surpasses existing advanced methodologies.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Estimation of Remaining Useful Life of Bearing Using Time–Frequency Spectrogram
Authors: R. Subha; Radhakrishnan Rekha; M. Selvadass
Abstract: Bearings are the most sensitive part of a motor drive system and predicting their health condition is very crucial in estimating the system’s Remaining Useful Life (RUL). Precise estimation of RUL is essential to increase machine reliability, decrease fault incidents, and prevent unscheduled downtime. The frequency, amplitude, and patterns of the vibration signals generated as a result of mechanical movements within the bearing system are indicative of its health status and the developments in the field of sensor technology have fueled data-driven approaches to discover the degradation trends by the analysis of condition monitoring data. Deep learning serves as a powerful and valuable prediction tool that can utilize raw data directly, eliminating the necessity for feature extraction. Spectrogram depicts the variation of frequency content in a signal over time and can serve as a potential diagnostic tool for detecting bearing irregularities. In this work, the spectrograms derived from vibration signals have been used to train a convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to predict the RUL of a bearing. The experimental data collected from the PRONOSTIA setup has been used for this purpose. The CNN model has been trained and tested and the results are presented. The performance of the model has been compared with similar works in the literature and found to be good.

Title: Few Shot Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aviation Hydraulic Pump Based on Variational Autoencoder and Wiener Process
Authors: Zhiwei Zheng; Jiahui Sun; Yuhong Huang; Lin Wang; Chao Zhang; Shaoping Wang; Rentong Chen
Abstract: As the core power components of aviation hydraulic systems, it is of great importance to keep ensure flight safety and reliability. However, it is still a big challenge to predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of hydraulic pump accurately due to its high reliability and long service life. To address the problem mentioned above, this paper proposes a novel few shot RUL prediction framework based on variational autoencoder (VAE) and Wiener process. Firstly, VAE and long short-term memory network (LSTM) are integrated together to implement data augmentation. Secondly, the degradation model is established based on the Wiener process considering random effects. Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Bearings Based on Generative Pretrained Transformer

Title: Digital Twin-Enhanced Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Bearings using Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Hybrid Model
Authors: Jie Zhou; Zhensheng Lin; Gang Niu
Abstract: Bearings are critical and highly susceptible components in mechanical equipment, with their operational status and lifespan being vital to the stable operation of the entire system. Initially, due to random fluctuations in the collected vibration signals influenced by various environments, wavelet transform is employed to denoise the signals. Subsequently, for the vibration signals during the bearing degradation phase, a multi-domain feature set is established. By constructing a comprehensive evaluation metric that considers feature monotonicity and trendability, the final degradation feature set is selected. The selected degradation features are then linearly weighted to construct a comprehensive health indicator. Finally, an MSCNN-Transformer model is developed. The MSCNN enhances the model's ability to extract features at different scales. By fitting the trend of the bearing's health indicator, the model predicts the bearing's remaining useful life. On this basis, a digital twin model that accurately reflects the physical characteristics and behaviors of the bearing is constructed and updated in real-time based on experimental data. The MSCNN-Transformer model algorithm is embedded into a visualization system, and a visualization platform developed using Virtual Reality technology integrates multidimensional data to optimize maintenance and repair processes in practical engineering applications.

Title: A Dual-stream Transformer Ensemble for Rolling Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Jingyi Huang
Abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings is critical for predictive maintenance. To overcome limitations of existing methods in capturing longterm dependencies and complex degradation patterns from raw vibration signals, this paper proposes a novel dual-stream Transformer framework. The framework integrates two advanced models: Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST), which excels at modeling local temporal features through patching, and inverted Transformer (iTransformer), which effectively captures cross-sensor correlations through architectural inversion. A twolayer MLP weighting module adaptively fuses their predictions by learning to assign optimal weights that integrate the complementary strengths of both streams. Furthermore, an exponential degradation model translates predicted vibration signals into RUL estimates using an exponential amplitude-todegradation mapping. Experimental results on the PHM2012 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method not only outperforms its individual components but also surpasses other mainstream deep learning approaches including CNN-LSTM and standard Transformer across all evaluation metrics, validating the effectiveness of this ensemble approach.

Title: Video-Based Vibration Analysis for Predictive Maintenance: A Motion Magnification and Random Forest Approach
Authors: Walid Gomaa; Abdelrahman Wael Ammar; Ismael Abbo; Mohamed Galal Nassef; Tetsuji Ogawa; Mohab Hossam

Traditional contact-based vibration sensors face limitations including measurement perturbations, point-specific data coverage, and installation constraints. This paper presents a novel non-contact machinery fault detection framework combining Eulerian video motion magnification with machine learning classification. The methodology comprises two integrated components. Primarily, a video-based vibration analysis pipeline utilizing Eulerian motion magnification with dense optical flow, which accomplish comprehensive signal processing for feature extraction using Fast Fourier transform. The video processing allowed to identify distinct vibration signatures, from imbalance conditions showing amplitude variations to proportional fault severity ultimately offering a cost-effective solution for industrial condition monitoring applications.

Title: Fuzzy Predictive Maintenance for Railway Transport Networks
Authors: Sarra Mellouli; Anis Mhalla; Simon Collart-Dutilleul; Hassani Messaoud
Abstract: In railway systems, every equipment item requires maintenance, which in turn can affect the availability of a certain machine and the planned transport schedule. The findings of this paper reveal that fuzzy logic can also be applied to sustain the travel process in the degraded modes of operation, while guaranteeing satisfactory traffic quality and safety levels for the customers by incorporating experts.

Title: Driving Sustainable Development Goals: Ensemble Classification for Efficient Industrial Machinery Predictive Maintenance
Authors: Rashmi Benni; Shashank Alagawadi; Shashikumar Totad
Abstract: Predictive maintenance, which leverages historical and real-time data to anticipate equipment failures, is pivotal in enhancing safety, reducing costs, extending machinery lifespan, and minimizing downtime across industries such as energy, transportation, and manufacturing. Traditional classification methods typically rely on a single model’s predictions. However, ensemble classification amalgamates predictions from multiple models, harnessing various perspectives to enhance adaptability and accuracy. This study delves into the application of ensemble methods—including Gradient Boosting (GB), CatBoost Classifier, and Random Forest for the predictive maintenance of industrial machinery. Each ensemble technique is meticulously evaluated in diverse industrial contexts, with an emphasis on how varying hyperparameters influence model performance. The study proposes a method for optimizing results through parameter adjustment. By boosting efficiency and reliability, promoting innovation via IoT and AI integration, and ensuring infrastructure sustainability, predictive maintenance aligns with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 9. It also supports SDG 12 by maximizing resource utilization, reducing waste and environmental impact, promoting sustainable production, and cutting energy consumption and emissions. Additionally, by lowering carbon emissions, mitigating environmental risks, and extending machinery lifespan to reduce frequent replacements, it contributes to SDG 13. This paper provides valuable insights and guidance for researchers and industries seeking enhanced strategies for machinery predictive maintenance.

Abstract: With the continuous advancement of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies, data-driven predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a key approach to enhancing equipment reliability and operational efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce a rolling prediction-based fault warning mechanism to enable early detection and proactive response to potential anomalies. A practical application on the vapor recovery system of gas stations is conducted to validate the system. Experimental results demonstrate that the IPRFformer model outperforms baseline models in terms of average prediction error and anomaly trend detection. During the maintenance phase, our method effectively suppresses false alarms through a triple-limit-exceeding trigger mechanism and successfully anticipates key faults in real-world scenarios, validating the system's early warning capability and practical engineering value.

Title: Gate Leakage Current Characterization and Remaining Useful Lifetime Prediction in Silicon Carbide MOSFETs
Authors: Mustafa Murat Sezer; Fatih Akici; Mojtaba Afshar; Bhanu Teja Vankayalapati; Bilal Akin
Abstract: This article presents a comprehensive study on gate leakage current characterization of silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs and the prediction of the device's remaining useful lifetime (RUL) using machine learning (ML) methods. Recent studies in SiC MOSFETs reliability recognize gate leakage currents as an aging indicator. However, most measurements are confined to periodic measurements of one device type. This limitation raises concerns in SiC MOSFETs, particularly for safety-critical applications like aerospace and electric vehicles (EVs). To address this concern, this study proposes a functional circuit capable of measuring gate leakage current at 100 samples per second rate, facilitating the aging and failure characterization accurately. In addition, it showcases the effective application of practical ML methods for predicting device longevity. Experimental measurements across devices from different vendors consistently reveal declining gate leakage current and increasing threshold voltage with aging. Thanks to the high-resolution measurement capability, for the first time it is also shown that the gate leakage current surges from nanoampere levels to milliampere levels within 1-2 s at the end of the lifetime, signifying impending device failure. This time window provides a safe-stop opportunity that enables an additional protective action way before any fault-related current or voltage overshoots appear. Finally, through the application of a combination of gate leakage current measurements and practical ML methods, the accurate prediction of the RUL of SiC MOSFETs is achieved.

Authors: Lydia Yahiaoui; Mohamed Mohammedi; Khaled Hamouid
Abstract: Recent advances in Predictive Maintenance (PdM) are revolutionizing the railway industry by enabling early detection of failures and optimizing maintenance strategies. This research introduces a novel approach for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of train Air Production Units (APUs) using advanced deep learning models. The proposed methodology leverages a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to analyze complex temporal patterns in sensor data, significantly enhancing RUL prediction accuracy. A key innovation of this work lies in the integration of the MetroPT and MetroPT-3 datasets with maintenance reports, creating a comprehensive dataset for prediction. Prior to model development, data processing and feature selection were performed using a GradientBoostingRegressor. Extensive testing demonstrates the model's exceptional performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.08, a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.01, and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.11. These results underscore the approach's effectiveness in accurately predicting the RUL of train APUs. Additionally, SHAP analysis was conducted to enhance the model's interpretability by elucidating its predictions and highlighting key feature interactions, further validating its reliability.

Title: AI for Predictive Maintenance in Supply Chain Machinery
Authors: Raghad Mohammed Hadi; Cheng Ling Tan; Najlaa Abd Hamza; Shaker Al-Qudah; Fadi Ammouri
Abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a cornerstone of operational efficiency in modern supply chains, enabling organizations to anticipate and mitigate machinery failures before they disrupt production and logistics. The focus of this paper is to integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques consisting of machine learning and deep learning for the predictive maintenance of supply chain machinery. AI models can foresee failures, recommend optimal maintenance schedules, and augment equipment reliability by the real-time data from Internet of Things (IoT) sensors alongside past maintenance records. The application of many different AI algorithms like anomaly detection, time-series forecasting, and reinforcement learning for actual supply chain incidents is discussed. This study investigates the influence of AI-driven predictive maintenance on cutting downtime, increasing cost-effectiveness, and streamlining supply chain throughput. Moreover, we come to grips with challenges like data heterogeneity, scalability, and integration into existing platforms. The results emphasize the disruptive capabilities of AI in predictive maintenance as well as pave the road for more resilient and adaptive supply chain operations with intelligence.

Title: Towards Predictive Maintenance of Heavy-Duty Trucks Exploring Telemetry and Warranty Data
Authors: Juliana R. Viscenheski; Ricardo Luders; Heitor Lopes; Thiago H. Silva
Abstract: Cargo transportation is essential to Brazil's industrial development, with road freight responsible for approximately 60% of all cargo movement. Among transport companies, maintenance ranks as one of the highest operating costs, directly impacting fleet efficiency and total cost of ownership. For manufacturers, unexpected component failures, particularly under warranty, add costs and harm brand reputation. This study proposes a data-driven approach integrating telemetry and warranty data from Euro 6 heavy-duty trucks to identify vehicles with a higher likelihood of component failure, specifically within the powertrain system (engine/transmission assembly). After filtering vehicles for operational homogeneity, we apply feature selection based on correlation analysis and extract time-series features. Two methods are used to define reference failure profiles: (i) a baseline strategy using averaged feature vectors of failed and non-failed vehicles, and (ii) an unsupervised clustering approach using Fuzzy C-Means (FCM). These profiles are then used to compute failure risk scores for each vehicle based on their proximity to failed and healthy centroids. Our contributions include: (i) a detailed evaluation of FCM parameters and their effect on failure prediction precision, and (ii) the identification of usage-related features as stronger predictors of failure than component-specific variables. Results show that the clustering-based strategy significantly improves failure identification compared to the baseline, demonstrating the potential to support targeted preventive maintenance with minimal false positives.

Title: Edge AI for Predictive Maintenance: A Comparative Study on SCANIA Heavy-Duty Truck Component Failures
Authors: G. Ethiraj; S. Dhansehvaran; M. Pradeep Kumar
Abstract: We present in this article an edge AI system for predictive maintenance of SCANIA heavy vehicle trucks based on the SCANIA Component X dataset (365 files) (ResearchData. se dataset 2024-34). Our proxy-content method can serve as a virtual diagnostic system, which has predictive capability of failure of an anonymized critical engine component (here we call it Component X) 3-7 days before the time. Three models (Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM) were built and compared to make performance analysis comprehensive. Given the extreme imbalance of the data set (failures account for less than 2%), model evaluation was based on rare-event detection metrics such as F1 and PR AUC. Our results indicate that XGBoost is the superior model at an F1-score of 84.7% and PR-AUC of 82.1% with SCANIA test set. The optimal model is tested on a Raspberry Pi 4, which is able to run an inference of or 42.1ms with its memory footprint at 67.2MB. Therefore, our model shows a real-time realization which could be deployed in a car. All of this work is supported by an interactive Streamlit web dashboard for the fleet managers with actionable alerts and recommendations for maintenance. This paper demonstrates that AI-based predictive maintenance is feasible and has the strong potential of decreasing unplanned downtime by 70% and lowering operational cost for commercial trucking fleets.

Title: Application of Machine Learning Methods and Hybrid Modeling for Predicting the Remaining Useful Life of Equipment
Authors: Vasiliy Alchakov; Vladislav Pisarev
Abstract: The article examines the problem of predicting power transformers remaining useful life based on the analysis of dissolved gas concentrations in transformer oil. The study is based on a time-series analysis of hydrogen, carbon monoxide, ethylene, and acetylene concentration measurements over an extended operational period. The study involved data preprocessing and time series aggregation to identify patterns and factors influencing the remaining useful life of the equipment. Various data aggregation strategies were applied, including classical averaging and automated extraction of informative features. Different machine learning methods were employed to predict the remaining useful life of transformers, including ensemble methods such as gradient boosting, decision trees, and multilayer perceptrons. The implementation additionally included a feature classification stage aimed at identifying the most significant factors, improving regression forecasting accuracy. A comparative analysis of different approaches was conducted using established prediction quality metrics: mean absolute error, coefficient of determination, root mean square error, mean absolute percentage error, and classification evaluation metric. The research yielded a hybrid approach that combines classification and regression methods, facilitating a more accurate estimation of the equipment's residual service life. The proposed method can be integrated into transformer condition monitoring systems.

Title: Hybrid Convolutional Network for Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Huaiwang Jin; Sheng Wang; Yang Yang; Hang Wang; Zhongding Fan; Yongbin Liu
Abstract: Since graph convolutional networks can handle non-Euclidean data and can capture the interrelationships among different signal samples, they have been widely applied in the field of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. However, when using graph convolutional networks for bearing RUL prediction, the over-smoothing problem limits the increase in the number of network layers, thereby weakening the model's feature extraction ability. To enhance the feature extraction ability of graph convolutional networks and improve the accuracy of bearing RUL prediction, in this paper, a bearing RUL prediction method based on graph convolution network and time convolution network is proposed. In this method, a PathGraph is constructed based on the temporal sequence of the degradation signal to extract the temporal dependency between samples; and a network model integrating graph convolution and time convolution is constructed, which effectively extracts the temporal and spatial features contained in the graph samples. Through experimental verification, the results show that this method can effectively improve the prediction accuracy of the RUL of bearings.

Title: Personalized local initialization based federated learning for bearing remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Xi Chen; Siliang Lu; Hui Wang; Ruqiang Yan; Jiawen Xu
Abstract: Existing bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction methods often rely on specific datasets to train models optimized for particular operating conditions, disregarding samples from different conditions. Given the similarities in deterioration mode and vibration characteristics among bearings, common degradation features can be beneficial across machines. To enhance prediction models by leveraging information from diverse datasets, we propose a personalized local initialization based federated learning (PLI-FL) method. This method aims to develop individualized RUL prediction models for bearings operating under different conditions. The framework involves a central server and multiple clients, with each client possessing monitoring data generated under a specific working condition. Initially, clients train their local models, which are then aggregated by the server using federated averaging to create a global model. Clients subsequently combine the global model with their local models in an adaptive manner to establish personalized initialized models for the next round of local training. Through several iterations of local combination, training, and central aggregation, each client retains desirable degradation features from the global model and individualized features from the local model. Thus, personalized models are constructed for clients in a global model-assisted manner. Experimental results using bearing data demonstrate the effectiveness of the PLI-FL method in improving RUL prediction.

Title: Towards Efficient Predictive Maintenance: Evaluating LSTM Autoencoders, CNNs, and RNNs for Industrial Machinery Anomaly Detection
Authors: Md Ismail Hossian; Hasanur Zaman Anonto; Sudipto Roy; Nur Uddin Mahmud Arif; Md Sazid Ashraf; Nasimur Rezwan; Abu Shufian
Abstract: This work investigates a variety of anomaly detection models in the scope of machinery faults including the 1D CNN, LSTM Autoencoders, RNN architectures. We tested and compared the models in terms of test accuracy, convergence time, and predictive accuracy with the fewest misclassifications in profile anomalies. Of all the models evaluated, the LSTM Autoencoder was the most accurate, with a 99.5% test accuracy. This performed well in learning temporal patterns and achieved low RMSE, which made it well-suited to anomaly detection and sensor data reconstruction. But the parameter tuning was tedious, and it took a long time to train it. The 1D CNN model achieved a test accuracy of 98.1%, indicating rapid initial learning and high accuracy in anomaly detection, while demonstrating slower convergence and minor misclassifications over time. While the RNN did well on sequential data achieving 97.7% test accuracy, its convergence speed was low, and this also contributed to the high training loss. The experimental results show that the LSTM Autoencoder has the fastest convergence speed and the highest accuracy among various machine learning and deep learning models used for normal and abnormal fault machinery detection, which can be treated as a more reliable anomaly detection model.

Title: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance Algorithm in Lithium Battery Energy Storage System
Authors: Haijun Wu; Changyu Zhao; Fanhua Wang; Gang Wang
Abstract: Lithium ion batteries stand out among numerous energy storage technologies due to their excellent energy storage performance, especially their lightweight, high energy density, and outstanding electrochemical stability. They have become star products in many application fields and demonstrate broad development prospects. However, lithium-ion batteries also face many challenges in practical applications, such as performance degradation under abusive conditions and natural aging, which may pose a threat to their long-term stable operation. In response to this situation, this article innovatively proposes an intelligent fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance algorithm that integrates deep learning (DL). This algorithm can capture and analyze real-time operational data of lithium battery energy storage systems (LIBESS), accurately identifying potential failure modes of the system. More importantly, it can also reliably predict the future system state based on historical data, thereby deploying maintenance strategies in advance, effectively avoiding failure risks, and significantly extending the service life of LIBESS. The experimental verification results show that the algorithm not only has high diagnostic accuracy, but also demonstrates strong foresight and practicality in fault prediction.

Title: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for IIoT Driven Predictive Maintenance Using NASA C-MAPSS Dataset
Authors: Dimple Kapoor; Deepali Gupta; Mudita Uppal; Shrikant Mapari; S. Sankar Ganesh; R. Niranjan Devanathan
Abstract: The integration of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and predictive maintenance (PdM) models is transforming industrial asset management via condition-based monitoring and failure prediction. The successful execution of predictive maintenance (PdM) solutions in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) settings necessitates the evaluation of suitable machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models capable of handling high-dimensional sensor data. This study proposes a PdM methodology driven by IIoT and evaluates four data-driven models: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), utilizing the NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engine dataset. Experimental results indicate that RF performs better with an RMSE of 18.17 and R2 of 80.87%, better than other models. These results highlight the potential of traditional ML models for PdM in IIoT applications with a need for real-time, understandable, and cost-effective predictions. Future research will investigate hybrid and deployable edge models for enhancing accuracy and scalability.

Authors: Hongjiao Luo; Tian Ran Lin; Yajun Shang
Abstract: A remaining useful life (RUL) prediction technique is proposed based on deep learning network for end-to-end bearing RUL prediction. The technique introduces a depth-wise separable convolution into the denoising autoencoder (DAE) framework to construct a separable convolutional denoising autoencoder (SCDAE), which can effectively learn the spatial features from the bearing lifespan degradation data, and then an ordered long short-term memory network (ON-LSTM) is used to extract the temporal information between adjacent sample segments from the bearing degradation data, thereby rendering a more accurate bearing RUL prediction. An exponential weighted average method is employed to smooth the trend of the RUL prediction. Additionally, the effectiveness of the proposed technique is evaluated by comparing the prediction results with those obtained using other commonly employed data-driven RUL prediction techniques. It is shown that the proposed technique can yield a more accurate bearing RUL prediction than the other data-driven techniques.

Title: Smart Dashboard for Predictive Analytics of Transformer Remaining Useful Life (Rul)
Authors: Nur Avika Febriani; Ika Noer Syamsiana; Arwin Datumaya Wahyudi Sumari; Rachmat Sutjipto; Rahma Nur Amalia; Irwan Heryanto Eryk
Abstract: Electricity is an essential element in meeting human needs. A global increase in demand for electrical energy has been observed over time. The reliability of electricity supply is contingent upon the efficacy of transformer life prediction systems. Power transformers play a pivotal role in the effective distribution of electrical energy. Presently, the estimation of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is predominantly conducted manually. The necessity of a rapid and effective method for evaluating their condition has been underscored, prompting the emergence of smart web dashboards as a prominent solution for transformer condition monitoring and RUL estimation. The approach employed in this study utilizes the Knowledge Growing System (KGS) method. The KGS method is an artificial intelligence and expert system-based approach designed to continuously develop and update knowledge within a system. KGS facilitates continuous learning, enabling the RUL prediction model to adapt to evolving real-world conditions. The implementation of a web-based transformer RUL prediction application has proven to improve work efficiency and productivity by automating the storage and management of transformer measurement data to obtain accurate transformer life expectancy estimates. This approach is intended to ensure the reliability of the power system, to prevent sudden failures, and to reduce operational costs.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Aged Power Transformers: A Case Study Using Degree of Polymerisation and Furan Analysis
Authors: B. Koti Reddy; Pradeep Kumar Yemula; Vishal Devulapelly; Rammohan Rao Vemula; Bhanu Ganesh Ganta
Abstract: This paper presents a detailed case study on the estimation of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of oil-filled power transformers that have been in continuous service for periods ranging from 20 to 54 years. The ageing of transformers is primarily governed by the deterioration of their solid insulation, and accurate prediction of residual life is essential for ensuring grid reliability, planning maintenance, and avoiding costly failures. While thermal ageing laws such as the Arrhenius model have been traditionally employed, they often oversimplify ageing by considering temperature as the sole factor. In this study, particular emphasis is placed on chemical-based diagnostics, specifically Furan analysis, which provides insight into cellulose degradation, and the Degree of Polymerization (DP), which serves as a direct indicator of paper mechanical strength. Data from 16 operational transformers were collected and analyzed, and life estimation was performed using established empirical relationships. The findings reveal that several units still retain significant service potential beyond their nominal design life, demonstrating the practical value of DP and Furan analysis in condition-based life assessment and strategic asset management.

Title: Prediction of Rolling Bearings' Remaining Useful Life Based on Efficient Channel Attention TCN and Bidirectional GRU
Authors: Saihan Ma; Xiuqing Wang; Yuqing Li; Honghao Wang; Xudong Liu; Wenxia Du
Abstract: Rolling bearings are key parts of mechanical device, and performance degradation and failures may cause system downtime or damage. Therefore, predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings accurately is crucial for effective equipment maintenance. To address the problems of laborious feature extraction processes, insufficient feature extraction, and low prediction accuracy of traditional methods, we propose the model named ETCN-BiGRU for predicting rolling bearings' RUL, which combines the temporal convolution and bidirectional gated recurrent unit, and employs the efficient channel attention. We utilize dilated convolution to extract both local and global features for the ETCN-BiGRU model simultaneously. Additionally, the proposed model incorporates the BiGRU to capture the temporal relationships between the rolling bearings' sensor data, which is collected in both forward and backward time steps. Moreover, the ECA is employed in the TCN-BiGRU network to enhance the channel dimension's feature representation capacity. Experimental results of the PHM 2012 bearing datasets show the proposed model can accurately predict rolling bearings' RUL. The ETCN-BiGRU model has higher prediction accuracy and better stability than the comparison models.

Title: Assessment of PWM Techniques for Two-Level Inverters Analyzing their Influence on DC-Link Capacitor Remaining Useful Life
Authors: Eduardo Bascur; Abraham M. Alcaide; Jose I. Leon; Juan F. Ramos; Alfonso Manchado-Perez; R. Portillo; Leopoldo G. Franquelo
Abstract: System reliability represents a fundamental aspect in power converter operation. Within the spectrum of critical components, semiconductor devices and capacitors stand out as the most significant elements. This research examines the implementation of diverse pulse-width modulation (PWM) strategies within two-level voltage source inverters (VSI), with emphasis on both continuous and discontinuous modulation approaches. These methodologies are assessed regarding their influence on system efficiency and harmonic-related losses within the DC-link capacitor. The investigation encompasses essential operational variables including switching frequency, apparent power, and power factor. This work seeks to determine which modulation strategy provides optimal performance for capacitor loss reduction and to establish the most suitable technique based on specific application demands.

Title: Remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings based on cross attention mechanism and BiTCN, BiGRU
Authors: Changhu Zhou; Kerong Zhang; Jirui Yue; Yankuo Yin
Abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid prediction model, BiTCN-BiGRU-CA, which is designed to address the challenging problem of residual service life (RUL) prediction in rolling bearings. This model integrates the advantages of the cross-attention (CA) mechanism, the bidirectional time convolutional network (BiTCN), and the bidirectional gated cycle unit (BiGRU) neural network, which enables the efficient extraction and intelligent integration of spatio-temporal features present in bearing vibration signals. This results in a notable enhancement in prediction accuracy and model versatility. The BiTCN-BiGRU-CA model has been shown to outperform existing traditional models in terms of accuracy and versatility through experimental verification using the PHM IEEE2012 bearing data set. This provides a robust technical foundation for the formulation of maintenance strategies and the prediction of rolling bearing life.

Title: COMPARISON OF MACHINE LEARNING METHODS FOR PREDICTING REMAINING USEFUL LIFE IN HIGH-PRESSURE PACKING IN PLUNGER-TYPE HYPER COMPRESSORS
Authors: Jiun Wei Liou; Jin Wei Liang
Abstract: In this study, multiple machine learning methods were compared for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of high-pressure packing in plunger-type hyper compressors. To ensure consistency, unified failure criteria were applied across run-to-fail datasets for training and testing. Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) was employed as a modern approach to streamline the implementation and comparison among various machine learning models. This work focused solely on regression methods for RUL prediction. The datasets used for this study were derived from sensors within a local chemical factory, including 13 run-to-failure datasets for training and 4 testing datasets pre-processed using the same failure criteria. Key features, such as processed R-values and cumulative energy metrics, were extracted for RUL prediction. Particle Filter (PF), Sequence-to-sequence (Seq2seq) network and a two-layer Feedforward Neural Network (NN) were evaluated alongside the top three regression models identified by PyCaret, an AutoML tool. Since PF utilized only R-value while NN, Seq2seq and AutoML models incorporated both leakage and vibration features, direct performance comparisons were valid only among NN, Seq2seq and AutoML methods. The PF results, though listed, serve as an alternative approach with corresponding performance metrics. Although the AutoML models rely on simpler regression techniques, the seq2seq network, as a more complex model, demonstrated comparable performance with two-layer NN in literature after applying the appropriate failure criteria to the testing datasets.

Title: ST-MambaFormer: Multi-Scale Spatial-Temporal Feature Fusion for Tool Remaining Useful Life Prediction in Smart Manufacturing
Authors: Sirun Zhu; Rui Chen; Na Li; Yiming Wu; Wei Guo
Abstract: Tool wear is closely related to product quality and machine efficiency, and ensuring its safe and reliable operation is essential for digital manufacturing. However, using singular signals and feature extraction methods constrains the accuracy and generalization capability of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction model. Motivated by these problems, this paper proposes a novel tool RUL prediction model named ST-MambaFormer, which integrates a ResNet50 backbone network, a Mamba-based time series model, an iTransformer for spatial feature extraction, and a multi-level feature fusion mechanism. The model uses multi-sensor data and fuses spatial and temporal features to achieve multi-scale dynamic modeling of the tool degradation process. In this model, the Mamba model efficiently captures long-term temporal dependencies in sensor data and enhances sensitivity to critical degradation changes through its dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism. Meanwhile, the iTransformer attentively extracts spatial correlations among sensors and identifies stable wear distribution features by utilizing static position encoding and a self-attention mechanism. Furthermore, a modified multi-level feature fusion strategy is presented to enable effective global feature aggregation for RUL prediction. The proposed model is evaluated on the open-source PHM2010 dataset. Comparative experiments, ablation studies, and transfer tasks are conducted to validate the model's effectiveness. The ablation study confirms the importance of spatial-temporal feature extraction and fusion. Experimental results indicate that the proposed model reduces prediction errors and obtains higher accuracy compared to three baseline models - ResNet50, Mamba, and iTransformer. Its overall trend fitting and generalization capabilities offer a practical and valuable solution for tool health management in industrial applications.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings Using mLSTM (Matrix LSTM)
Authors: Jiaheng Zhao; Shibao Sun; Pengcheng Zhao
Abstract: Accurately modeling long-term dependencies and facilitating cross-timestep feature interaction are two major challenges in predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of rolling bearings from vibration data. To address these shortcomings, we propose a novel RUL prediction method based on the mLSTM architecture. The method initially extracts features from raw signals at multiple scales, encompassing time-domain, frequency-domain, and complexity metrics. This process constructs a degradation-sensitive feature set. A Health Indicator (HI) is established to quantify the bearing's performance degradation trajectory throughout its lifecycle. The proposed method introduces an mLSTM network architecture. In mLSTM, the hidden state vector of traditional LSTM is extended to a matrix form. Cross-timestep feature interaction is then achieved using multi-head attention. To verify the effectiveness of our approach, experiments were performed using the PHM2012 bearing dataset. Compared to the best baseline model, GRU, the proposed method reduced MSE, RMSE, and MAE by 35.997%, 19.158%, and 25.506%, respectively. This outcome confirmed the superiority of the proposed method.

Title: A Hybrid CEEMDAN and BiGRU Approach to Predicting Rolling Bearing Remaining Useful Life
Authors: Zhengrui Zhang; Lirong Xie
Abstract: To overcome issues related to acoustic disturbances, inadequate characteristic identification, and extended temporal correlation difficulties in forecasting bearing remaining operational lifespan (RUL), this research introduces a CEEMDAN-BiGRU framework. Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) preprocessing suppresses noise and extracts multi-band features, resolving the issues of mode mixing. The Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) network captures bidirectional degradation patterns through efficient temporal modeling, wavelet denoising and polynomial fitting enhance the prediction interpretability. Tests conducted using the PHM-IEEE-2012 benchmark reveal the suggested approach attains a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0438 alongside a relative error (RE) of 1.85%, outperforming models based on EMD/EEMD decomposition and networks such as LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU, which validates its robustness and prediction accuracy under complex operating conditions.

Authors: Jun Yang; Chen He; Jie Zhong; Yanming Lei

Title: A Phase Adaptive Approach to Self-Data-Driven Online Remaining Useful Life Prediction

Title: Sparse temporal fusion network for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearing
Authors: Dongpeng Li; Zhuyun Chen; Jiaxian Chen; Ruyi Huang; Weihua Li
Abstract: Deep Learning (DL)-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction can achieve high accuracies while the inner inference mechanism remains black-box. Despite that the existing explanation strategies or interpretable methods can achieve a certain level of transparency in the model, those deep structures themselves still cannot be explained analytically. To provide more interpretation to the network structure while retain comparable prediction performance, a novel end-to-end framework called sparse temporal fusion network (STFNet) is constructed to estimate the RUL of rolling bearing. First, the time domain signal in every time step is first extracted from the sparse encoder, in which the unrolled network is a white-box structure that can be interpreted. Next, the acquired sparse representation is sent to the temporal fusion module to improve temporal context awareness. Finally, the fused representation is fed into the regressor for RUL prediction. Experiments on the PRONOSTIA bearing dataset demonstrate strong predictive performance compared with other classical frameworks. Moreover, the reconstruction signals can be derived to reveal what the features are extracted in the unrolled network.

Title: FAT: Fusion-Attention Transformer for Remaining Useful Life Prediction

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
Authors: Xinyi Cheng; Jianfei Zheng; Qi Zhang; Lei Jiang; Hong Pei; Qing Dong
Abstract: As an important component of mechanical systems, the monitoring of the health state and remaining life prediction of bearings is of great significance in preventing failures and reducing downtime. First, the bearing vibration signals are decomposed using VMD to obtain several intrinsic modal function (IMF) components; subsequently, the SDP method is used to extract valid features from each IMF component to ensure the validity of the features. Next, the time-domain, frequency-domain, and entropy features of the IMF components are extracted separately, and the trend factor is utilized for feature selection. In order to reduce the dimensionality and retain the key features, a Weighted Dynamic Local Linear Embedding (WD-LLE) algorithm is proposed to reduce the dimensionality of the features. Finally, the final trend data of the bearing is obtained by weighted fusion of the WD-LLE results of each IMF component, and the remaining life is predicted using the Bi-LSTM model. The experimental results show that the method has higher accuracy and robustness compared with the traditional prediction methods.

Title: Flow Field Degradation Simulation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Marine Lubricating Oil Pumps

Abstract: Marine lubricating oil pumps are critical for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of vessel power systems by supplying lubricant to their components. First, gear tooth flank wear progression at different time intervals is computed through wear simulation. Subsequently, CFD analysis is employed to calculate key performance characteristics of the lubricating oil pump under varying wear states, thereby generating performance degradation data. Finally, a degradation model for the pump's volumetric efficiency is established based on a Wiener process incorporating random effects. Unknown parameters within this degradation model are estimated using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, enabling RUL prediction and reliability assessment. The reliable life of the target lubricating oil pump under rated pressure is calculated as 3, 6 2 0 hours. Results demonstrate that the proposed wear simulation model and flow field simulation model accurately characterize the degradation of flow field characteristics under gear pair wear conditions. The acquired flow field characteristic data enables effective reliability assessment and RUL prediction for marine lubricating oil pumps.

Title: A Method for Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Rolling Bearings Based on Federated Learning Pre-training
Authors: Wangzhuo Yang; Xian Zhou; Cunxuan Huo; Ke Li; Bo Chen
Abstract: Due to the complex operating conditions of rolling bearings and the scarcity of data samples, it is difficult to accurately model the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction models. Additionally, the use of traditional centralized data-driven methods poses data privacy and security issues. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for predicting the Remaining Useful Life of rolling bearings based on federated learning pretraining. Under the distribution of data from different operating conditions at each client, the federated learning concept is used to obtain a fusion model through multiple rounds of model information exchange between clients and the central server. This fusion model serves as the initial model for each client, which then improves the predictive performance for the current bearing by leveraging the degradation information of bearings under other operating conditions contained in the model. Experiments based on the PHM2012 bearing dataset and compared with centralized, local training, and classical federated learning methods show that the method proposed in this paper is effective for bearing RUL prediction.

Abstract: Dynamic adaptive prognostics method is attracting increasing attention in remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings, owing to selecting different models for prediction, and more accurately capturing the degradation trend. Finally, the uncertainty evaluation and RUL prediction results are obtained by the Kalman filter (KF). To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, trend prediction was performed on doublerow tapered roller bearings. Experimental result identifies that the proposed method better describes the process of bearing degradation.

Title: Turbine startup optimization and remaining useful life: A case study

Title: TransKAN: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Remaining Useful Life Prediction

To address these challenges, we propose Transformer-KAN (TransKAN), a novel hybrid model that integrates Transformer-based temporal feature extraction with the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for enhanced non-linear feature mapping. By leveraging the multi-head attention mechanism, the Transformer module efficiently learns long-range dependencies and degradation patterns in time-series data, while KAN enhances non-linear representation learning by bridging approximation theory with modern machine learning. We assess TransKAN on the widely used CMAPSS dataset, comparing its performance against leading deep learning models. Experimental results highlight its superior accuracy in RUL estimation, reinforcing its effectiveness in predictive maintenance.

Title: Physics Guided Dynamic Weighting Graph Neural Network for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings
Authors: Yongchang Xiao; Ziji Hong; Dongdong Liu; Lingli Cui
Abstract: While graph neural networks (GNNs) demonstrate significant capability in extracting features from graph-structured data and show effectiveness in machine remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, prevailing approaches often overlook the integration of inherent physical priors associated with bearing degradation. This limitation impedes the accurate modeling of the intricate interplay between complex degradation dynamics and multi-faceted failure mechanisms. This paper presents a GNN architecture guided by physical information, embedding the constitutive relationship between input feature evolution and physical degradation laws into the GNN structure via regularization constraints. Specifically, we propose a physics-informed loss function that minimizes the RUL prediction error during the bearing degradation process while adhering to fundamental physical principles. By dynamically adjusting weights according to the trend changes in monitoring data, the loss function of model is further refined, thereby enhancing its training process. Moreover, an attention mechanism is integrated to optimize the spectral graph convolution operation, mitigating the adverse effects of ambiguous features during continuous spectral graph convolution. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior accuracy and physical interpretability of proposed method compared to existing approaches.

Title: Enhancing Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0: Leveraging AI for Optimal Machinery Health Management
Authors: Lahiru Ubesigha; Chathura Rajapaksha; Thilini Mahanama; Dinesh Asanka
Abstract: This research introduces a multi-stage predictive maintenance framework to enhance the prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) in machinery by leveraging advanced AI-driven models. The framework comprises two primary phases: development modeling and active prediction. In the development phase, Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) are employed to synthesize fault data and address class imbalances during data preparation and training. A hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers processes time-series data, effectively capturing both local temporal features and long-term dependencies for accurate RUL prediction. The active prediction phase utilizes real-time data to continuously monitor machinery health and provide timely RUL forecasts. The system integrates a Fault-Finding Reference Unit and an Error Condition Classification Unit, where fault types are classified using Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) enhanced through active continual learning. Human experts contribute by updating the knowledge base, ensuring the system adapts and improves over time. This comprehensive approach aims to optimize maintenance schedules, reduce machine downtime, and enhance operational efficiency in Industry 4.0 environments.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings Based on Full-Band Feature Feedback Adaptive Fusion
Authors: Lei Jiang; Jianfei Zheng; Xinyi Cheng; Lihao Yang; Xi Chen; Qihui Han
Abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components in mechanical systems, and accurately estimating their Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is essential for ensuring reliability and minimizing maintenance costs. However, current prediction approaches make limited use of frequency-domain features and often overlook the integration of prediction outcomes in feature fusion. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces an RUL prediction framework that leverages full-frequency-band degradation feature extraction combined with adaptive feedback-based fusion. First, a 1/3 binary tree filtering strategy is used to perform multi-scale decomposition of the vibration signals, and the Wasserstein distance (WD) is employed to extract full-frequency-band degradation features. Next, a dynamic feedback mechanism is introduced to adaptively adjust Health Indicators (HI). Experimental results on the XJTU-SY dataset confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Title: Predictive Maintenance of an Hydraulic System Using Spiking Neural Networks

Abstract: Predictive maintenance is a vital component of modern machinery management, allowing operators to anticipate and prevent equipment failures. In this study, we introduce a novel approach using spiking neural networks (SNNs) for predictive maintenance of hydraulic systems. While prior research has used traditional feature engineering and machine learning or artificial neural networks for predictive maintenance of hydraulic systems, this study utilizes SNNs instead. SNNs are event-driven artificial neural networks that can process real-time data with high accuracy, making them an ideal tool for predictive maintenance. The proposed approach leverages historical sensor data to accurately predict system failures in hydraulic systems. The public data set used was experimentally obtained with a hydraulic test rig with 17 sensors distributed throughout the system. The system had four independent modes of failure with varying degrees of severity and a fifth parameter indicating whether the system had reached stable conditions or not. The pre-processed data was used to train the SNN, which was then tested for its ability to predict system failures. The results showed that the SNN was able to accurately predict system cooling condition failures with a high degree of accuracy(99.46%), precision(99.73%), Recall(98.95%), F1-Score(98.95%), demonstrating its potential for use in predictive maintenance applications. In conclusion, this study highlights the significance of SNNs as a valuable tool for improving the reliability and efficiency of hydraulic systems. With further development, SNNs are poised to become the gold standard in predictive maintenance.

Title: An intelligent hybrid deep learning model for rolling bearing remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Linfeng Deng; Wei Li; Xinhui Yan
Abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of rolling bearings is one of the intricate and important issues for equipment intelligent maintenance and health management. Various machine learning models and methods have been applied to rolling bearing RUL prediction. Therefore this paper proposes an intelligent hybrid deep learning model for achieving accurate RUL prediction of rolling bearings. Firstly, the one-dimensional vibration signal is transformed into the corresponding two-dimensional time-frequency diagram via Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). Secondly, the diagram is input into a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) consisting of a basic three-layer feed-forward network to obtain a one-dimensional feature vector. And lastly, the obtained feature vector is input into an integrated model based on Deep Autoregressive and Transformer to produce the probability distribution and obtain the prediction results of rolling bearing RUL. Extensive experiments on two rolling bearing datasets show that the proposed model outperforms six other comparative models in extracting bearing fault features and predicting bearing RUL, which demonstrates that the proposed model can effectively extract bearing fault features and accurately predict bearing remaining useful life.

Title: PMBCT: The Probabilistic Multiscale Bayesian Convolutional Transformer for Trustworthy Remaining Useful Life Prediction

Finally, comprehensive RUL prediction experiments are carried out based on a bearings dataset for validating the effective and competitive performances of the PMBCT-based RUL prognostic approach.

Title: An Enhanced Approach for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Bearings Using Incomplete Lifecycle Data

Abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings is crucial for ensuring optimal equipment operation and timely maintenance. The network operates in three distinct phases: first, feature parameters indicative of bearing degradation trends are extracted across time, frequency, and time-frequency domains. Second, pre-training is performed in a mask self-supervised learning mode with contrastive learning on extensive incomplete lifecycle data, effectively distinguishing similar and dissimilar degradation patterns. Finally, the model undergoes fine-tuning in a supervised phase using complete lifecycle data. To further improve prediction accuracy, we employ a channel-independent transformer network, while RUL estimation is accomplished by integrating multi-source features through a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) layer. The proposed method is rigorously evaluated on both the IEEE PHM 2012 and XJTU-SY datasets and benchmarked against state-of-the-art approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively captures the complex dynamic behavior of rolling bearings, achieving high accuracy and generalization in RUL prediction.

Title: A Remaining Useful Life Prediction Method for Rolling Bearing Based on TCN-Transformer

Abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings is crucial to ensure the stable operation of equipment. This study presents a TCN-transformer model and a two-stage degradation feature optimization methodology to address these challenges. The first stage uses Kalman filtering to suppress abnormal noise in the degradation index. Probability prediction and interval prediction are incorporated into rolling bearing RUL prediction to enhance the reliability of the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on the publicly available dataset XJTU-SY.

Results show that XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 99.99% and the fastest training time in current-state classification, while LSTM provided more realistic forecasting performance with gradually decreasing accuracy of 98.3% for 7 days and 95.9% for 30 days, as prediction horizons extended. Chronological evaluation confirmed that both models performed consistently, with perfect accuracy attributed to the dataset's single-class composition near the timeline end. Overall, XGBoost is better suited for immediate condition monitoring, whereas LSTM offers credible temporal forecasting for long-term maintenance planning.

Title: Predictive Maintenance in Textile Manufacturing Using Artificial Intelligence

Title: Data-Driven Method for Predicting Remaining Useful Life of Bearings Based on Multi-Layer Perception Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Network
Authors: Yongfeng Tai; Xingyu Yan; Xiangyi Geng; Lin Mu; Mingshun Jiang; Faye Zhang
Abstract: The remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearing is vital in safety and reliability guarantee. In engineering scenarios, only a small amount of bearing performance degradation data can be obtained through accelerated life testing. In the absence of lifetime data, the hidden long-term correlation between performance degradation data is challenging to mine effectively, which is the main factor that restricts the prediction precision and engineering application of the residual life prediction method. To address this problem, a novel method based on the multi-layer perception neural network and bidirectional long short-term memory network is proposed. Firstly, a nonlinear health indicator (HI) calculation method based on kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) and exponential weighted moving average (EWMA) is designed. Then, using the raw vibration data and HI, a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) neural network is trained to further calculate the HI of the online bearing in real time. Furthermore, The bidirectional long short-term memory model (BiLSTM) optimized by particle swarm optimization (PSO) is used to mine the time series features of HI and predict the remaining service life. Performance verification experiments and comparative experiments are carried out on the XJTU-SY bearing open dataset. The research results indicate that this method has an excellent ability to predict future HI and remaining life.

Title: Health Indicator Construction and Remaining Useful Life Prediction Based on MSC-LSTM-AE Model for Working Bearings
Authors: Yuanyuan Qu; Shichen Fu; Ming Yong; Jingyao Tian; Zhaoqian Lv; Ruizhi Li
Abstract: In the prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for rotating mechanical components, the extraction and construction of health or degradation indicators are crucial. To effectively construct health indicators (HIs) without relying on manual experience, this article proposes an unsupervised method for bearing HI construction and RUL prediction. First, a multiscale convolution and long short-term memory combined autoencoder (MSC-LSTM-AE) network is built to extract encoded features containing time-dependent degradation information. Then, support vector regression (SVR) is employed to calculate anomaly scores based on the encoded features of healthy and faulty data, to construct HIs representing the bearing degradation process. The first prediction time (FPT) is subsequently determined based on the pruned exact linear time (PELT) algorithm to form the crucial series of HI versus RUL. Finally, a prediction network combining a convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) is utilized and trained for bearing’s RUL prediction. The proposed method is validated on the Xi’an Jiaotong University (XJTU)-Sumyoung Technology Co., Ltd. (SY) bearing dataset, and the experimental results show that the constructed HIs provide a more distinct degradation trend compared to other methods, thereby enhancing RUL prediction performance.

Title: DGT-former: a dual-channel time-frequency fusion model for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
Authors: Yuhui Shi; Xinhui Yan; Yuanwen Zhang; Dun Yang; Qian Song; Weiqiang Zhang; Linfeng Deng
Abstract: Significant breakthroughs have been achieved in the prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of rolling bearings based on deep learning. However, existing deep learning methods still have limitations. First, most of them adopt single-modal input or ignore the correlation between the different input data, which restricts the ability of extracting key degradation features; second, there are still challenges in modelling long-term temporal dependencies. To address these issues, this paper introduces a deep learning prediction framework called DGT-former, which incorporates a Dual-channel Gated Convolutional Network (DGConv), a Temporal Squeeze-and-Excitation module (TSE) and stacked Informer encoders. The network includes time- and frequency-domain channels, with the TSE attention module embedded in both to enhance representation of key degradation stages. Time-domain signals are converted to frequency-domain signals via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), and both signals are input into the DGConv. The dual-channel features are concatenated and fed into the stacked Informer encoders. Moreover, applying its ProbSparse self-attention mechanism can effectively capture the long-term dependencies in sequences, and finally the RUL prediction results are obtained by mapping the fully connected layer. Experimental analysis on two rolling bearing datasets and comparison with other methods show that the proposed method outperforms them in accuracy and generalisation.

Title: Prediction of remaining useful life and downtime of induction motors with supervised machine learning
Authors: Muhammad Dzulfiqar Anindhito; Suharjito
Abstract: This research aims to use a vibration monitoring system along with machine learning techniques to predict the downtime and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of three-phase induction motors in the manufacturing sector. Title: Prediction model optimization of gas turbine remaining useful life based on transfer learning and simultaneous distillation pruning algorithm
Authors: Yu Zheng; Liang Chen; Xiangyu Bao; Fei Zhao; Jingshu Zhong; Chenhan Wang
Abstract: For the application of deep learning (DL) models in the field of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and predictive maintenance (PdM) of complex equipment, the insufficient training data and large model are the two major problems. To address these issues, a model training method based on transfer learning and a simultaneous distillation pruning algorithm were proposed. By introducing prior knowledge, three transfer learning modes are devised to reduce the demand of training data. Additionally, the simultaneous distillation pruning algorithm was devised to make the model lightweight, and an iterative pruning method was adopted to trim the large neural network model. By analyzing the performance of different transfer learning modes, the effectiveness of the proposed method can be demonstrated. The number of model parameters and the performance before and after pruning were compared. The results demonstrated that, without significant alterations to the prediction performance, the proposed model exhibited the capability to markedly reduce the number of model parameters. Based on the proposed methods, the challenges of insufficient data and efficiency encountered by DL models could be effectively addressed.

Title: An Online Adaptive Multidegradation Model for Accurate Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Zhijian Wang; Zhijie Li; Weibo Ren; Zhongxin Chen; Yanfeng Li; Lei Dong; Xiaosheng Si; Xin Fan
Abstract: The majority of existing online remaining useful life (RUL) prediction models for rolling bearings adopt a single degradation model, and lack the capacity for real-time assessment of model matching. Furthermore, these models determine the first prediction time (FPT) using subjective thresholds, which often results in inaccuracies and considerable deviations in subsequent online RUL predictions. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes an online adaptive matching multidegradation model for RUL prediction. First, a curvature analysis incorporating a dynamic sliding window strategy is proposed. This strategy determines the first prediction time in real time by analyzing the change in curvature of the root-mean-square values within a dynamic sliding window. Second, an online parallel prediction algorithm with multiple degradation models is developed. This algorithm selects the most suitable prediction model by dynamically evaluating the degree of matching between different degradation models and the actual data, thereby ensuring the timeliness of the prediction model. Finally, the validation of the proposed approach is conducted by accelerating the degradation rolling bearing test and the IMS rolling bearing dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in accurately identifying FPT and predicting online RUL.

Title: A stage-related online incremental transfer learning-based remaining useful life prediction method of bearings
Authors: Weisen Guo; Fang Li; Ping Zhang; Long Luo
Abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings holds significant research value in bearing health management, particularly in the rapidly advancing field of intelligent manufacturing. How to realize the accurate online RUL prediction still faces many challenges, including the diverse degradation trends in bearings, the scarcity of labeled data, and the inconsistencies in the data marginal distributions. This paper proposes a Stage-related Online Incremental Adversarial Domain Adaption (SR-OIADA) transfer learning algorithm for bearing RUL prediction. It employs a dynamic domain adaptation strategy, which integrates incremental learning and transfer learning, facilitating the online acquisition of degradation knowledge aligned with degradation stages. A novel online degradation stage division algorithm is proposed to adaptively detect the health status of online monitored bearings, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of online learning. By incrementally training the deep models in a prediction-to-transfer manner, the model undergoes incremental updates at checkpoints, taking full advantage of new online samples. Experiments are conducted on real rolling bearing datasets to validate the proposed methods, demonstrating excellent predictive performance and highlighting the superiority compare with the non-transfer and offline methods.

Title: Multilevel Feature Alignment Method for Advancing Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearing
Authors: Xuewu Pei; Yiping Gao; Xinyu Li; Liang Gao; Xingxin Zhao
Abstract: Rolling bearings are the key components of various equipment and easily subject to failure, remaining useful life (RUL) prediction technology can grasp their health statuses to make a reasonable maintenance plan. Transfer learning methods for rolling bearing cross-domain RUL prediction focus on the direct alignment of the degradation process between the target domain and source domain. However, the working condition and degradation process of rolling bearing to be predicted are unknown, which are different from the target domain or source domain. The caused data distribution discrepancy has seriously affected the RUL prediction acceptance. To solve this problem, a multilevel feature alignment (MLFA) method for advancing RUL prediction without target domain data for training is proposed. Specifically, a proposed weighted TOPSIS is implemented for supervised label making to train a robust RUL prediction prior model. The three-level feature alignment (TLFA) strategy, which involves feature alignment by the proposed adaptive nonlinear state estimation, envelope spectrum (ES), ES-combined deep convolutional autoencoder, is developed to mitigate the data distribution discrepancy between the predicted and prior entities. TLFA transforms prediction tasks from cross-domain to different failure behaviors. Extensive experiments conducted on both public and industrial scene run-to-failure bearing datasets validated the superiority of the MLFA. These results from comparison experimental show that MLFA improves mean absolute error and root mean absolute error (RMSE) about 0.061 and 0.054 individually than some state-of-the-art methods.

Title: Privacy-Preserving Cross-Silo Federated Learning for Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Distribution Transformers
Authors: Qi Wu; Yuhang Ma; Baokang Zhang; Fanghong Guo; Wen An Zhang; Xiang Qiu
Abstract: Due to the growing necessity for a reliable power supply and the aging of distribution transformers (DTs), estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of these transformers has gained wide attention in the power industry. However, there is an inevitable data shortage that restricts the performance of the estimation. In addition, data sharing sometimes tends to result in the leakage of sensitive information. These are the main issues that need to be resolved currently. For this purpose, a privacy-preserving cross-silo federated learning (FL) method is developed for the RUL estimation of DTs, namely ADP-FedRUL. Specifically, a crosssilo FL architecture enables different data silos to train a global model without the need to share raw data. In this way, it extracts composite health index (CHI) from multisource sensor data and integrates the advantages of data to facilitate accurate RUL estimation while preserving privacy. First, the proposed Pearson–Spearman correlation metric, along with Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) and autoencoders, is used to group and fuse health indicators (HIs), thereby obtaining a health indicator (HI) that effectively reflects the bearing degradation process. Based on the classification results, the Adaptive Attention GraphSAGE–LSTM (AAGL) model, also introduced in this study, is employed to precisely predict the bearing’s remaining useful life.

Title: Dynamic Energy Sparse Self-Attention Based on Informer for Remaining Useful Life of Rolling Bearings
Authors: Cheng Shi; Qifei Li; Hui Chen; Yuanwei Song; Qianqi Le
Abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life of rolling bearings presents significant challenges due to their nonstationary degradation patterns. Conventional methods struggle with long sequences and are strongly dependent on manual feature extraction, which can lead to inefficiencies and biased predictions. The proposed model uses the auto-reassignment transform to extract more accurate features from the raw vibration signals, and the dynamic energy sparse self-attention mechanism adapts the attention weights based on the energy distribution. In addition, the Monte Carlo dropout method is employed to quantify uncertainty and enhance model robustness. Experimental results obtained on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing advanced methods, achieving a reduction in mean absolute error and root mean square error, demonstrating its superior ability to handle complex bearing degradation prediction tasks.

Title: Time-frequency synchronisation contrastive learning-driven multi-sensor remaining useful life prediction
Authors: Li Jiang; Miaojun Wang; Peijie You; Xin Zhang
Abstract: Deep learning techniques play a crucial role in predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of mechanical equipment. Nevertheless, obtaining a substantial number of labeled samples is a challenge, and the prediction accuracy tends to decline when the labeled samples are insufficient. Moreover, existing RUL prediction methods usually extract the degradation characteristics only from one single domain, which is insufficient for a high-accuracy prediction. To address these challenges, a time-frequency synchronization contrastive learning-driven (TFSCL) multi-sensor remaining useful life prediction model is proposed. The proposed TFSCL utilizes a large amount of unlabeled data for model pre-training and key feature extraction, and it introduces a novel time-frequency fusion contrastive loss function to optimize the pre-training process. It employs a dual-channel structure at the sensor and timestamp levels, incorporating an attention mechanism that adaptively adjusts sensor feature weights, enabling more accurate extraction of critical information while effectively mitigating interference from irrelevant data. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed TFSCL, two case studies are conducted, with different labeling ratios being used. The experimental results demonstrate that even with lower labeling ratios, the proposed TFSCL model still achieves a satisfactory prediction effect and outperforms other advanced methods.

Title: Prediction Method for the Remaining Useful Life of Power MOSFETs Based on Deep Learning
Authors: Le Gao; Chaoming Liu; Fengjiang Wu; Yongfeng Qin; Yuhang Wang; Mingxue Huo
Abstract: Power switching devices serve as critical components in power conversion systems, making their lifespan evaluation essential for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of such systems. The proposed method integrates the global search capabilities of a genetic algorithm to optimize model hyperparameters with the global attention mechanism of the transformer model to construct a robust device lifespan prediction framework. The results demonstrate that the optimized model achieves an average absolute percentage error significantly lower than traditional particle filter models, improving prediction performance by a factor of 3-5.

Title: Sinkhorn divergence-based contrast domain adaptation for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings under multiple operating conditions
Authors: Yan Han; Ailin Hu; Qingqing Huang; Yan Zhang; Zhichao Lin; Jinghua Ma
Abstract: Under multiple operating conditions, the degradation characteristics of rolling bearings show diverse distributions. Domain adaptation (DA) achieves effective alignment between source and target domains by extracting domain-invariant features. However, in the prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) for bearings, numerous DA methods overlook mutual information from target-specific data and encounter potential challenges such as the vanishing gradient problem during the alignment of data distributions, leading to limited performance. To address these challenges, a novel method called Sinkhorn Divergence-based Contrast Domain Adaptation (SD_CDA) is proposed to predict RUL under multiple operating conditions. Firstly, an adversarial training framework is constructed to initially extract domain-invariant features. Subsequently, the cross-domain temporal mixup strategy is proposed for the data augment, which obtains positive samples to serve contrastive learning. Then self-supervised momentum contrast (MoCo) is employed to extract mutual information from target-specific data, preserving its specificity. Finally, Sinkhorn divergence is introduced to further align the fine-grained structure of the source domain and target domain, and enhance the transfer ability of the model. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed method under multiple operating conditions.
