Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction Approach for Aviation Bearings Based on Multigenerator Generative Adversarial Network and CBAM
Authors: Zhaohui Yang; Yudong Wang; Yuanbo Yang; Ni Li; Chunlin Zhang
Abstract: The remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of aviation bearings is of paramount importance in reducing additional maintenance costs and enhancing the monitoring and reliability of aviation equipment, while is still a challenge especially when data samples are few and hard to analyze. Although scholars have done a lot of research on it, the data processing approach with the efficiency of prediction is still not up to expectations. A novel approach based on multigenerator generative adversarial network (GAN) and convolutional block attention module (CBAM) is proposed, which can effectively solve the above two problems. In this article, we first build a multigenerator GAN, utilizing the Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) framework to augment data. The efficiency and quality of data generated by the generators are improved through weight sharing and feature fusion strategies. Then, the augmented data are fed into the constructed convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract unhealthy data with degenerate features, while reducing the learning burden of the prediction network. Finally, the fully processed data are fed into the network based on CBAM and long short-term memory (LSTM) to get the RUL prediction of bearings. The proposed approach is evaluated using the public FEMTO dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed approach is effective in improving the accuracy and stability of RUL prediction for aviation bearings.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings Based on CBAM-CNN-LSTM
Authors: Bo Sun; Wenting Hu; Hao Wang; Lei Wang; Chengyang Deng
Abstract: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is vital for ensuring the reliability and safety of equipment and components. This study introduces a novel method for predicting RUL that utilizes the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to address the problem that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) do not effectively leverage data channel features and spatial features in residual life prediction. Firstly, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is applied to convert the data into the frequency domain. The resulting frequency domain data is then used as input to the convolutional neural network for feature extraction; Then, the weights of channel features and spatial features are assigned to the extracted features by CBAM, and the weighted features are then input into the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to learn temporal features. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model is verified using the PHM2012 bearing dataset. Compared to several existing RUL prediction methods, the mean squared error, mean absolute error, and root mean squared error of the proposed method in this paper are reduced by 53%, 16.87%, and 31.68%, respectively, which verifies the superiority of the method. Meanwhile, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves good RUL prediction accuracy across various failure modes.

Abstract: The remaining Useful Life (RUL) forecast for rolling bearings is still a crucial part of condition-based maintenance (CBM) for mechanical systems. Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Bearings Using Multiscale Temporal-Enhanced Deformable Attention With Soft Thresholding
Authors: Fengshuo Guo; Weiming Fu; Jiahu Qin; Qichao Ma; Yu Kang
Abstract: The run-to-failure monitoring data of bearings can be utilized for modeling and analysis to predict their remaining useful life (RUL). Such data typically contain degradation features across multiple time scales and are often accompanied by noise interference. However, most existing deep learning (DL) methods struggle with effectively suppressing noise, dynamically capturing key degradation patterns, and integrating multiscale degradation features. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel end-to-end RUL prediction method for bearings based on multiscale temporal-enhanced deformable attention with soft thresholding (MTEDAST). Specifically: 1) a soft-threshold denoising block based on an autoencoder (AE) is introduced, which dynamically adjusts the denoising threshold according to data characteristics, thereby effectively removing low-amplitude noise and enhancing key feature representations; 2) a temporal-enhanced deformable attention (TEDA) mechanism that incorporates temporal bias information into the attention mechanism is proposed, enabling it to dynamically adapt and capture critical temporal degradation patterns; and 3) a dynamic multiscale attention fusion (DMAF) block is designed, which employs element-wise multiplication to dynamically integrate multiscale features, enhancing informative scales while suppressing irrelevant ones. Experimental results on the PHM2012 and XJTU-SY datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches with an average improvement of 28.04% in the score metric and average reductions of 36.66% and 35.89% in mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean-square error (RMSE), respectively.

Title: A Method for Remaining Useful Life Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification of Rolling Bearings Based on Fault Feature Gain

Abstract: In the field of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, accurately evaluating incipient faults in bearings by using conventional health indicators (HIs) poses challenges, while traditional neural network models fail to provide reliable uncertainty distributions for credible output. Finally, experimental results obtained from an accelerated degradation test bench for rolling bearings validate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that FFG enables accurate assessment of bearing health status while providing crucial insights into the underlying failure modes. Furthermore, the GRU-BNN model performs more accurately in RUL prediction and can better quantify the uncertainty of RUL.

Title: Bayesian Adversarial Adaptation Network With Feature Disentanglement for Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Yongbo Cheng; Junheng Qv; Liangqi Wan; Te Han
Abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is vital for the safety of engineering assets. In the real scenario, due to the lack of failure data and variable working conditions, the accuracy of predictive RUL is significantly compromised as models struggle to generalize across diverse operating environments. Existing solutions manage to shift the degradation information from the ideal laboratory environment to the complex real-world environment. However, they fail to consider the heterogeneity of operating machines under different working conditions. This ignorance of inherent properties will eventually hamper the accuracy of RUL prediction. Consequently, a novel Bayesian adversarial Fast Linear Attention with a Single Head (FLASH) Transformer with feature disentanglement model (BAFTFD) was proposed in this article to tackle with the problem. The proposed BAFTFD model can disentangle the private feature representations from the raw data, preserving the shared feature representation for the prediction. The adversarial training method is also exploited to facilitate the transfer of degradation knowledge. Besides, the feature extractor is equipped with the effective FLASH Transformer model to retain the most informative degradation features for model training, improving the efficiency of feature extraction. Moreover, considering the impact of insufficient training data, inherent data noise on the trustworthiness of the predictive results, the Bayesian DL method is adopted to quantify the prediction uncertainties, ensuring the reliability of maintenance decisions. Two commercial turbofan datasets are leveraged to validate the designed model.

Title: Early Failure Point Monitoring for Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Bearings Using Covariance Transfer Enabled T2 Control Chart
Authors: Chao Chen; Xianqi Wu; Hui Wang; Li Zhang; Liling Han; Wei Fan
Abstract: T2 control chart, a prevalent statistical process control technique, has extensively employed in the realm of bearing early failure monitoring within the setting of prognostics and health management. However, insufficient historical data as well as the nonidentical distributions between training and testing date, caused by stochastic noise and fluctuating operational conditions, inevitably increase the risk of false alarms and hinder the robustness of bearing early failure monitoring. To address the challenges, a covariance transfer enabled T2 control chart (CTET2CC) is proposed for bearing early failure monitoring under varying operational conditions. First, feature extraction is conducted via the multitime scale phase space warping (MPSW) method. Thereafter, a Gaussian process is employed to derive functional relationships in the source and target domains, respectively, in order to construct the T2 profile control chart. Then, the domain-invariant statistics can be efficiently learned from a large number of source domain profile samples through singular value decomposition (SVD), which excels in capturing the essential features of profile samples, and providing a robust representation of the underlying structure. Furthermore, a covariance transfer through SVD strategy is designed by re-weighting the target statistics. Finally, the corresponding T2 control chart is reconstructed to boost the stability of the controlled phase for target task. Experimental results verify that the proposed method is expected to be an effective technique for bearing early failure monitoring.

Title: Predictive Maintenance of Farming Equipment Using AI
Authors: Ahmed Sebihi; Marwan Alakhras
Abstract: In modern agriculture, an increase in the use of advanced farming devices requires the use of proactive maintenance strategies, which are essential to reduce downtime, cut costs, and achieve operational efficiency. In this research study, we examine the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to predict the maintenance of farming equipment, which involves the application of machine learning models and the Internet of Things (IoT) sensors for the real-time collection and analysis of data. The framework involved comprises predictive analytics integration, anomaly detection algorithms, and the use of historical maintenance records to locate the points of failure of the equipment. The remarkable contributions of this study are the construction of a predictive maintenance pipeline, the evaluation of the performance of the models using publicly available and proprietary datasets, and the creation of a scalable architecture for those real-world deployment. The results illustrate machinery reliability enhancement, cost losses from inefficient maintenance reduction, and productivity growth agriculture. The paper addresses the game-changing effect that AI could have in resource optimization and the progress of sustainable precision agriculture.

Title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction Method of Rolling Bearing Based on Frequency-domain TCAE-Informer
Authors: Hao Yan; Siyu Li; Xianbiao Zhan; Enzhi Dong; Liang Wen; Xisheng Jia
Abstract: Rolling bearing is a key component in a large number of rotating machines, and its remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is related to whether an equipment can operate safely and stably. In order to solve the current problem of low accuracy of RUL prediction, a prediction method combining temporal convolutional autoencoder (TCAE) and Informer (TCAE-Informer) network in frequency domain is proposed for RUL of rolling bearings. The method designs a TCAE for the frequency-domain signals of different time samples of rolling bearings, and adaptively extracts the depth features that better reflect the full-life degradation law of rolling bearings. An Informer network model is built, and with the help of its learning advantage in long sequence information, the mapping relationship between the depth features and the RUL of rolling bearings is effectively fitted to realize the RUL prediction function of rolling bearings. XJTU-SY bearing dataset is used to compare and validate the evaluation indexes of three RUL prediction results. The results show that the proposed method is able to achieve more accurate RUL prediction effect under different working conditions compared with many existing methods, which proves that it has superior RUL prediction ability and generalization ability. The anti-interference test is carried out for different methods. In the test, the proposed method shows better RUL prediction effect under different noise conditions, which proves that it has superior anti-interference ability of RUL prediction.

Title: Adaptive Multistage Sparse Gaussian Process Regression for Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Authors: Wei Fan; Xiaoxu Gao; Liling Han; Zhenying Xu; Chao Chen; Long Chen
Abstract: The remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings directly affects their operational efficiency and safety, rendering accurate RUL prediction essential for ensuring reliable performance. However, existing RUL prediction methods often rely on a single-stage degenerate model, which limits their accuracy. In addition, conventional data-driven approaches require extensive computational costs due to the extensive quantification of monitoring data. To solve these problems, an adaptive multistage degradation framework based on sparse Gaussian process regression (GPR) is proposed in this article. The degradation process is divided into multiple stages based on change points, whose number is determined by the elbow method, and the change points are adaptively selected from binary segmentation (BS), the degradation angle (DA) index, and the exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) through error assessments at each stage. A degradation indicator and sparse GPR model with a matched kernel function selected based on trend variations is constructed for each stage. The proposed method is validated on both a simulated signal and a PHM challenge bearing dataset. Comparative experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness and superiority over alternative models.

Title: AI-based remaining useful life prediction for transmission systems: Integrating operating conditions with TimeGAN and CNN-LSTM networks
Authors: Yeon Sub Sim; Chun Kwon Lee; Jae Sang Hwang; Gu Young Kwon; Seung Jin Chang
Abstract: The remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is key for ensuring the stability of transmission power systems. However, there is no sufficient actual life-cycle, and no mature physics-of-failure model of the power transmission facilities, which make it difficult to predict RUL. In this paper, we propose an AI-based transmission line RUL prediction method which incorporates the measured operating conditions of each line. The proposed method sets the basic linear asset unit as one cable segment and joint boxes on both sides. A feature extraction and piecewise-based RUL model was designed using asset data from 1,458 actual transmission lines accumulated by measuring unit over a period of 44 years. Consequently, the RULs which depend on load operating conditions of target assets can be successfully predicted using CNN-LSTM. In addition, a data augmentation algorithm based on time-series generative adversarial networks was developed to address the issue of imbalanced failure data and further improve the accuracy of RUL prediction. The performance of the proposed RUL estimation method is further verified using real-world data. The proposed method shows an improvement in fault-healthy classification accuracy by 35.72%, 21.43%, and 7.14% compared to existing feature extraction methods, including deep neural networks (DNN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and autoencoder (AE), respectively. Additionally, when compared to representative deep learning models for RUL estimation, it achieves the best performance with RMSE and Score of 0.074 and 0.066, respectively. Moreover, the proposed method is capable of accurately estimating RUL even for equipment in the early failure period, where the actual operating time is short.

Title: 5G Architectures Enabling Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Industrial IoT: A Holistic Study
Authors: Nicolo Longhi; Lorenzo Mario Amorosa; Sara Cavallero; Enrico Buracchini; Roberto Verdone
Abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of industrial connectivity, significant strides have been made in the integration of 5th generation (5G) cellular technology with Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. At the same time, data-driven analytics has become an effective tool for leveraging information from interconnected industrial devices, enabling organizations to gain valuable insights and make informed decisions. However, among these advancements, the holistic perspective of end-to-end analysis related to their integration remains a critical aspect that has yet to be comprehensively addressed. To this end, we investigate 5G IIoT network architectures that support automated guided vehicles (AGVs) on a factory floor as an illustrative example. In particular, we leverage real sensor data collected by AGVs to estimate their remaining useful life (RUL) using a deep learning (DL)-based pipeline. We conduct an in-depth analysis to assess the compatibility of 5G New Radio infrastructures with the aforementioned case study, focusing on round trip time (RTT) requirements and emphasizing the inter-dependencies between communication network and data-driven application.

Title: Remaining useful life prediction model of cross-domain rolling bearing via dynamic hybrid domain adaptation and attention contrastive learning
Authors: Xingchi Lu; Xuejian Yao; Quansheng Jiang; Yehu Shen; Fengyu Xu; Qixin Zhu
Abstract: Performance degradation and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction are of great significance in improving the reliability of mechanical equipment. Existing cross-domain RUL prediction methods usually reduce data distribution discrepancy by domain adaptation, to overcome domain shift under cross-domain conditions. However, the fine-grained information between cross-domain degradation features and the specific characteristics of the target domain are often ignored, which limits the prediction performance. Aiming at these issues, a RUL prediction method based on dynamic hybrid domain adaptation (DHDA) and attention contrastive learning (A-CL) is proposed for the cross-domain rolling bearings. In the DHDA module, the conditional distribution alignment is achieved by the designed pseudo-label-guided domain adversarial network, and is assigned with a dynamic penalty term to dynamically adjust the conditional distribution when aligning the joint distribution, for improving the fine-grainedness of domain adaptation. The A-CL module aims to help the prediction model actively extract the degradation information of the target domain, to generate the degradation features that match the characteristics of the target domain, for improving the robustness of RUL prediction. Then, the proposed method is verified by the ablation and comparison experiments conducted on PHM2012 and XJTU-SY datasets. The results show that the proposed method performs high accuracy for cross-domain RUL prediction with good generalization performance under three different cross-domain scenarios.

Title: Predictive Maintenance in Underground Mining with Isolation Forest for Anomaly Detection
Authors: S. Muthumarilakshmi; S. Murugan; D. P. Sangeetha; S. P. Vimal; M. Hebzibah; Ve Sathishkumar
Abstract: Underground mining operations have considerable difficulties in ensuring equipment dependability, since unforeseen failures may result in expensive downtime, safety risks, and diminished output. This paper investigates a predictive maintenance framework using Isolation Forest (IF), an unsupervised machine learning (ML) method for anomaly identification, to tackle these difficulties. The approach examines sensor data, encompassing vibration, temperature, and pressure measurements, gathered from subterranean mining machinery over a six-month duration. This method facilitates the early identification of flaws by detecting atypical operational patterns that develop into significant failures. The experimental assessment revealed that the IF model attained 94.2% accuracy in identifying defective behavior, proactively identified 85% of prospective equipment failures, and facilitated a 40% reduction in unexpected downtime, together with a 25% drop in total maintenance expenditures. These results underscore the capability of ML-driven predictive maintenance to enhance the safety and efficiency of mining operations. The presented approach demonstrates how anomaly detection may prolong equipment lifetime, optimize resource allocation, and improve operational resilience in high-risk subterranean settings.

Title: Remaining useful life prediction method of bearings based on the interactive learning strategy
Authors: Hao Wang; Jing An; Jun Yang; Sen Xu; Zhenmin Wang; Yuan Cao; Weiqi Yuan
Abstract: To address the issues of low accuracy, high time cost, and different failure modes in predicting the remaining useful life of rolling bearings, a remaining useful life prediction model based on an interactive learning convolution network with a feature attention mechanism (ILCANet) was proposed in this paper. The model divided time series data into an odd part and an even part, and the interactive learning strategy improved the ability of the model to extract features from long series. The binary tree structure was used to increase the number of network layers and to subdivide sequence features. In the model, residual connection was introduced to prevent the gradient from disappearing. In addition, in order to determine the degree of contribution of different features, a feature attention mechanism was embedded to assign weights to features. Experiments were conducted with PHM2012 and XJTU-SY datasets, and the results showed that the proposed method had better prediction accuracy in RUL prediction than other prediction methods.

Title: Siamese Neural Network for Few-Shot Visual Inspection of Steel Surface Defects in Predictive Maintenance Systems
Authors: Egor Antonyants; Anna Aletdinova; Vitalii Zaozernov; Alexander Leontiev; Anton Vasiliev
Abstract: The deployment of automated visual inspection systems for surface defect diagnosis is critically important for the transition to preventive maintenance of industrial equipment. However, the effective training of deep neural networks is hindered by the lack of annotated data. This paper proposes an approach based on Siamese Neural Network to solve the problem of surface defect classification under conditions of a limited number of samples. The method is trained to evaluate the semantic similarity between a pair of images, which enables the identification of defects without the need for extensive datasets. To verify the approach, comparative experiments were conducted on the public Northeastern University Surface Defect Database. The proposed Siamese Neural Network model, which uses a convolutional encoder and a contrastive loss function, achieved an accuracy of 0.867, outperforming classical machine learning methods: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform/Support Vector Machine (0.836) and Histogram of Oriented Gradients/Support Vector Machine (0.813). The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the metric learning-based approach for industrial inspection tasks and its potential for integration into predictive maintenance systems to improve reliability and reduce operational costs.

Title: Predictive Maintenance for Drones: Comparative Study of Lightweight Machine Learning Models for Vibration Prediction
Authors: Moubarak Hamidou; Wassim Khiati; Raef Cherif; Nawres Khlifa
Abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of four machine learning (ML) models: linear regression, decision tree, support vector regression (SVR), and random forest for predicting vibrational anomalies using multivariate data collected from inertial, barometric, and positional sensors embedded on a VTOL (Vertical Take-off and Landing) drone. The objective is to develop a lightweight predictive maintenance solution suitable for embedded system constraints. The models are compared based on prediction accuracy (R2, MAE, MSE), training time, memory usage and their potential for real-time deployment. Experimental results show that the random forest model offers the best tradeoff between performance and computational cost, while SVR provides higher accuracy at the expense of greater computational load. These findings highlight the relevance of classical models for implementing predictive maintenance on embedded platforms.

The study detailed that 79.77% of downtime is caused by machinery downtime, prolonged setup times, and unnecessary routes. To address these inefficiencies, techniques such as Predictive Maintenance 4.0 to optimize machinery, SMED to reduce setup times, and SLP with digital support to improve route efficiency were implemented. With these improvements, validated through simulation in Arena software, the company was able to increase its OTD by 25.09%, reduce machine downtime by 47.87%, setup times by 39.99%, and distance traveled by 36.56%, according to the performance indicators defined for each root cause. These results helped close the identified gap and demonstrate the effectiveness of the tools implemented in the metalworking sector.

Title: APPLICATION OF MACHINE LEARNING MODELS FOR PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE OF BIOTECHNICAL SYSTEMS
Authors: Adrian Iosif; Edmond Maican; Sorin Ştefan Biriș; Nicolae Valentin Vlăduț
Abstract: Ensuring the reliability and efficiency of agricultural machinery is critical for modern farming operations. Traditional maintenance strategies, including corrective and preventive approaches, often lead to unexpected downtime or excessive servicing costs. This study explores the application of machine learning-based predictive maintenance for agricultural equipment, focusing on the hydraulic system of a Massey Ferguson 7700 S tractor. Real-time sensor data was collected, with hydraulic pressure selected as the primary diagnostic metric for detecting early signs of mechanical degradation. A predictive maintenance framework was developed using seven machine learning models: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, KMeans, DBSCAN, Autoencoders, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and XGBoost. These models were individually applied to identify pressure anomalies indicative of potential failures. To enhance detection accuracy, a "Council of the Wise" ensemble approach was introduced, where an anomaly was validated only if at least four of the seven models agreed on its presence. This consensus-based method reduced false positives and improved fault identification reliability. Results demonstrated that integrating multiple models effectively distinguished significant anomalies from noise, capturing both transient mechanical instabilities and gradual wear-related failures. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning-driven predictive maintenance in optimizing maintenance schedules, reducing unplanned downtime, and extending equipment lifespan. This study establishes a scalable, data-driven maintenance approach that enhances the operational resilience of agricultural machinery, ensuring greater efficiency and sustainability in farming operations.

Title: Predictive Maintenance Based on Deep Learning: Early Identification of Failures in Heavy Machinery Components
Authors: Pablo Cabrera Melgar; Luis Hilasaca Chambi; Ra´ul Sulla Torres
Abstract: Deep learning-based predictive maintenance is a key strategy in industry to prevent unexpected failures, reduce downtime, and improve operational safety. This study presents an advanced approach for early fault detection in heavy machinery components using image analysis, focusing on four critical defect types: hose wear, piston failure, corrosion, and moisture. To this end, three state-of-the-art object detection models were implemented and compared: YOLOv11, RT-DETR, and YOLO-World. The dataset consists of images captured in real-life industrial environments exhibiting variations in lighting, texture, and material degradation. A manual preprocessing and annotation process was applied to improve training quality. Model performance was evaluated using key metrics such as the precision-recall (PR) curve and the confusion matrix to determine the most efficient technique for real-time fault detection. Experimental results show that YOLOv11 achieves the highest overall accuracy, with an mAP@0.5 of 83.8%, followed by YOLO-World at 82.4% and RT-DETR at 80.3%. In terms of efficiency, YOLO-World offers a balance between accuracy and detection speed, while RT-DETR shows stable performance but lower accuracy for certain defect types. These findings confirm that deep learning-based detection models enable the rapid and accurate identification of industrial defects, facilitating the implementation of predictive maintenance strategies.

Title: Optimized Gradient Boosting for Predictive Maintenance: A Two-Task Framework for RUL Estimation and Failure Classification
Authors: S. Navaneeth; Vimala Mathew
Abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is a cornerstone of Industry 4.0, with the promise of reducing operating expenses, minimizing unexpected downtime, and enhancing system reliability. This paper presents an integrated framework using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to address two core PdM issues: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation (regression) and binary failure prediction (classification). We illustrate the efficacy of the framework on two very different, practical-world datasets: a lithium-ion battery cycle life dataset for RUL estimation and a massive-scale IoT-based smart manufacturing dataset for failure classification. For both, we utilize state-of-the-art hyperparameter optimization techniques-Optuna for regression and Bayesian Optimization for classification-to realize optimal predictive performance. The XGBoost Regressor tuned for battery RUL prediction had an R2 of 0.9998 and an RMSE of 4.59 cycles, far surpassing usual regression baselines and state-of-the-art deep learning models reported recently. The XGBoost Classifier designed for machine failure prediction had a high accuracy of 98.9% and AUC-ROC of 0.9988, demonstrating its dominance against other usual classifiers on an imbalanced large dataset. The results incontrovertibly demonstrate that a professionally tuned XGBoost model is a strong, adaptive, and extremely potent tool for tackling major regression and classification problems in predictive maintenance.

Title: Advanced Predictive Maintenance of Phoenix Contact Relays: A Digital Twin and Machine Learning Approach
Authors: Modi Shivang Bhaskarkumar; Bagavathi P. Sivakumar
Abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) leveraging digital twin technology offers a transformative approach to maintaining industrial equipment, minimizing downtime, and reducing maintenance costs. We focus on the predictive maintenance of Phoenix Contact relays using a comprehensive dataset of relay sensor readings (the Phoenix Contact Relay dataset). By implementing advanced machine learning models, including a bagging and boosting model, different types of LSTM, and an Autoencoder with a fully connected neural network, we aim to predict relay failures accurately. Our approach involves data preprocessing, feature extraction, and feature augmentation to create the dataset that improves the predictive capabilities of these models. To provide a dynamic, real-time representation of the relay, We use a digital twin framework that continuously simulates its behavior and predicts potential failures. This integration tries to improve the accuracy but also provides insights into the underlying causes of relay degradation. In industrial applications, we try to demonstrate that using digital twin technology alongside machine learning and deep learning models can result in highly efficient and reliable predictive maintenance.

Title: PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE FOR ROTORCRAFT: A DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH WITH MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR ENHANCED AVAILABILITY
Authors: Gianbattista Dario Natale; Federico Guglielmin; Andrea Ricci; Domenico Andreocci; Alessandro Scandroglio; Nicolò Vallana
Abstract: Predictive maintenance represents a critical advancement in rotorcraft fleet management, offering substantial improvements in operational availability while reducing unscheduled downtime costs. This paper presents two complementary data-driven approaches utilizing machine learning algorithms for enhanced rotorcraft component monitoring. The first methodology addresses transmission system health monitoring through an unsupervised Principal Component Analysis algorithm that consolidates approximately one thousand health indices from accelerometer data into a single normalized health score. This approach successfully detected transmission failures an average of twenty-four flight hours in advance across a fleet of approximately seven hundred aircraft, achieving false positive rates below one per ten flight hours and false negative rates below one per sixty flight hours based on millions of flight hours of operational data. The second methodology employs virtual sensor technology combined with machine learning models to predict damage indices and remaining useful life for rotor components that cannot be directly instrumented during service operations. Gradient boosting and convolutional neural network approaches were implemented using flight data and inferred virtual sensor measurements to estimate component degradation. Both methodologies demonstrate fleet-wide applicability, providing maintenance organizations with actionable insights for proactive component replacement scheduling and logistics optimization.

Title: Optimizing Predictive Maintenance: Addressing Imbalanced Data with Sampling Techniques and Stacking Models in Fault Prediction
Authors: Ye Shang
Abstract: In the modern industrial field, industrial machinery failures can bring high production losses and significant maintenance losses to enterprises. Predictive maintenance has become an important research direction to solve this problem, and fault prediction is the core link in predictive maintenance. Mastering fault prediction methods is crucial. This article is based on the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset of UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository. It mainly constructs a fault prediction model through decision trees, random forests, and MLPClassifier in machine learning, and explores the optimal model based on this dataset. On this basis, various methods such as random oversampling, random undersampling, SMOTE, etc. were used to optimize the fault prediction scheme for the imbalanced sample problem that occurred in the experiment. Some methods are effective, but the performance of the model is not significantly improved, so further explore the fault prediction scheme using Stacking to integrate multiple models, compare the evaluation results of single model and multiple models, and the scheme using Stacking to integrate decision trees, random forests and MLPClassifier models has the best effect in this experiment, with F 1 score of 0. 8 0 9 8. This conclusion indicates the importance of using Stacking ensemble method to integrate multiple models in mechanical fault prediction. At the same time, it also verified the positive effect of various data augmentation methods on handling imbalanced data for fault prediction in the model. This study also provides a reference for future industrial machinery fault prediction.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Enhanced Telematics Data Simulation for Predictive Maintenance in E-Mobility Fleet Operations
Authors: Akash Ambulkar; Sammit J. Deshpande
Abstract: Predictive maintenance is a cornerstone for reliable e-mobility fleet management, yet acquiring sufficient failure-mode data in real fleets is both expensive and time-consuming. This paper introduces a machine learning-enhanced simulation pipeline to generate synthetic telematics datasets that mimic real-world electric vehicle operational patterns and component degradation. A generative adversarial network (GAN) is trained on limited real-world battery, motor, and sensor data from telematics units to produce diverse, physically plausible trajectories of state-of-health indicators. The simulated data populates a digital twin of an EV fleet, upon which gradient boosting and recurrent neural network models are evaluated for anomaly detection and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. Title: Neuromorphic Audio Dataset for Predictive Maintenance in Peristaltic Pumps
Authors: Juan M. Montes-Sánchez; Juan P. Domínguez-Morales; Saturnino Vicente-Díaz; Ángel Jiménez-Fernández
Abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) applications are becoming more and more popular, in part because Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms are becoming more powerful and affordable. However, this method requires a lot of data which need to be specific to the application. Only a few audio datasets on the topic are available, most of them are focused on generic systems, and none to the best of our knowledge has been created from a neuromorphic engineering approach, which offers benefits in terms of power consumption and robustness among others. We used a Neuromorphic Auditory Sensor (NAS) to record a neuromorphic audio dataset that covers two different scenarios of PdM in actual equipment from a commercial device. We focused on faults due to deterioration of the peristaltic pumps caused by aging and also on detecting the presence of undesired air bubbles in the hydraulic circuit. The audio information was processed in Address Event Representation (AER) format, which was then converted into a set of labeled sonogram images of 0.5 s each. We used a window overlap of 50%, which enlarges the number of samples and improves training results. All of these data are now available as a public dataset. We did a classification test for both scenarios by training a DenseNet121 model that achieved a F1 weighted average of 0.99 for the aging scenario and 0.71 for the bubble scenario. Further processing should be done in the future to improve the results on the bubble scenario.

Title: Advancing Predictive Maintenance in Agriculture: Empowering Farmers through IoT-Driven Machine Learning for Enhanced Equipment Performance and Operational Efficacy

Abstract: The agricultural industry has adopted modern machinery for key operations, which has made equipment reliability important for productivity and minimizing downtime. The use of traditional maintenance approaches, which are reactive or time-based, is insufficient for modern agriculture. By placing IoT sensors on tractors, harvesters, and other equipment, critical operational data like temperature, vibration, fuel consumption, and other usage patterns can be monitored 24/7, resulting in improving the life quality, such as education quality, public health, and clean energy technology. Machine learning models analyze this data for anomaly detection, predicting component failures, and formulating maintenance schedules. This improves maintenance scheduling as any problem is actively dealt with in advance so that equipment failure can be reduced, the lifespan of the machinery can be enhanced, and the farm's level of making decisions can be improved. The study hypothesizes the predictive maintenance IoT-ML framework and confirms it by simulations and a case study of medium-sized farming enterprises. The study indicates that there is enhanced operational efficiency, a reduction in costs, and access to more equipment by farmers. One more implication of this study is that it shows both the lack of data connectivity in rural areas and the necessity to provide farmers with the skills in the digital field. The core finding of the job discussed in this paper is that machine learning applied to the IoT devices enables farmers to make data-driven decisions, which involve sustainability and optimize the current operation practices in agriculture.

Title: Development of a Generator Condition Monitoring Device for Predictive Maintenance Applications Considering Temperature and Vibration Analysis
Authors: Vann Anthony C. Viray; Marven E. Jabian
Abstract: A condition monitoring device is developed to support predictive maintenance strategies for industrial generators by acquiring vibration and temperature data - two common indicators of mechanical and thermal faults. The system integrated a digital accelerometer and a non-contact infrared sensor, with an ESP32 microcontroller serving as the main processing unit to monitor real-time operational parameters. Data are collected at fixed intervals and transmitted wirelessly using an NRF24L01 module. Additional features included battery monitoring, LED indicators, and an alarm system. All components are integrated onto a custom-printed circuit board and enclosed within a 3D-printed housing. The device is designed to operate non-intrusively, powered by either an external source or a rechargeable battery, with power-saving capabilities via light sleep mode for extended deployment. Initial tests demonstrated accurate sensor readings and effective wireless transmission, validating the device's capability for fault detection. Although currently limited to data acquisition and transmission, the system is capable of future integration with data logging, analytics, or machine learning models for advanced predictive maintenance. This solution offers a cost-effective and practical approach to real-time generator condition monitoring.

Title: SMOTE-Enhanced Predictive Maintenance of Hydraulic Systems using Random Forest and Logistic Regression

Abstract: The industry's hydraulic system defects often result in excessive repairs and unexpected downtime. One of the most difficult parts of predictive maintenance is dealing with an imbalance in the data. In most cases, such as my research, we have a lack of failure cases compared to a sizeable number of nominal or normal operating records. This ultimately causes difficulty for a model in detecting rare faults like we have with hydraulic systems. This current work tackles the problem by utilizing Random Forest and Logistic Regression models along with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to have a more balanced dataset. Each model was evaluated on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Overall, the results show that SMOTE enabled the model to identify faults in a more successful manner, while especially benefiting rare failure cases. Of the studied models, Random Forest with SMOTE proved to be the most successful, giving a better performance with higher accuracy and fewer errors. This enables a better approach to hydraulic system maintenance and limit unexpected breakdowns.

Title: Application of Two-Parameter Weibull Distribution for Predictive Maintenance: A Case Study

Abstract: The maintenance of facilities, machinery, and infrastructure is a fundamental aspect of any organization. Title: DATA-DRIVEN PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE USING THE GOMPERTZ CURVE
Authors: Zdeněk Aleš; Jaroslav Mrázek; Marián Kučera; Michal Strnad
Abstract: This paper presents the application of the Gompertz function in the context of machine condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. The proposed methodology focuses on modeling the nonlinear progression of wear using diagnostic signals collected during machine operation. While both structural and operational data can be utilized, operational signals such as temperature, pressure, and oil contamination provide the advantage of continuous, real time, and noninvasive monitoring. The asymptotic and asymmetric nature of the Gompertz function makes it particularly suitable for representing bounded degradation processes, especially in components with predefined wear thresholds. The paper introduces algorithms for estimating model parameters and calculating the remaining useful life (RUL) of machine elements. These algorithms, implemented in Python, enable real time evaluation of component condition and support data driven, proactive maintenance planning. The results demonstrate that Gompertz based modeling offers a robust and interpretable approach to improving machine reliability and optimizing maintenance strategies in accordance with Industry 4.0 principles.

Title: Alert Lifecycle and Best Practices for Predictive Maintenance Alert Lifecycle Management
Authors: Justin Sindewald; Ryan Latini; Joseph Rice
Abstract: The predictive maintenance alert lifecycle is a critical topic in the aviation industry. Stakeholders, including operators, suppliers, and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), require effective frameworks to support the value proposition of predictive maintenance products and services. However, defining alert effectiveness is challenging due to the lack of industry standards for the end-to-end lifecycle of predictive maintenance alerts. Adding to the challenge, different stakeholders may want to optimize on different objectives. Often, alert performance is measured prematurely or not at all. To ensure high-quality alerts, all alerts should be managed through their entire lifecycle until obsolescence. This whitepaper outlines a clear conceptual framework for the predictive maintenance alert lifecycle and best practices alert lifecycle management. Future work will expand upon the qualitative benefits discussed herein with quantitative results achieved from applying this framework to assess alert effectiveness at scale within the Boeing alert catalog.

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Nanosatellite Power Systems: Enhancing Reliability Through Machine Learning
Authors: Amina Daghouri; Mustapha Ahricha; Imane Khalil; Mohammed Alae Chanoui; Soumia El Hani; Zouhair Guennoun
Abstract: Nanosatellites have revolutionized space exploration by offering cost-effective and accessible platforms for scientific research, Earth observation, and deep-space missions. However, their limited power capacity and lack of continuous ground intervention expose them to unexpected system failures, particularly within Electrical Power Systems (EPS), which are crucial for mission success. Conventional fault detection relies on predefined thresholds and rule-based monitoring, which often fail to detect early performance degradation, increasing the likelihood of power failures, reduced mission lifespans, and data loss. To improve the reliability of nanosatellite power systems, an AI-driven predictive maintenance approach is introduced, enabling real-time anomaly detection and fault prediction. By leveraging machine learning techniques, this method examines historical telemetry data to detect patterns in battery behavior, power distribution variations, and solar panel efficiency changes. The framework implements onboard lightweight AI models that perform two key functions: detecting anomalies in real time by continuously monitoring EPS behavior using telemetry parameters such as voltage, current, temperature, and state of charge, and enabling predictive fault prevention by anticipating potential failures and taking preventive actions. This approach optimizes power management, extends battery life, and reduces reliance on ground-based monitoring, ultimately enhancing the satellite's autonomy and reliability. Simulations show that this AI-based system achieves more than 90% accuracy in fault detection while reducing false alarms by 40%, significantly increasing system resilience and energy efficiency. Unlike traditional threshold-based methods, the predictive maintenance framework provides an adaptive and robust solution for identifying and mitigating EPS anomalies. The integration of AI in satellite power system monitoring marks a significant advancement in autonomous spacecraft management, allowing nanosatellites to diagnose and address power-related issues without external intervention. This capability is particularly valuable for deep-space missions and large-scale satellite constellations, where immediate operator support is often unavailable. AI-driven predictive maintenance offers a scalable and effective solution to extending mission durations, optimizing energy consumption, and minimizing failure risks, ensuring nanosatellites achieve greater operational reliability in increasingly demanding space environments.

Title: Implementing Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance (PdM) and Equipment Failure Prevention in the Manufacturing Sector
Authors: Rabia Emhamed Al Mamlook; Mohammed Almaiah; Qais Al-Na’amneh; Hasan Gharaibeh; Ahmad Nasayreh
Abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) in the manufacturing sector is crucial for monitoring structure failures and scheduling the Maintenance of machines. This research aims to use machine learning (ML) methods to build and validate precise models for predicting Maintenance and avoiding failures in industrial machinery. It also focuses on evaluating the efficacy of different ML models in predictive maintenance within the manufacturing sector. The study seeks to identify which models can most effectively predict equipment failures, with a detailed comparison of the performance of ANN, LR, and DT models based on various statistical metrics. Their performance was assessed utilizing F1-score, accuracy, recall, and the area under the curve. The results recommend that the Decision Tree (DT) model offers the best predictive performance with an F1-score of 0.982, an accuracy of 0.978, a recall of 0.969, and an area under the curve of 0.980. The most significant influencing features for predicting failure mechanisms were the mean of rotation, pressure, and error 4 count through twenty-four hours. The study suggests that ML can improve maintenance estimates, enhance equipment reliability, and realize the best realizable value in the manufacturing sector.

Title: Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance Technology of Hydraulic and Pneumatic Transmission System

Abstract: With the rapid development of industrial field, hydraulic and pneumatic transmission system, as the core power transmission mode, plays an important role in improving production efficiency. Through noise reduction, feature extraction and classifier identification, the fault diagnosis of hydraulic and pneumatic transmission systems is realized accurately. In this study, random forest (RF) algorithm is used to build a health state evaluation model, and BP neural network (BPNN) is used to predict the remaining service life of the system, which provides strong support for the maintenance decision of enterprises. The experimental results show that the fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance methods designed in this study have high accuracy and stability. The classification accuracy of fault diagnosis model is generally high, reaching an average accuracy of 90%; Predictive maintenance model has high prediction accuracy, and the error is controlled within 5% in predicting the remaining service life.

Title: Enhancing Smart Manufacturing with Secure Predictive Maintenance: A Data-Driven Approach
Authors: Sunitha Safavat; Danda B. Rawat
Abstract: In smart manufacturing systems, Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is essential for optimizing equipment performance and reducing unplanned downtime for automated systems and machinery. Managing the vast amounts of real-time operational data generated by these systems requires a secure, scalable data-driven approach for robust PdM. This paper introduces a secure PdM framework employing Hyperbolic Cosine Differential Privacy (HCDP) to enhance attribute privacy in big datadriven predictive maintenance. Specifically, the system handles large-scale data acquisition, pre-processing, data grouping, and attribute extraction, with key attributes protected by HCDP. Next, the PdM analysis is conducted using Transfer Learning Generalized Collapsing Long Nuclear Logarithmic Entropy Short Term Memory (TL-GCLNLESTM), a model that leverages transfer learning to adapt to diverse scenarios and identify patterns within massive data streams ensuring predictive security. Then the Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Schwefel Explanation (LIMSE) framework interprets predictive outcomes, enhancing transparency and decision-making. If a failure is predicted/anticipated, the maintenance schedule is recomended using Ramp Multi-peak Gaussian Fuzzy (RMG-Fuzzy), with alerts issued accordingly. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy showcasing the efficacy of the proposed approach for PdM in smart manufacturing maintenance.

This predictive strategy, based on lifecycle phases and trends, facilitates targeted maintenance interventions before major failures occur. This article investigates PHM integration for pneumatic valve membrane maintenance in the biopharmaceutical sector. It proposes a method to identify experimental data, define lifecycle criteria, analyse these criteria, compare them with planned maintenance practices, and evaluate signal drifts to characterise the membrane state for future predictive maintenance development.

Authors: Mukesh Kumar Nigam; Shwetank Avikal
Abstract: Optimizing the frequency and nature of maintenance on industrial equipment is the primary goal of the field of study known as Predictive Maintenance (PDM). New challenges and avenues in PDM have drawn the attention of many researchers towards the risk management strategy that may contribute to the success of PDM implementation. This paper aims to conduct a risk assessment in Predictive Maintenance 4.0 (PDM 4.0). In the 1st phase, risk factors were identified and analysed through a systematic literature review and expert opinions. In the 2nd phase, risk evaluation was conducted by the integrated approach of Best Worst Method (BWM) and Fuzzy Proximity Index Value (FPIV) methods. In the proposed integrated approach, risk criteria were identified through a literature review, and their weights were determined using the BWM. The final risk ranking of these criteria has been tabulated by FPIV, a novel MCDM method. A comparison was made between MCDM approaches, Fuzzy COPRAS and FPIV for risk ranking. Rank reversal and sensitivity analysis were performed to check the robustness of the integrated approach. The proposed models are illustrated with a real-world case study involving an online vibration monitoring system in a fertilizer organization using high-speed rotary machines. The results of the integrated approach demonstrate that high investment costs, inadequate vendor industry experience, inadequate training programs about PDM 4.0, inadequate modelling techniques, and regulatory & legal risks, are the top five risks that need to be mitigated by practical methodology.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Domain Adaptation for Predictive Maintenance of Ball Screw Feed Drives Using Maximum Mean Discrepancy
Authors: Ramakrishna Garine; Nirmal Kumar Balaraman
Abstract: To remain competitive in the global market, companies must optimize their production processes. The vast amounts of data and modern information and communication technologies present significant opportunities for advanced diagnostics and maintenance. By analyzing machine and production data, proactive maintenance can be implemented-which enhances quality standards and production line efficiency. Ball screw feed drives-commonly found in industrial machines-require monitoring due to their importance in machinery. Given the varying operating conditions, prognostics and health management systems must be robust enough to adapt to continuous changes in machine faults. Modern domain adaptation methods have become popular in these systems to address shifts in machine data. Therefore, this study introduces a Deep Learning based domain adaptation model to predict the health of ball screw feed drives. During model training-domain shifts in the model's latent feature spaces are measured and minimized using the maximum mean discrepancy method. By using this method to the Convolutional Neural Network layers results in a more effective reduction of domain shifts. The impact of different hyperparameter choices in the domain adaptation module is assessed to ensure optimal performance. A novel labeled maximum mean discrepancy metric is introduced-which uses a small portion of training target labels for improved accuracy in predicting machine health.

Title: Advanced Prognostic Models for Predictive Maintenance: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
Authors: Sahil; Urvashi
Abstract: Predictive maintenance is an essential technique used by organizations to reduce unexpected equipment failures and improve operational effectiveness. Estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of machinery is an essential aspect of this process, which helps industries like manufacturing, water treatment, and aerospace schedule maintenance in advance and avoid costly breakdowns. This study looks at a number of methods for estimating Remaining Useful Life (RUL), such as hybrid approaches, statistical methods, and machine learning models. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are examples of deep learning techniques that make it easier to analyze sensor data, while physics-based models improve accuracy by taking consideration of actual conditions. Planning maintenance for complex systems is improved when these approaches are included into hybrid models.Some issues still exist without technological developments, such as high processing power requirements, challenges handling real-time data, and a limited ability to understand predictions produced by AI. While accuracy has increased with advanced techniques like Bayesian neural networks, particle filtering, and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), more research is required for real-time implementation. This study highlights the use of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction in water purification systems, in which artificial intelligence establishes the best time to replace filters, maintaining water purity while decreasing costs.

Title: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance in Semiconductor SEM Equipment
Authors: Kai Jin; Hua Li; Edgar Alexis Olivares
Abstract: Predictive maintenance has emerged as a pivotal strategy in the semiconductor industry, leveraging machine learning algorithms to anticipate equipment failures and optimize maintenance schedules. Semiconductor manufacturing facilities rely on complex machinery and equipment to produce integrated circuits and other semiconductor devices. Any unexpected downtime or equipment failure can lead to significant production losses and costly repairs. Predictive maintenance stands out from other maintenance categories as it precludes any failures to equipment components. By implementing predictive maintenance solutions powered by machine learning, semiconductor companies can monitor the health of their equipment in real-time, detect potential issues before they escalate into failures, and schedule maintenance proactively to minimize downtime. In this paper, the application of predictive maintenance techniques within semiconductor manufacturing is explored, focusing on the development and deployment of machine learning models to predict equipment failures based on sensor data collected from scanning electron microscope (SEM) metrology equipment. The approach adopted in this study involves simulating sensor output data from wafer runs, training machine learning models on the generated dataset, and deploying the models as real-time inference endpoints. By integrating Azure Machine Learning Designer and Power BI, the accuracy and performance of the predictive maintenance model is assessed. Results of the study demonstrate the efficacy of machine learning in accurately forecasting equipment failures, thereby minimizing downtime and optimizing operational efficiency in semiconductor manufacturing facilities. Overall, this study underscores the transformative potential of predictive maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, paving the way for enhanced operational resilience and sustained competitiveness in the industry.

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Industrial IoT with Real-Time Fault Detection and Prediction
Authors: A. Hency Juliet
Abstract: Predictive maintenance for industrial machinery uses data analysis and advanced techniques to forecast equipment failures. This proactive approach schedules maintenance to minimize downtime and optimize operational efficiency. Achieving accurate, consistent, and well-integrated IoT sensor data is difficult, as poor data quality can result in inaccurate predictions and false alerts. Scaling real-time fault detection and prediction requires substantial computational power and optimized algorithms to process the continuous influx of data from multiple machines. To address data quality and integration issues while enhancing real-time processing and scalability, a Custom Neural Network technique can be used to improve IoT sensor data accuracy and consistency, and efficiently manage the computational demands of continuous data influx for fault detection and prediction. The proposed system, leveraging an extended Neural Network technique, enhances prediction accuracy by efficiently managing diverse industrial datasets and improves real-time fault detection through optimized data processing and reduced latency. The model demonstrated a remarkable accuracy of 92.86%, showcasing its ability to accurately identify both faulty and non-faulty equipment. With a precision of 90.91%, a perfect recall of 100%, and an F1 score of 95.24%, the model exhibited a well-balanced fault detection performance, minimizing false positives while ensuring thorough fault identification, all while processing in real-time with an efficient time complexity of 2.49 seconds.

Title: Optimization of Operations in Industry 4.0 Settings with Real-Time Predictive Maintenance Working with Machine Learning
Authors: S. B. Prakalya; V. Seethalakshmi; Murthoty Satheesh Babu; Zakaria Azzam; Ginni Nijhawan; M. Dinesh
Abstract: Since Industry 4.0 introduced cutting-edge technologies like IoT, Big Data, and AI into operational processes, the industrial and manufacturing sectors have changed drastically. Predictive maintenance with these technologies is promising. It reduces maintenance costs and downtime by predicting equipment failure using real-time data. In Industry 4.0, this project studies real-time predictive maintenance utilizing ML techniques to optimize industrial operations. IoT sensor data can be used to build predictive models to detect wear and malfunction in machines and tools. This makes procedures short and effective, allowing rapid action. Deep learning models, decision trees, regression models, and machine learning methods are used to analyze massive amounts of time-series data produced by industrial machinery. By finding new sensor data patterns and correlations, these systems may be able to predict equipment failure. Another essential part of the project is integrating predictive models with IoT systems. It tracks equipment health and operation in real time. Technology's continual machine data analysis improves maintenance plans and reduces unscheduled downtime. It also sends out real-time alerts to users. Data quality, interpretability of models, and scalability are three more issues that this study attempts to resolve for predictive maintenance systems operating in complicated industrial settings. The findings show that in an Industry 4.0 environment, predictive maintenance driven by machine learning may greatly increase operational efficiency while decreasing costs and boosting total production.

Title: Machine Learning Approaches for Predictive Maintenance in Smart Manufacturing Environments
Authors: Naina Chaudhary; Pratap Patil; Z. Tanveer Baig; Mohit Bhandwal; Manik Rakhra; Prabha Kiran
Abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) is a key enabler for Industry 4.0. Predictive maintenance has one goal: to predict equipment failures in the future to minimize downtimes (and resulting costs) in production. Today's intelligent smartmanufacturing environment of sensors, big data analytics and machine learning (ML) has enabled around-the-clock machine health surveillance. This manuscript provides a review and a critical evaluation of state-of-the-art ML methodologies for PdM by categorizing the methodologies in supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning. The applicability of these methods in the fault detection, remaining useful life (RUL) estimation, and anomaly detection is investigated. A case study using vibration and temperature datasets obtained from CNC machinery is used to show the comparative performance of Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Long Short Shane Memory (LSTMs) Neural Networks. According to evaluation performances including accuracy, precision, recall and mean absolute error (MAE), LSTM-based models outperformed the conventional ML approaches in terms of modeling the temporal dynamics of sensor data. It also discusses the problems such as data imbalance, model interpretability, and real-time application, and provides recommendations for hybrid architecture and edgecomputing implementation. Accordingly, a framework for ML algorithm selection and implementation in PdM systems in smart manufacturing scenarios is proposed in this study, aiming at increased reliability, safety, and cost efficiency.

Title: Machine Learning Framework for Industrial Machine Sound Classification in Predictive Maintenance
Authors: Nur Fatinah Md Hafiz; Syamsiah Mashohor; Mohammad Habib Shah Ershad Mohd Azrul Shazril; Azizi Mohd Ali; Mohd Fadlee A. Rasid
Abstract: Predictive maintenance, utilising anomalous sound classification, demonstrates a strong potential to identify mechanical faults in industrial machinery. This research proposes a machine learning-based framework for classifying anomalous sounds in industrial machines, with a particular focus on CT scan machines and fan units. The study utilises both real-world data from CT scan machine sound and the Malfunctioning Industrial Machine Investigation and Inspection (MIMII) dataset. It offers a comprehensive analysis of sound signal processing techniques, synthetic data generation methods, feature extraction processes, and classification using machine learning models to support predictive maintenance applications. In this research, sound data from a CT scan machine was collected using an Internet of Things (IoT) connected microphone located on the machine in a Klang Valley hospital. Due to the limited availability of faulty condition data, synthetic anomalous data for both operational and non-operational conditions were generated using a noise injection method. Features derived from Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and Mel Spectrogram representations were employed to analyse the sound data. The dataset for CT scan machine sounds is categorised into four distinct classes: anomalous operational sound (Aop), anomalous non-operational sound (Anop), normal operational sound (Nop), and normal non-operational sound (Nnop). In contrast, the MIMII dataset is classified into two categories: normal and abnormal. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was used for a sound classification system, achieving training accuracies of 98.22% with Mel spectrogram features and 98.12% with MFCC features. The results emphasise the possibility of using CNN-based sound classification to effectively anticipate and maintain CT scan machines. This finding also has the potential to be applied to predictive maintenance applications by detecting both normal and anomalous operating sounds in industrial machinery.

Title: Optimizing Industrial IoT Predictive Maintenance Using Quantum Algorithms on Google Quantum AI
Authors: Sandeep Chouhan; Ramandeep Sandhu; Sorab Kumar; Sardar M.N. Islam
Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has transformed the concept of predictive maintenance by creating the possibility of real-time monitoring of machinery and equipment. However, the large volumes and complexity of data generated by IIoT sensors do pose significant challenges for data processing techniques. Quantum computing can be a transformative solution based on quantum algorithms that might improve predictive maintenance models. This paper discusses the integration of quantum algorithms on Google Quantum AI for optimising IIoT-based predictive maintenance systems. Techniques such as Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) and quantum k-means clustering enable faster data processing and further enhance the accuracy of the anomaly detection process. Techniques such as Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) help in optimizing schedules for maintenance and resource allocation to reduce downtime and operational costs. Therefore, quantum simulations do better forecasts with the proper handling of equipment wear, and material degradation, bringing with themselves proper maintenance actions taken proactively. The real-time, parallel processing capability from the combined quantum computer and IIoT streams will lead to better, faster, low-cost maintenance decisions. Sustainably implemented quantum-fortified techniques are expected to give the least or no false positives, ensure events of unplanned downtime occurrence, and optimize maintenance resource usage. While further quantum advancement and breaking data integration challenges remain to be faced before reaching mass impact, now with the advancement of quantum technology it is possible to drastically change the landscape in the industrial space for predictive maintenance by revealing long-term efficiency gains in addition to cost savings. The paper unfolds potential advantages, challenges, and future direction on implementing quantum algorithms for IIoT-driven predictive maintenance systems.

Title: Advancing Machine Learning-Based IoT Sensor Data Processing for Industrial Predictive Maintenance Applications
Authors: Dinesh Kumar Arivalagan; Sathiyandrakumar Srinivasan
Abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) solutions are revolutionizing industrial operations because to the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML). With the use of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, these systems can track machinery health and identify when it might break down, which in turn improves operating efficiency and decreases downtime. Processing, interpreting, and making decisions in real-time are all made much more difficult by the massive amounts of diverse data produced by IoT devices. Modern predictive maintenance relies heavily on machine learning since it provides strong solutions for processing such complicated data. The article delves into recent developments in processing data from Internet of Things (IoT) sensors using ML for predictive maintenance in commercial settings. With an emphasis on supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning methods, it provides a synopsis of current research in processing sensor data. Data preprocessing and dimensionality reduction techniques are among the options proposed in the paper as means to enhance model accuracy and efficiency while dealing with noisy, high-dimensional IoT data. The article also emphasizes how edge computing helps with real-time data processing, which makes PdM systems even more scalable. This work's main contribution is an in-depth analysis of machine learning (ML) models used to Internet of Things (IoT) data for RUL estimation, anomaly detection, and failure prediction. Title: Improve Deep Learning for Industrial IoT Predictive Maintenance: Mechanisms for Time-Series Forecasting to Prevent Equipment Failure
Authors: N. V.S. Natteshan; Mohammad Omar Sabri; P. Sevanthi; Kambham Pratap Joshi; Biroju Papachary; G. Karthikeyan
Abstract: In the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) age, the industrial operation of manufacture and production systems has been completely revolutionized with real-time connectivity, monitoring and control of industrial machinery. At the heart of this change is Predictive Maintenance, an intelligent practice that draws the insights it needs for smarter decision-making from the ongoing collection and analysis of real-time data. Conventional maintenance methods, such as reactive or based on schedules, frequently lead to unplanned downtime, spare parts wastage, or breakdown. This work presents an enhanced deep learning model specially tailored for time-series prediction in IIoT to enhance predictive maintenance accuracy. The proposed approach is based on the correlation between temporal patterns in time series data generated by sensors and the state of the sensor network and it explores more advanced deep learning architectures such as Long Short-Term Memory networks, Gated Recurrent Units and Temporal Convolutional Networks. These models are also enriched with attention mechanisms and mixed ensemble strategies to enhance the accuracy in failure prediction and decrease false alarms. Significant industrial parameters (e.g. vibration, temperature, pressure, number of operation cycles) are constantly tracked, preprocessed and normalized, so that the system can be trained in a supervised manner. Emphasis is on predicting anomalies and degradation trends over time to initiate timely maintenance actions. Experimental verification was carried out both on benchmark industrial data, such as NASA's C-MAPSS and real time sensor data originating from IIoT-enabled production lines. Finding indicated that the model showed better performance than the classical statistical and simple machine-learning models in terms of prediction accuracy, mean absolute error and interpretability. This approach not only increases operational reliability, it also generates competitive advantages by minimizing unscheduled downtimes and maximizing the service life of equipment. The work shows that the combination of state-of-the-art deep learning models within IIoTs could fundamentally change the landscape of predictive maintenance. The proposed framework presents an intelligent data-driven decision support system suitable for smart manufacturing and digital transformation goals.

Title: Predictive Maintenance Automation: Artificial Maintenance Management Agent (AMMA) Framework
Authors: A. Qura; A. Ibrahim
Abstract: This paper describes an innovative Artificial Maintenance Management Agent (AMMA) designed to detect and predict anomalies in machinery equipment, besides managing spare parts orders. The primary focus is on leveraging deep learning models and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to facilitate real-time maintenance and improve user experience respectively. This paper will show how to reduce downtimes, extend the equipment's useful life, and enhance the cost efficiency of inventory management. The approach involves the integration of state-of-the-art deep learning models for the detection and prediction of machine faults, with Large Language Models (LLMs) for interactive user engagement and inventory management. AMMA is architected to continuously learn from real-time operational data stored in a database, enabling it to identify patterns of potential failures. Additionally, it demonstrates current and future predictions on a dashboard. Through its natural language processing capabilities, the agent interacts with maintenance personnel, providing actionable insights and automating spare parts ordering for current and future failures. Preliminary results demonstrate that AMMA exceeded an accuracy of 90% in detecting anomalies in a simulated boiler fault dataset, with loss function value below 0.19, a precision higher than 0.93, a recall higher than 0.93 and a F1 score higher than 0.88 in test set. Showing a high capability to accurately detect machine anomalies before they escalate into costly failures. In addition, models that can be implemented in the agent for failure prediction have shown an accuracy score exceeding 90% in predicting the failures in a 3W dataset which is a public dataset for undesirable real events in oil wells. Observations highlight AMMA's potential to transform maintenance strategies from reactive to proactive, ultimately leading to enhanced safety. The use of the LLM OpenAI API model to enhance the user experience, besides suggesting spare parts according to the failure type, reduces operational costs and human error and increases productivity. The novelty of the proposed AMMA lies in introducing an application of deep learning and LLMs to enhance maintenance effectiveness, offering a unique solution and a step ahead of the current computerized maintenance management system (CMMS). It provides an AI-powered framework for predictive maintenance management, thereby enhancing existing solutions and advancing the state of knowledge in the industry.

Title: Implementing Next-Gen Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Machineries: A Comparative Analysis of Small, Medium & Large Enterprises
Authors: Krunal Patel; Aishvarya Hariharan; Rahul Sucharitha
Abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is transforming industrial processes by leveraging data-driven insights to reduce failures and enhance performance. The global predictive maintenance (PdM) Market is expanding rapidly, making it a high value opportunity in the coming years. In 2023, the market was worth roughly $10 billion, and its projected to reach about $ 60 Billion by 2030, growing at annual CAGR around 29-30% [26] Several converging factors are accelerating the adoption of predictive maintenance across industries like technological advancements (IoT & AI), costly Unplanned downtime (estimated at ∼ $50 billion per year across industries) and can erode 5-20% of productivity capacity [26], shift from Reactive to Proactive culture, data-driven asset management and falling technology costs [27]. This study examines industry-specific case studies that illustrate the implementation of PdM across small, medium, and largescale industries. The findings indicate that small-scale industries utilize IoT-enabled PdM with a high degree of predictive accuracy, although they face challenges such as substantial initial investments and a shortage of skilled personnel for PdM implementation. Medium-sized industries employ decision support systems (DSS) with open-source software for data management due to their costeffectiveness, flexibility, and reliability, despite potential difficulties in integrating DSS with legacy systems. Large industries, such as those in steel production, deploy AI-PdM programs on a larger scale to enhance efficiency and minimize waste; however, the complexity and extensive data analysis required can be costly. The comparison suggests that the scale of an industry influences the appropriateness of each PdM strategy as a singular solution. Larger industries adopt advanced AI-PdM models due to the inefficiency of estimating PdM costs given the complexity of data-driven problem-solving with pre-existing data. This study underscores the importance of prioritizing stage exercises by scale within industries, particularly when space is constrained. Further investment is required in data and infrastructure to enhance workforce capabilities through training.
